```
1	"""
2	Apibara live test — SOLD (ended) IAAI lots, with the filters IAAI supports.
3	
4	Run (from anywhere; paths resolve off this file's location):
5	    python test/test_apibara_sold_iaai_01.py
6	
7	Budget: 1 call per page, MAX_PAGES pages (default 1) = 1 call of your 100/mo.
8	
9	FILTER GRANULARITY ON IAAI
10	--------------------------
11	i)   DATE RANGE   server-side. auction_date_from / auction_date_to, YYYY-MM-DD.
12	ii)  BODY STYLE   client-side only, but RELIABLE here: vehicle_specs.body_style
13	                  is populated on 100% of IAAI records observed
14	                  (Sedan / Coupe / Sedan-Hatchback). No server-side param exists.
15	iii) DAMAGE       server-side `damage` is an INCLUDE-only whitelist and its enum
16	                  (Fire/Hail/Theft/Water/Chemical/Rollover/Mechanical/Vandalized/
17	                  Repossession) cannot express collision damage, which is most
18	                  lots. There is no exclude param, so exclusion is client-side
19	                  against condition.primary_damage.
20	
21	IAAI damage vocabulary is POSITIONAL (Left front, Right rear, Left rear,
22	Right side, Front & rear, ...) — finer than Copart's. Exclusion needles below
23	are written for that vocabulary.
24	
25	IAAI-only bonus fields (absent on Copart): ActualCashValue (27/27 observed),
26	EstimatedRepairCost (17/27), body_style, Seller / SellerType.
27	
28	Reads APIBARA_API_KEY from the repo-root .env; saves raw JSON to
29	test_run/apibara_sold_iaai_01.json.
30	"""
31	import json
32	import os
33	import time
34	import urllib.error
35	import urllib.parse
36	import urllib.request
37	from pathlib import Path
38	
39	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent   # repo root
40	ENV_PATH = ROOT / ".env"
41	OUT_DIR = ROOT / "test_run"
42	
43	BASE = "https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction"
44	RATE_DELAY = 1.5
45	MAX_PAGES = 1                      # each page = 1 API call, 20 lots
46	
47	# --- server-side filters (sent to the API) ---------------------------------
48	PARAMS = {
49	    "platform": "iaai",
50	    "make": "Audi",
51	    "model": "S5",
52	    "year_from": 2018,
53	    "year_to": 2023,
54	    "lot_sub_status": "Ended",     # sold / finished lots
55	    "auction_date_from": "2026-04-20",   # (i) YYYY-MM-DD
56	    "auction_date_to": "2026-05-11",
57	    "per_page": 20,
58	}
59	
60	# --- client-side filters (applied to the response) -------------------------
61	# (ii) keep only these body styles; empty list = keep all
62	BODY_STYLES = ["Coupe"]            # e.g. ["Coupe"] / ["Sedan", "Sedan/Hatchback"]
63	
64	# (iii) drop lots whose primary/secondary damage matches any needle
65	EXCLUDE_DAMAGE = ["water", "flood", "burn", "fire", "rollover", "storm"]
66	
67	
68	def read_env_key(path=ENV_PATH, name="APIBARA_API_KEY"):
69	    if not os.path.exists(path):
70	        return ""
71	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
72	        for line in f:
73	            line = line.strip()
74	            if line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
75	                continue
76	            k, _, v = line.partition("=")
77	            if k.strip() == name:
78	                return v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
79	    return ""
80	
81	
82	def money(v):
83	    return f"${v:,.0f}" if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and v else "—"
84	
85	
86	def get(api_key, path, params):
87	    url = f"{BASE}{path}?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True)
88	    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={
89	        "Accept": "application/json", "X-API-Key": api_key})
90	    try:
91	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
92	            return resp.getcode(), json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
93	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
94	        return e.code, {"error_body": e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]}
95	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
96	        return 0, {"error": str(e)}
97	
98	
99	def body_style(v):
100	    return (v.get("vehicle_specs") or {}).get("body_style") or ""
101	
102	
103	def damage_text(v):
104	    c = v.get("condition") or {}
105	    return f"{c.get('primary_damage') or ''} {c.get('secondary_damage') or ''}".lower()
106	
107	
108	def keep(v):
109	    """Client-side (ii) + (iii). Returns (bool, reason)."""
110	    if BODY_STYLES and body_style(v) not in BODY_STYLES:
111	        return False, f"body_style={body_style(v) or 'null'}"
112	    hit = next((n for n in EXCLUDE_DAMAGE if n in damage_text(v)), None)
113	    if hit:
114	        return False, f"damage~{hit}"
115	    return True, ""
116	
117	
118	def show(v, i):
119	    p = v.get("pricing") or {}
120	    a = v.get("auction") or {}
121	    c = v.get("condition") or {}
122	    si = ((v.get("details") or {}).get("sale_information")) or {}
123	    rc = c.get("run_condition")
124	    run = (rc.get("value") if isinstance(rc, dict) else rc) or "—"
125	
126	    print(f"  [{i}] {v.get('year','?')} {v.get('make','')} {v.get('model','')}"
127	          f"  lot {v.get('lot_number','?')}  [{body_style(v) or 'body n/a'}]")
128	    print(f"      SOLD {money(p.get('last_sold_price_usd'))} on {a.get('last_sold_day') or '—'}"
129	          f"   status={a.get('last_sold_status') or '—'}"
130	          f"   last bid={money(p.get('current_bid_usd'))}"
131	          f"   buy_now={money(p.get('buy_now_usd'))}")
132	    print(f"      Damage:  {c.get('primary_damage') or '—'}"
133	          f"  / 2nd: {c.get('secondary_damage') or '—'}   runs: {run}")
134	    print(f"      ACV:     {si.get('ActualCashValue') or '—'}"
135	          f"   est. repair: {si.get('EstimatedRepairCost') or '—'}")
136	    print(f"      Seller:  {si.get('Seller') or '—'} ({si.get('SellerType') or '—'})"
137	          f"   title: {(v.get('sale_document') or {}).get('name') or '—'}")
138	
139	
140	def main():
141	    api_key = read_env_key()
142	    if not api_key:
143	        raise SystemExit(f"No APIBARA_API_KEY found in {ENV_PATH}")
144	
145	    out = {"platform": "iaai", "params": PARAMS,
146	           "body_styles": BODY_STYLES, "exclude_damage": EXCLUDE_DAMAGE,
147	           "pages": []}
148	    calls, cursor, kept, dropped = 0, None, [], []
149	
150	    print("=" * 78)
151	    print("IAAI — sold/ended lots")
152	    print(f"  server-side: {PARAMS}")
153	    print(f"  client-side: body_styles={BODY_STYLES or 'ALL'}  "
154	          f"exclude_damage={EXCLUDE_DAMAGE}")
155	    print("=" * 78)
156	
157	    while calls < MAX_PAGES:
158	        params = dict(PARAMS)
159	        if cursor:
160	            params["cursor"] = cursor
161	        code, data = get(api_key, "/vehicles", params)
162	        calls += 1
163	        out["pages"].append({"status": code, "raw": data})
164	        if code != 200:
165	            print(f"\n  HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:400]}")
166	            break
167	        rows = data.get("data") or []
168	        for v in rows:
169	            ok, why = keep(v)
170	            (kept if ok else dropped).append((v, why))
171	        cursor = (data.get("meta") or {}).get("next_cursor")
172	        print(f"\n  page {calls}: {len(rows)} lot(s) returned"
173	              f"   (more pages: {bool(cursor)})")
174	        if not cursor:
175	            break
176	        time.sleep(RATE_DELAY)
177	
178	    print(f"\n  KEPT {len(kept)}   dropped {len(dropped)} by client-side filters\n")
179	    for i, (v, _) in enumerate(kept, 1):
180	        show(v, i)
181	    if dropped:
182	        print("\n  --- dropped ---")
183	        for v, why in dropped:
184	            print(f"      lot {v.get('lot_number','?'):>10s} {v.get('year')} "
185	                  f"{v.get('model','')}  ({why})")
186	
187	    OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
188	    out_path = OUT_DIR / "apibara_sold_iaai_01.json"
189	    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
190	        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
191	    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
192	    print(f"Done. {calls} API call(s) used. Raw JSON -> {out_path}")
193	
194	
195	if __name__ == "__main__":
```

*Result*
```
1	"""
2	Apibara live test — CONTROL TEST for server-side proximity filtering.
3	
4	Run (from anywhere; paths resolve off this file's location):
5	    python test/test_apibara_sold_iaai_02.py
6	
7	Budget: 1 call of your 100/mo.
8	
9	WHAT THIS TESTS
10	---------------
11	Identical to test_apibara_sold_iaai_01.py except for three added server-side
12	params:  zip=98003  radius=3000  units=mi
13	
14	3000 miles covers the entire lower 48 from Federal Way, WA — so the CORRECT
15	answer is the same ~15 lots that _01 returned. Any shortfall is the finding.
16	
17	The question being settled: `zip`+`radius` filtering is computed on Apibara's
18	side against its own `facility` table (proven — `facility.id` equals IAAI's
19	`StorageLocationBranch`, coords match to the decimal, `facility.zip` exists
20	where IAAI provides none, and Copart records carry `facility` despite having
21	no `details` block at all). But `facility.lat` is populated on only **3 of 75**
22	observed records. If the radius filter joins against that same sparse data, it
23	will silently drop lots that genuinely are in range.
24	
25	  same ~15 lots, `distance` populated  -> index is complete, the response field
26	                                          is just lazily serialised; server-side
27	                                          filtering is safe to rely on.
28	  only 1-3 lots                        -> the join really is sparse; `zip`+
29	                                          `radius` is unusable and client-side
30	                                          math on details.attributes.StorageLocation*
31	                                          (IAAI-only) plus /locations for Copart
32	                                          is the only option.
33	
34	Also reports whether the top-level `distance` field populates once a zip is
35	supplied — it was null on all 75 records pulled so far, because no search had
36	ever passed one.
37	
38	Reads APIBARA_API_KEY from the repo-root .env; saves raw JSON to
39	test_run/apibara_sold_iaai_02.json and diffs against
40	test_run/apibara_sold_iaai_01.json when that file exists.
41	"""
42	import json
43	import math
44	import os
45	import urllib.error
46	import urllib.parse
47	import urllib.request
48	from pathlib import Path
49	
50	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent   # repo root
51	ENV_PATH = ROOT / ".env"
52	OUT_DIR = ROOT / "test_run"
53	BASELINE = OUT_DIR / "apibara_sold_iaai_01.json"
54	
55	BASE = "https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction"
56	
57	# Federal Way, WA 98003 — transport destination
58	DEST_ZIP = "98003"
59	DEST_LAT, DEST_LNG = 47.3223, -122.3126
60	ROAD_FACTOR = 1.2          # great-circle -> rough road miles (US long-haul)
61	
62	# --- server-side filters: _01's PARAMS + the three proximity params ---------
63	PARAMS = {
64	    "platform": "iaai",
65	    "make": "Audi",
66	    "model": "S5",
67	    "year_from": 2018,
68	    "year_to": 2023,
69	    "lot_sub_status": "Ended",
70	    "auction_date_from": "2026-04-20",
71	    "auction_date_to": "2026-05-11",
72	    "per_page": 20,
73	    # --- the three under test ---
74	    "zip": DEST_ZIP,
75	    "radius": 3000,
76	    "units": "mi",
77	}
78	
79	
80	def read_env_key(path=ENV_PATH, name="APIBARA_API_KEY"):
81	    if not os.path.exists(path):
82	        return ""
83	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
84	        for line in f:
85	            line = line.strip()
86	            if line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
87	                continue
88	            k, _, v = line.partition("=")
89	            if k.strip() == name:
90	                return v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
91	    return ""
92	
93	
94	def get(api_key, path, params):
95	    url = f"{BASE}{path}?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True)
96	    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={
97	        "Accept": "application/json", "X-API-Key": api_key})
98	    try:
99	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
100	            return resp.getcode(), json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
101	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
102	        return e.code, {"error_body": e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]}
103	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
104	        return 0, {"error": str(e)}
105	
106	
107	def haversine_mi(lat, lng):
108	    R = 3958.8
109	    p1, l1, p2, l2 = map(math.radians, (DEST_LAT, DEST_LNG, lat, lng))
110	    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(
111	        math.sin((p2 - p1) / 2) ** 2
112	        + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin((l2 - l1) / 2) ** 2))
113	
114	
115	def coords(v):
116	    """(lat, lng, source) from whichever layer has them."""
117	    at = (v.get("details") or {}).get("attributes") or {}
118	    la, lo = at.get("StorageLocationLatitude"), at.get("StorageLocationLongitude")
119	    if la and lo:
120	        return float(la), float(lo), "details.attributes"
121	    f = v.get("facility") or {}
122	    if f.get("lat") is not None and f.get("lng") is not None:
123	        return float(f["lat"]), float(f["lng"]), "facility"
124	    return None, None, "none"
125	
126	
127	def baseline_lots():
128	    if not BASELINE.exists():
129	        return None
130	    d = json.loads(BASELINE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
131	    return {v.get("lot_number") for p in d.get("pages", [])
132	            if p.get("status") == 200
133	            for v in (p.get("raw", {}).get("data") or [])}
134	
135	
136	def main():
137	    api_key = read_env_key()
138	    if not api_key:
139	        raise SystemExit(f"No APIBARA_API_KEY found in {ENV_PATH}")
140	
141	    print("=" * 78)
142	    print(f"CONTROL TEST — server-side proximity filter (zip={DEST_ZIP}, "
143	          f"radius=3000 mi)")
144	    print(f"  {PARAMS}")
145	    print("=" * 78)
146	
147	    code, data = get(api_key, "/vehicles", PARAMS)
148	    out = {"params": PARAMS, "dest_zip": DEST_ZIP, "status": code, "raw": data}
149	
150	    if code != 200:
151	        print(f"\n  HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:400]}")
152	        if code == 422:
153	            print("  -> 422 means one of zip/radius/units was rejected.")
154	        _save(out)
155	        return
156	
157	    rows = data.get("data") or []
158	    cursor = (data.get("meta") or {}).get("next_cursor")
159	    dist_set = sum(1 for v in rows if v.get("distance") is not None)
160	    fac_set = sum(1 for v in rows if (v.get("facility") or {}).get("lat") is not None)
161	
162	    print(f"\n  returned {len(rows)} lot(s)   (more pages: {bool(cursor)})")
163	    print(f"  top-level `distance` populated: {dist_set}/{len(rows)}")
164	    print(f"  `facility.lat` populated:       {fac_set}/{len(rows)}\n")
165	
166	    print(f"  {'lot':>10s} {'branch':>7s} {'API dist':>9s} {'haversine':>10s} "
167	          f"{'~road':>7s}  source            location")
168	    for v in sorted(rows, key=lambda x: haversine_mi(*coords(x)[:2])
169	                    if coords(x)[0] is not None else 9e9):
170	        at = (v.get("details") or {}).get("attributes") or {}
171	        la, lo, src = coords(v)
172	        hav = f"{haversine_mi(la, lo):8.0f}" if la is not None else "       —"
173	        road = f"{haversine_mi(la, lo) * ROAD_FACTOR:6.0f}" if la is not None else "     —"
174	        api_d = v.get("distance")
175	        print(f"  {str(v.get('lot_number')):>10s} "
176	              f"{str(at.get('StorageLocationBranch') or (v.get('facility') or {}).get('id') or '—'):>7s} "
177	              f"{str(api_d if api_d is not None else '—'):>9s} {hav} mi {road} mi  "
178	              f"{src:17s} {(v.get('location') or {}).get('display') or '—'}")
179	
180	    base = baseline_lots()
181	    print()
182	    if base is None:
183	        print(f"  (no baseline at {BASELINE} — run test_apibara_sold_iaai_01.py "
184	              f"to enable the diff)")
185	    else:
186	        got = {v.get("lot_number") for v in rows}
187	        missing, extra = base - got, got - base
188	        print(f"  BASELINE (_01, no proximity params): {len(base)} lot(s)")
189	        print(f"  THIS RUN (radius=3000 mi):           {len(got)} lot(s)")
190	        if missing:
191	            print(f"  DROPPED by the filter ({len(missing)}): {sorted(missing)}")
192	        if extra:
193	            print(f"  NEW vs baseline ({len(extra)}): {sorted(extra)}")
194	        out["baseline_count"] = len(base)
195	        out["dropped"] = sorted(missing)
196	        out["extra"] = sorted(extra)
197	
198	        print("\n  VERDICT:")
199	        if not missing:
200	            print("    No lots dropped -> Apibara's geo index is complete; the sparse")
201	            print("    `facility` block in responses is only lazy serialisation.")
202	            print("    Server-side zip+radius filtering is SAFE to rely on.")
203	        elif len(got) <= 3:
204	            print("    Nearly everything dropped -> the radius filter joins against the")
205	            print("    same sparse facility data seen in responses. zip+radius is")
206	            print("    UNUSABLE; use client-side math on StorageLocation* (IAAI only)")
207	            print("    plus /locations for Copart.")
208	        else:
209	            print(f"    Partial loss ({len(missing)} of {len(base)}) -> the join is")
210	            print("    incomplete. Server-side filtering silently hides lots; treat any")
211	            print("    proximity-filtered result as a floor, not a complete set.")
212	
213	    _save(out)
214	
215	
216	def _save(out):
217	    OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
218	    out_path = OUT_DIR / "apibara_sold_iaai_02.json"
219	    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
220	        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
221	    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
222	    print(f"Done. 1 API call used. Raw JSON -> {out_path}")
223	
224	
225	if __name__ == "__main__":
226	    main()
227	
```

```
Apibara.tech adapter — PRIMARY discovery source (real Copart + IAAI).

Docs: https://apibara.tech/llms-full.txt
Base:  https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction
Auth:  X-API-Key header
Search: GET /vehicles   (cursor pagination, per_page max 20)
Lookup: GET /vehicles/{vin-or-lot}

Unlike MarketCheck, Apibara returns the fields that matter for salvage:
current bid, primary/secondary damage, title/sale-document, odometer,
run condition, seller type, sale date, location, photos.

Env:
  APIBARA_API_KEY     required for live discovery/lookup
  APIBARA_BASE_URL    default https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction
  APIBARA_MAX_PAGES   default 1 (20 lots/page; keep low on the free plan)
  APIBARA_MOCK=1      testing only: canned response, no HTTP

import os

import httpx

API_KEY = os.getenv("APIBARA_API_KEY", "")
BASE = os.getenv("APIBARA_BASE_URL", "https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction").rstrip("/")
MAX_PAGES = int(os.getenv("APIBARA_MAX_PAGES", "1"))

# Copart/IAAI primary_damage -> our damage_type codes
_DAMAGE_MAP = [
    (("water", "flood"), "flood"),
    (("burn", "fire"), "fire"),
    (("theft", "stripped", "stolen", "missing"), "theft_recovery"),
    (("hail",), "hail"),
    (("frame", "undercarriage", "rollover", "roll over"), "frame"),
    (("minor dent", "scratch", "normal wear", "vandalism", "cosmetic"), "minor_collision"),
    (("front", "rear", "side", "all over", "top", "roof"), "moderate_collision"),
]


def is_configured() -> bool:
    return bool(API_KEY) or MOCK


def _headers() -> dict:
    return {"Accept": "application/json", "X-API-Key": API_KEY}


def _map_damage(primary: str, secondary: str = "") -> str:
    text = f"{primary} {secondary}".lower()
    for needles, code in _DAMAGE_MAP:
        if any(n in text for n in needles):
            return code
    return "other"


def _map_title(rec: dict) -> str:
    sd = rec.get("sale_document") or {}
    name = str(sd.get("name") or "").lower()
    if "clean" in name or "clear" in name:
        return "clean"
    # salvage/rebuilt/flood/junk/parts/non-repairable all use the salvage fee table
    return "salvage"


def _map_damage_full(rec: dict) -> str:
    """Damage code, preferring the sale-document group (catches flood/fire even
    when primary_damage is a collision code)."""
    cond = rec.get("condition") or {}
    sd = rec.get("sale_document") or {}
    group = str(sd.get("sale_document_group") or "").lower()
    if "water" in group or "flood" in group:
        return "flood"
    if "fire" in group or "burn" in group:
        return "fire"
    return _map_damage(cond.get("primary_damage") or "", cond.get("secondary_damage") or "")
```

```
"""
Apibara pull for the analytics pipeline — parameterised successor to
test/test_apibara_sold_iaai_01.py and test/test_apibara_sold_copart_01.py.

Run (from anywhere; paths resolve off this file's location):

    python analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py iaai sold \
        --make Audi --model S5 \
        --year-range 2018-2023 \
        --auction-date-range 2026-04-20 2026-05-11 \
        --seller insurance \
        --body-style -coupe \
        --engine-type V6

BUDGET: 1 API call per page, `--max-pages` pages (default 1) of your 100/month.
Use `--dry-run` to print the exact request URL and the resolved filters without
spending a call. Nothing else in this script hits the network.

OUTPUT (both written, same basename, into analytics/sold-data/):
    <basename>.json   raw pages + resolved filters + flattened rows
    <basename>.csv    flattened rows only — the analytics input

WHAT IS SERVER-SIDE vs CLIENT-SIDE
----------------------------------
server-side : platform, make, model, year_from/to, lot_sub_status,
              auction_date_from/to, per_page, cursor
client-side : body style, engine type, seller class, damage exclusion
              (Apibara has no param for any of them; `damage` exists but is an
              INCLUDE-only whitelist whose enum cannot express collision damage)

SELLER CLASSIFICATION  (`--seller insurance|dealer|any`)
-------------------------------------------------------
There is no single trustworthy field, so `seller_class()` cascades, and the
field that decided each lot is recorded in the `seller_class_source` column so
the classification stays auditable:

  1. seller.type == "insurance"                 -> insurance   (both platforms)
     seller.type == "non_insurance"             -> dealer      (Copart only)
  2. details.sale_information.SellerType         -> IAAI-only mirror of the above
  3. name keywords on seller.name / .Seller      -> insurance if it looks like a
     carrier, else dealer

Measured on the current test_run/ pulls:
  Copart 20/20 typed cleanly (11 insurance / 8 non_insurance / 1 unknown).
  IAAI   10/15 typed "insurance"; the other 5 come back seller.type="unknown"
         with SellerType absent — and their names ("Turo Inc", "Alamo Financial
         Group") are exactly the third-party/fleet sellers the dealer bucket is
         meant to catch. IAAI never emits "non_insurance", so on IAAI *dealer is
         inferred, not stated*: it means "named seller that is not a carrier".
         `--seller insurance` is the precise half of the filter; treat
         `--seller dealer` on IAAI as a lead list, not a fact.

ENGINE TYPE  (`--engine-type V4|V6|other`, repeatable)
-----------------------------------------------------
Matching is by CYLINDER COUNT, not literal layout — a transverse "V4" is
essentially a marketing fiction, real 4-cylinders are inline, so V4 == any
4-cylinder. V6/V8 likewise mean 6/8 cylinders. `other` = anything else,
including engines that could not be parsed (electric, unparseable strings).
Source is vehicle_specs.engine: IAAI is rich ("3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo,
354HP", layout "V"), Copart is bare ("3.0L 6", layout null) — hence the
count-first approach; layout-based matching would drop every Copart lot.

BODY STYLE  (`--body-style [-]<style>`, repeatable, IAAI ONLY)
-------------------------------------------------------------
Prefix with "-" to exclude, no prefix to include (mixing both = include-list
wins, then exclusions apply). vehicle_specs.body_style is populated on 100% of
IAAI records (Sedan / Sedan/Hatchback / Coupe / Convertible) and null on 100%
of Copart records. Passing --body-style with `copart` is refused rather than
silently returning nothing.

DAMAGE
------
Default exclusion needles differ per platform because the vocabularies do:
IAAI is positional (Left front / Right rear / Front & rear), Copart is coarse
(Front end / Rear end / Side / All over). Override with --exclude-damage or
switch off with --no-damage-filter.

Reads APIBARA_API_KEY from the repo-root .env.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]          # repo root
ENV_PATH = ROOT / ".env"
OUT_DIR = ROOT / "analytics" / "sold-data"

BASE = "https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction"
RATE_DELAY = 1.5                                    # free plan = 1 req/sec

# platform -> default damage needles (matched against primary + secondary)
DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_DAMAGE = {
    "iaai": ["water", "flood", "burn", "fire", "rollover", "storm"],
    "copart": ["water", "flood", "burn", "fire", "rollover", "all over",
               "mechanical"],
}

# name fragments that identify an insurance carrier when seller.type is useless
_INSURER_NEEDLES = [
    "insurance", "insur", "casualty", "assurance", "indemnity", "underwrit",
    "mutual", "geico", "usaa", "state farm", "progressive", "allstate",
    "farmers", "nationwide", "esurance", "safeco", "travelers", "hartford",
    "amica", "erie", "aaa ", "auto club", "root ", "lemonade",
]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# env + transport
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def read_env_key(path=ENV_PATH, name="APIBARA_API_KEY"):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return ""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
                continue
            k, _, v = line.partition("=")
            if k.strip() == name:
                return v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return ""


def build_url(path, params):
    return f"{BASE}{path}?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True)


def get(api_key, path, params):
    req = urllib.request.Request(build_url(path, params), headers={
        "Accept": "application/json", "X-API-Key": api_key})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            return resp.getcode(), json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, {"error_body": e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return 0, {"error": str(e)}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# field accessors — every one of these tolerates a missing/None parent block
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sale_info(v):
    """IAAI-only details.sale_information (Copart has details=None)."""
    return ((v.get("details") or {}).get("sale_information")) or {}


def body_style(v):
    return (v.get("vehicle_specs") or {}).get("body_style") or ""


def damage_text(v):
    c = v.get("condition") or {}
    return f"{c.get('primary_damage') or ''} {c.get('secondary_damage') or ''}".lower()


def run_condition(v):
    rc = (v.get("condition") or {}).get("run_condition")
    return (rc.get("value") if isinstance(rc, dict) else rc) or ""


def lot_url(v):
    lot = v.get("lot_number") or ""
    if not lot:
        return ""
    if "iaa" in (v.get("platform") or "").lower():
        return f"https://www.iaai.com/VehicleDetail/{lot}"
    return f"https://www.copart.com/lot/{lot}"


def norm_style(s):
    """'Sedan-Hatchback' / 'sedan hatchback' -> 'sedan/hatchback'."""
    s = (s or "").strip().lower()
    return re.sub(r"[\s_-]+", "/", s)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derived classifications
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def seller_class(v):
    """-> (class, source). class in {insurance, dealer, unknown}."""
    stype = ((v.get("seller") or {}).get("type") or "").strip().lower()
    if stype == "insurance":
        return "insurance", "seller.type"
    if stype in ("non_insurance", "non-insurance", "dealer"):
        return "dealer", "seller.type"

    itype = str(sale_info(v).get("SellerType") or "").strip().lower()
    if itype:
        if "insur" in itype:
            return "insurance", "sale_information.SellerType"
        return "dealer", "sale_information.SellerType"

    name = str((v.get("seller") or {}).get("name")
               or sale_info(v).get("Seller") or "").strip().lower()
    if not name or name == "unknown":
        return "unknown", "none"
    if any(n in name for n in _INSURER_NEEDLES):
        return "insurance", "seller.name"
    return "dealer", "seller.name~inferred"


_ENGINE_LAYOUT_CYL = re.compile(r"\b([VILWHB])[\s-]?(\d{1,2})\b", re.I)
_ENGINE_CYL_ONLY = re.compile(r"\d(?:\.\d)?\s*L\s*[\s-]*(\d{1,2})\b", re.I)
_ENGINE_CYL_WORD = re.compile(r"\b(\d{1,2})\s*[- ]?CYL", re.I)


def engine_info(v):
    """-> (cylinders|None, layout|'', raw). Count-first; see module docstring."""
    eng = (v.get("vehicle_specs") or {}).get("engine") or {}
    raw = str(eng.get("raw") or "")
    layout = str(eng.get("layout") or "")

    m = _ENGINE_LAYOUT_CYL.search(raw)
    if m:
        return int(m.group(2)), (layout or m.group(1).upper()), raw
    for rx in (_ENGINE_CYL_ONLY, _ENGINE_CYL_WORD):
        m = rx.search(raw)
        if m:
            return int(m.group(1)), layout, raw
    return None, layout, raw


def engine_class(v):
    """-> 'V4' / 'V6' / 'V8' / 'other'. Cylinder count drives it."""
    cyl, _, _ = engine_info(v)
    if cyl in (4, 6, 8):
        return f"V{cyl}"
    return "other"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# client-side filtering
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def keep(v, f):
    """Apply resolved client-side filters `f`. -> (bool, reason)."""
    if f["include_styles"] or f["exclude_styles"]:
        bs = norm_style(body_style(v))
        if f["include_styles"] and bs not in f["include_styles"]:
            return False, f"body_style={bs or 'null'}"
        if bs in f["exclude_styles"]:
            return False, f"body_style={bs} (excluded)"

    if f["engine_types"] and engine_class(v) not in f["engine_types"]:
        return False, f"engine={engine_class(v)}"

    if f["seller"] != "any":
        cls, _ = seller_class(v)
        if cls != f["seller"]:
            return False, f"seller={cls}"

    hit = next((n for n in f["exclude_damage"] if n in damage_text(v)), None)
    if hit:
        return False, f"damage~{hit}"

    if f["live_only"] and (v.get("auction") or {}).get("state") == "finished":
        return False, "auction=finished"

    return True, ""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# flattening — this is the analytics contract; CSV columns are these keys
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def flatten(v):
    p = v.get("pricing") or {}
    a = v.get("auction") or {}
    c = v.get("condition") or {}
    sd = v.get("sale_document") or {}
    loc = v.get("location") or {}
    specs = v.get("vehicle_specs") or {}
    si = sale_info(v)
    cyl, layout, eng_raw = engine_info(v)
    cls, src = seller_class(v)

    return {
        "platform": v.get("platform"),
        "lot_number": v.get("lot_number"),
        "vin": v.get("vin"),
        "year": v.get("year"),
        "make": v.get("make"),
        "model": v.get("model"),
        "title": v.get("title"),
        "body_style": body_style(v) or None,
        "engine_raw": eng_raw or None,
        "engine_cylinders": cyl,
        "engine_layout": layout or None,
        "engine_class": engine_class(v),
        "engine_hp": (specs.get("engine") or {}).get("hp"),
        "drive_type": specs.get("drive_type"),
        "transmission": specs.get("transmission"),
        "exterior_color": specs.get("exterior_color"),
        "odometer_mi": (v.get("odometer") or {}).get("mi"),
        "primary_damage": c.get("primary_damage"),
        "secondary_damage": c.get("secondary_damage"),
        "run_condition": run_condition(v) or None,
        "has_key": c.get("has_key"),
        "loss": c.get("loss"),
        "sale_document": sd.get("name"),
        "sale_document_group": sd.get("sale_document_group"),
        "seller_name": (v.get("seller") or {}).get("name") or si.get("Seller"),
        "seller_type_raw": (v.get("seller") or {}).get("type"),
        "seller_type_iaai": si.get("SellerType"),
        "seller_class": cls,
        "seller_class_source": src,
        # IAAI-only economics — null on every Copart lot
        "acv_usd": si.get("ActualCashValue"),
        "est_repair_usd": si.get("EstimatedRepairCost"),
        "current_bid_usd": p.get("current_bid_usd"),
        "buy_now_usd": p.get("buy_now_usd"),
        "last_sold_price_usd": p.get("last_sold_price_usd"),
        "last_sold_day": a.get("last_sold_day"),
        "last_sold_status": a.get("last_sold_status"),
        "auction_state": a.get("state"),
        "auction_at": a.get("auction_at") or v.get("ad"),
        "location_display": loc.get("display"),
        "selling_branch": si.get("SellingBranch"),
        "distance_api": v.get("distance"),
        "thumbs_count": (v.get("media") or {}).get("thumbs_count"),
        "url": lot_url(v),
    }


CSV_COLUMNS = list(flatten({}).keys())


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def parse_year_range(s):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d{4})\s*(?:[-:]\s*(\d{4}))?\s*", s or "")
    if not m:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"--year-range wants YYYY-YYYY or YYYY, got {s!r}")
    lo = int(m.group(1))
    hi = int(m.group(2) or m.group(1))
    if hi < lo:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"--year-range {lo}-{hi} is backwards")
    return lo, hi


def parse_date(s):
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(s.strip())
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"dates must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {s!r}") from None


def build_arg_parser():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="pull_apibara_01.py",
        description="Pull Apibara auction lots into analytics/sold-data/.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="Each page costs 1 call of the 100/month free plan. "
               "Use --dry-run to see the request without spending one.")
    ap.add_argument("platform", choices=["iaai", "copart"],
                    type=str.lower, help="auction platform")
    ap.add_argument("mode", choices=["live", "sold"], type=str.lower,
                    help="sold = lot_sub_status=Ended; live = open lots")
    ap.add_argument("--make")
    ap.add_argument("--model")
    ap.add_argument("--year-range", type=parse_year_range, metavar="YYYY-YYYY")
    ap.add_argument("--auction-date-range", nargs="+", type=parse_date,
                    metavar="YYYY-MM-DD",
                    help="one date = today..that date; two = from..to")
    ap.add_argument("--seller", choices=["insurance", "dealer", "any"],
                    type=str.lower, default="any",
                    help="client-side; see module docstring for how it is decided")
    ap.add_argument("--body-style", action="append", default=[], metavar="[-]STYLE",
                    help="IAAI only, repeatable. '-coupe' excludes, 'coupe' includes")
    ap.add_argument("--engine-type", action="append", default=[],
                    metavar="{V4|V6|V8|other}",
                    help="repeatable; matched on cylinder count")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-damage", metavar="a,b,c",
                    help="override the per-platform default needle list")
    ap.add_argument("--no-damage-filter", action="store_true",
                    help="keep every damage type")
    ap.add_argument("--max-pages", type=int, default=1,
                    help="pages to pull; EACH PAGE IS ONE API CALL (default 1)")
    ap.add_argument("--per-page", type=int, default=20,
                    help="lots per page, API max 20 (default 20)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="output basename or path (default: auto-named)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-raw", action="store_true",
                    help="omit the raw API pages from the JSON (smaller file)")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                    help="print the resolved request + filters, make no call")
    return ap


def resolve_filters(args):
    """CLI args -> the two dicts everything downstream reads."""
    params = {"platform": args.platform, "per_page": min(args.per_page, 20)}
    if args.make:
        params["make"] = args.make
    if args.model:
        params["model"] = args.model
    if args.year_range:
        params["year_from"], params["year_to"] = args.year_range
    if args.mode == "sold":
        params["lot_sub_status"] = "Ended"
    else:
        # No documented "Live" enum value; ask for everything and drop finished
        # lots client-side (see filters["live_only"]).
        params["lot_status"] = "All"
    if args.auction_date_range:
        d = args.auction_date_range
        if len(d) == 1:
            lo, hi = dt.date.today(), d[0]
        elif len(d) == 2:
            lo, hi = sorted(d)
        else:
            raise SystemExit("--auction-date-range takes one or two dates")
        params["auction_date_from"] = lo.isoformat()
        params["auction_date_to"] = hi.isoformat()

    include, exclude = set(), set()
    for raw in args.body_style:
        for tok in str(raw).split(","):
            tok = tok.strip()
            if not tok:
                continue
            if tok.startswith("-"):
                exclude.add(norm_style(tok[1:]))
            else:
                include.add(norm_style(tok.lstrip("+")))

    engines = set()
    for raw in args.engine_type:
        for tok in str(raw).split(","):
            tok = tok.strip().upper()
            if not tok:
                continue
            if tok not in ("V4", "V6", "V8", "OTHER"):
                raise SystemExit(
                    f"--engine-type must be V4/V6/V8/other, got {tok!r}")
            engines.add("other" if tok == "OTHER" else tok)

    if args.no_damage_filter:
        damage = []
    elif args.exclude_damage is not None:
        damage = [n.strip().lower() for n in args.exclude_damage.split(",")
                  if n.strip()]
    else:
        damage = list(DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_DAMAGE[args.platform])

    filters = {
        "include_styles": include,
        "exclude_styles": exclude,
        "engine_types": engines,
        "seller": args.seller,
        "exclude_damage": damage,
        "live_only": args.mode == "live",
    }
    return params, filters


def filters_json(f):
    return {k: (sorted(v) if isinstance(v, set) else v) for k, v in f.items()}


def default_basename(args, params):
    bits = ["apibara", args.platform, args.mode]
    bits += [str(x).lower().replace(" ", "-")
             for x in (args.make, args.model) if x]
    if args.year_range:
        bits.append(f"{args.year_range[0]}-{args.year_range[1]}")
    if "auction_date_from" in params:
        bits.append(f"{params['auction_date_from']}_{params['auction_date_to']}")
    bits.append(dt.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S"))
    return "_".join(bits)


def resolve_out_path(args, params):
    if args.out:
        p = Path(args.out)
        if not p.is_absolute():
            p = OUT_DIR / p
        return p.with_suffix("")
    return OUT_DIR / default_basename(args, params)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# reporting
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def money(v):
    return f"${v:,.0f}" if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and v else "—"


def show(r, i):
    print(f"  [{i}] {r['year']} {r['make']} {r['model']}  lot {r['lot_number']}"
          f"  [{r['body_style'] or 'body n/a'}]  {r['engine_class']}")
    print(f"      SOLD {money(r['last_sold_price_usd'])} on {r['last_sold_day'] or '—'}"
          f"   status={r['last_sold_status'] or '—'}"
          f"   last bid={money(r['current_bid_usd'])}"
          f"   buy_now={money(r['buy_now_usd'])}")
    print(f"      Damage:  {r['primary_damage'] or '—'}"
          f"  / 2nd: {r['secondary_damage'] or '—'}"
          f"   runs: {r['run_condition'] or '—'}"
          f"   odo: {r['odometer_mi'] or '—'} mi")
    print(f"      ACV:     {r['acv_usd'] or '—'}"
          f"   est. repair: {r['est_repair_usd'] or '—'}"
          f"   title: {r['sale_document'] or '—'}")
    print(f"      Seller:  {r['seller_name'] or '—'}"
          f"  -> {r['seller_class']} (via {r['seller_class_source']})"
          f"   loc: {r['location_display'] or '—'}")


def seller_audit(rows):
    """Every distinct (name, type, SellerType) -> class, so the inference is
    checkable by eye. This is the field the spec flagged as unverified."""
    seen = {}
    for r in rows:
        key = (r["seller_name"], r["seller_type_raw"], r["seller_type_iaai"])
        seen.setdefault(key, [0, r["seller_class"], r["seller_class_source"]])
        seen[key][0] += 1
    print("\n  --- seller classification audit (kept + dropped) ---")
    print(f"      {'n':>3s}  {'class':<10s} {'seller.type':<14s} "
          f"{'SellerType':<12s} source                 name")
    for (name, st, it), (n, cls, src) in sorted(
            seen.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0]):
        print(f"      {n:>3d}  {cls:<10s} {str(st or '—'):<14s} "
              f"{str(it or '—'):<12s} {src:<22s} {name or '—'}")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main(argv=None):
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)

    if args.body_style and args.platform == "copart":
        raise SystemExit(
            "--body-style is IAAI-only: vehicle_specs.body_style is null on "
            "100% of Copart records and no server-side param exists. Split by "
            "model name instead (Audi S5 = coupe vs S5 Sportback = 4-door).")
    if args.max_pages < 1:
        raise SystemExit("--max-pages must be >= 1")

    params, filters = resolve_filters(args)
    out_base = resolve_out_path(args, params)

    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"{args.platform.upper()} — {args.mode} lots")
    print(f"  server-side: {params}")
    print(f"  client-side: {filters_json(filters)}")
    print(f"  budget:      up to {args.max_pages} call(s)")
    print("=" * 78)

    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"\n  DRY RUN — no call made.\n  GET {build_url('/vehicles', params)}")
        print(f"  would write -> {out_base}.json / .csv")
        return 0

    api_key = read_env_key()
    if not api_key:
        raise SystemExit(f"No APIBARA_API_KEY found in {ENV_PATH}")

    out = {
        "generated_at": dt.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "argv": sys.argv[1:],
        "platform": args.platform,
        "mode": args.mode,
        "server_params": params,
        "client_filters": filters_json(filters),
        "pages": [],
    }
    calls, cursor, kept, dropped, all_rows = 0, None, [], [], []

    while calls < args.max_pages:
        page_params = dict(params)
        if cursor:
            page_params["cursor"] = cursor
        code, data = get(api_key, "/vehicles", page_params)
        calls += 1
        page = {"status": code}
        if not args.no_raw:
            page["raw"] = data
        out["pages"].append(page)

        if code != 200:
            print(f"\n  HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:400]}")
            break

        rows = data.get("data") or []
        for v in rows:
            row = flatten(v)
            all_rows.append(row)
            ok, why = keep(v, filters)
            (kept if ok else dropped).append((row, why))
        cursor = (data.get("meta") or {}).get("next_cursor")
        print(f"\n  page {calls}: {len(rows)} lot(s) returned"
              f"   (more pages: {bool(cursor)})")
        if not cursor:
            break
        time.sleep(RATE_DELAY)

    print(f"\n  KEPT {len(kept)}   dropped {len(dropped)} by client-side filters\n")
    for i, (r, _) in enumerate(kept, 1):
        show(r, i)
    if dropped:
        print("\n  --- dropped ---")
        for r, why in dropped:
            print(f"      lot {str(r['lot_number'] or '?'):>10s} {r['year']} "
                  f"{r['model'] or ''}  ({why})")
    if all_rows:
        seller_audit(all_rows)

    kept_rows = [r for r, _ in kept]
    out["counts"] = {"returned": len(all_rows), "kept": len(kept_rows),
                     "dropped": len(dropped), "calls_used": calls}
    out["rows"] = kept_rows
    out["dropped_rows"] = [{"lot_number": r["lot_number"], "reason": why}
                           for r, why in dropped]

    out_base.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    json_path = out_base.with_suffix(".json")
    csv_path = out_base.with_suffix(".csv")
    with open(json_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    with open(csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=CSV_COLUMNS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(kept_rows)

    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(f"Done. {calls} API call(s) used.")
    print(f"  JSON -> {json_path}")
    print(f"  CSV  -> {csv_path}  ({len(kept_rows)} row(s))")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```
# options whose value may legitimately start with "-" (e.g. "-coupe"), which
# argparse would otherwise read as the next flag
_MINUS_VALUE_OPTS = {"--body-style"}


def glue_minus_values(argv):
    """Rewrite `--body-style -coupe` into `--body-style=-coupe` so the exclude
    syntax works without shell-hostile quoting."""
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if (tok in _MINUS_VALUE_OPTS and i + 1 < len(argv)
                and argv[i + 1].startswith("-")):
            out.append(f"{tok}={argv[i + 1]}")
            i += 2
            continue
        out.append(tok)
        i += 1
    return out
```

```
def money_num(v):
    """IAAI reports money as text ('$29,240 USD'); analytics needs a number."""
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return float(v)
    m = re.search(r"-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?", str(v or ""))
    return float(m.group(0).replace(",", "")) if m else None
```

Done — [analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py](analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py). Verified without spending any API quota: dry-runs for the URL/param resolution, plus an offline replay of every filter and a stubbed end-to-end `main()` run against the saved `test_run/` pulls (15 IAAI + 20 Copart records). No files written into the repo, 0 of your 100 calls used.

**On the other chats:** I can't see them. What I do have is [.cc-discussion/Analyze car API architecture and endpoint flow.md](.cc-discussion/Analyze%20car%20API%20architecture%20and%20endpoint%20flow.md) — a 71KB session log in the repo. I didn't read it for this task since the two source scripts had what I needed, but say the word and I'll pull decisions out of it.

### The CLI, as specified

```bash
python analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py iaai sold \
    --make Audi --model S5 --year-range 2018-2023 \
    --auction-date-range 2026-04-20 2026-05-11 \
    --seller insurance --body-style -coupe --engine-type V6
```

One date in `--auction-date-range` means today→that date. `--dry-run` prints the exact request URL and resolved filters without calling. `--max-pages` defaults to 1 and each page is one call. Output goes to `analytics/sold-data/` as an auto-named pair: `.json` (raw pages + filters + rows) and `.csv` (45 flattened columns — the analytics input).

`--body-style -coupe` needed a small argv pre-pass ([pull_apibara_01.py:341](analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py#L341)); argparse otherwise reads `-coupe` as a flag. Passing `--body-style` with `copart` is refused outright rather than silently returning nothing.

### Insurance vs dealer — what actually qualifies it

You flagged this as needing verification. It does, and the answer differs by platform. `seller_class()` cascades `seller.type` → `details.sale_information.SellerType` (IAAI-only) → carrier-name keywords, and records which field decided in a `seller_class_source` column. Every run also prints a seller audit table so the inference stays checkable:

| | Copart (20 lots) | IAAI (15 lots) |
|---|---|---|
| `seller.type` | 11 insurance / 8 `non_insurance` / 1 unknown | 10 insurance / 5 **unknown** — never emits `non_insurance` |
| `SellerType` | absent (no `details` block) | `"Insurance"` on the same 10, absent on the rest |

So **`--seller insurance` is solid on both platforms.** `--seller dealer` is exact on Copart and *inferred* on IAAI — the 5 untyped lots include "Turo Inc" and "Alamo Financial Group", which are exactly the third-party sellers you want, but IAAI never states it. The name heuristic classes those two as dealer and leaves 3 genuinely nameless lots as `unknown` (excluded from both buckets). Treat IAAI dealer results as a lead list, not a fact.

### Two judgment calls

**`--engine-type` matches on cylinder count, not layout.** Copart's engine string is bare `"3.0L 6"` with `layout: null`, while IAAI gives `"3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo, 354HP"`. Layout-based matching would drop 100% of Copart lots. So `V4` means any 4-cylinder — which is what you want anyway, since a transverse V4 barely exists and real 4-cylinders are inline. I added `V8` since it fell out for free.

**IAAI's ACV and repair estimates arrive as strings** (`"$29,240 USD"`). The CSV carries both `acv_usd`/`est_repair_usd` as numbers and `acv_raw`/`est_repair_raw` as originals.

One thing to decide: `analytics/sold-data/` is **not** in `.gitignore` (unlike `test_run/`), so pulls will land in git. That may be intentional if the corpus is the deliverable — tell me which way you want it.

```
# GET /vehicles Query Parameters

## Complete Parameter List

According to the documentation, the exact documented search parameters are:

> "`s`, `platform`, `auction_type`, `lot_status`, `lot_sub_status`, `make`, `model`, `type`, `year_from`, `year_to`, `price_min`, `price_max`, `odometer_from`, `odometer_to`, `engine_size_from`, `engine_size_to`, `engine_hp_from`, `engine_hp_to`, `color[]`, `fuel_type[]`, `transmission[]`, `drive_type[]`, `cylinders[]`, `damage[]`, `run_cond`, `has_key`, `facility_id`, `loc_state`, `office_name`, `zip`, `radius`, `units`, `auction_date_from`, `auction_date_to`, `today_only`, `sale_document_pending`, `sale_document_type`, `seller_type`, `has_shipping_price`, `per_page`, `cursor`"

## Answers to Your Specific Questions

**(1) Body style / type parameter:**
The parameter is `type`. The documentation states to "Use values from `/vehicles/filters`" rather than providing a hardcoded enum, as "available filter metadata can evolve."

**(2) Seller type parameter and values:**
The parameter is `seller_type`. Documented normalized values are:

> "`dealer`, `finance`, `insurance`, `non_insurance`"

The docs note: "Seller normalization depends on source data."

**(3) Cylinders parameter:**
The parameter is `cylinders[]` (array format using repeated keys, matching the pattern of `color[]`, `fuel_type[]`, etc.). No specific enum values are documented—consult `/vehicles/filters` for current options.
```

```
`GET https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction/vehicles/filters`

## Query Parameters

The documentation does not specify any query parameters for this endpoint. The reference states: `"Use this endpoint before building a filter interface."`

## Response Contents

- Auction platform
- Makes
- Models grouped by make

- Year ranges

- Engine displacement ranges

- Sale documents
- Seller types
- Shipping availability
- States
- Facilities
```

917	
918	`data` is an **object**, not an array; rows carry **four keys**, not full records; there's an

"""
Apibara live test — are BODY STYLE and SELLER TYPE filterable SERVER-SIDE?

Run (from anywhere; paths resolve off this file's location):
    python test/test_apibara_filters_01.py

Budget: up to 5 calls of your 100/mo — one per enabled entry in RUN below.
Set any entry to False to skip it.

WHY
---
analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py filters body style and seller class
CLIENT-side, which burns page slots: an excluded lot still consumes one of the
20 rows a call returns. https://apibara.tech/llms-full.txt lists two params
that were never tried and would move both filters server-side:

    type          "Use values from /vehicles/filters" — docs never enumerate it.
                  Prior evidence says this is a vehicle CLASS, not a body style:
                  the response field `type` is "AUTOMOBILE" on 100% of records
                  observed. TEST 1 settles what values actually exist.
    seller_type   documented enum: dealer | finance | insurance | non_insurance
                  Four buckets — richer than the two that IAAI records expose
                  (seller.type is only ever "insurance" or "unknown" there).
                  If the SERVER knows a lot is `dealer` or `finance` while the
                  RESPONSE says "unknown", the filter beats the payload and the
                  insurance/dealer/other split becomes exact instead of inferred.

CONTROL SET
-----------
Every /vehicles probe reuses the exact PARAMS of test_apibara_sold_iaai_01.py,
whose 15 lots are already on disk in test_run/apibara_sold_iaai_01.json. That
baseline is the answer key:

    body_style   12 Sedan/Hatchback · 2 Coupe · 1 Convertible
    seller       10 seller.type="insurance" · 5 seller.type="unknown", of which
                 "Turo Inc" and "Alamo Financial Group" are the third-party
                 sellers the "other" bucket is meant to catch, and 3 are nameless

So each probe has a known-correct expected result, printed next to what came
back. A filter that returns all 15 is being IGNORED, not applied — that is the
failure mode to watch for, and it is why every probe diffs against the baseline
instead of just counting rows.

Reads APIBARA_API_KEY from the repo-root .env; saves raw JSON to
test_run/apibara_filters_01.json.
"""
import json
import os
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent   # repo root
ENV_PATH = ROOT / ".env"
OUT_DIR = ROOT / "test_run"
BASELINE = OUT_DIR / "apibara_sold_iaai_01.json"

BASE = "https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction"
RATE_DELAY = 1.5

# 1 call each — flip to False to skip
RUN = {
    "filters": True,        # TEST 1: enumerate /vehicles/filters
    "type_coupe": True,     # TEST 2: type=<coupe-ish value, if TEST 1 finds one>
    "seller_insurance": True,   # TEST 3: seller_type=insurance
    "seller_dealer": True,      # TEST 4: seller_type=dealer
    "seller_other": True,       # TEST 5: seller_type=non_insurance (+finance)
}

# identical to test_apibara_sold_iaai_01.py — the control set
PARAMS = {
    "platform": "iaai",
    "make": "Audi",
    "model": "S5",
    "year_from": 2018,
    "year_to": 2023,
    "lot_sub_status": "Ended",
    "auction_date_from": "2026-04-20",
    "auction_date_to": "2026-05-11",
    "per_page": 20,
}


def read_env_key(path=ENV_PATH, name="APIBARA_API_KEY"):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return ""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
                continue
            k, _, v = line.partition("=")
            if k.strip() == name:
                return v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return ""


def get(api_key, path, params=None):
    url = f"{BASE}{path}"
    if params:
        url += "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={
        "Accept": "application/json", "X-API-Key": api_key})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            return resp.getcode(), json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, {"error_body": e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:800]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return 0, {"error": str(e)}


def load_baseline():
    """-> {lot_number: {body_style, seller_type, seller_name}} from _01's pull."""
    if not BASELINE.exists():
        return {}
    d = json.loads(BASELINE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out = {}
    for p in d.get("pages", []):
        if p.get("status") != 200:
            continue
        for v in (p.get("raw", {}).get("data") or []):
            out[v.get("lot_number")] = {
                "body_style": (v.get("vehicle_specs") or {}).get("body_style"),
                "seller_type": (v.get("seller") or {}).get("type"),
                "seller_name": (v.get("seller") or {}).get("name"),
            }
    return out


def summarize(rows, base, label, expect_lots=None):
    """Print what came back and diff it against the baseline answer key."""
    got = {v.get("lot_number") for v in rows}
    print(f"\n  {label}: {len(rows)} lot(s) returned")

    for v in rows:
        bs = (v.get("vehicle_specs") or {}).get("body_style") or "—"
        s = v.get("seller") or {}
        print(f"      {str(v.get('lot_number')):>10s}  {bs:<18s} "
              f"seller.type={str(s.get('type') or '—'):<14s} {s.get('name') or '—'}")

    if base:
        missing = set(base) - got
        print(f"      vs baseline({len(base)}): kept {len(got & set(base))}, "
              f"dropped {len(missing)}, new {len(got - set(base))}")
        if len(got) == len(base):
            print("      *** returned the FULL baseline -> filter was IGNORED ***")
    if expect_lots is not None:
        exact = got == set(expect_lots)
        print(f"      expected exactly {sorted(expect_lots)} -> "
              f"{'MATCH' if exact else 'MISMATCH'}")
    return got


def main():
    api_key = read_env_key()
    if not api_key:
        raise SystemExit(f"No APIBARA_API_KEY found in {ENV_PATH}")

    base = load_baseline()
    coupes = [k for k, v in base.items() if v["body_style"] == "Coupe"]
    insured = [k for k, v in base.items() if v["seller_type"] == "insurance"]
    unknown = [k for k, v in base.items() if v["seller_type"] == "unknown"]
    named_unknown = [k for k in unknown if (base[k]["seller_name"] or "unknown")
                     .lower() != "unknown"]

    out = {"params": PARAMS, "run": RUN, "tests": {}}
    calls = 0

    print("=" * 78)
    print("SERVER-SIDE FILTER PROBE — body style (`type`) and `seller_type`")
    print(f"  control set: {PARAMS}")
    if base:
        print(f"  baseline on disk: {len(base)} lot(s) — "
              f"{len(coupes)} Coupe, {len(insured)} insurance, "
              f"{len(unknown)} unknown ({len(named_unknown)} of them named)")
    else:
        print(f"  NO BASELINE at {BASELINE} — diffs will be skipped")
    print("=" * 78)

    # ---- TEST 1: what values does `type` actually take? -------------------
    type_values = []
    if RUN["filters"]:
        print("\n[1] GET /vehicles/filters — enumerate `type` and `seller_type`")
        code, data = get(api_key, "/vehicles/filters")
        calls += 1
        out["tests"]["filters"] = {"status": code, "raw": data}
        if code != 200:
            print(f"    HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:300]}")
        else:
            payload = data.get("data") if isinstance(data.get("data"), dict) else data
            print(f"    top-level keys: {sorted(payload.keys())[:40]}")
            for key in ("types", "type", "vehicle_types", "body_styles",
                        "seller_types", "seller_type"):
                if key in payload:
                    val = payload[key]
                    print(f"    {key}: {json.dumps(val)[:600]}")
                    if key in ("types", "type", "vehicle_types", "body_styles"):
                        if isinstance(val, list):
                            type_values = [
                                (x.get("value") or x.get("name") or x.get("label"))
                                if isinstance(x, dict) else x for x in val]
        time.sleep(RATE_DELAY)

    # ---- TEST 2: does `type` filter body style? ---------------------------
    if RUN["type_coupe"]:
        candidate = next((t for t in type_values
                          if "coupe" in str(t).lower()), None)
        print(f"\n[2] GET /vehicles with type=<coupe> "
              f"(candidate from TEST 1: {candidate!r})")
        if candidate is None:
            candidate = "Coupe"
            print("    no coupe-like value in /vehicles/filters — trying the "
                  "literal 'Coupe' anyway, to see if it 422s or is ignored")
        params = {**PARAMS, "type": candidate}
        code, data = get(api_key, "/vehicles", params)
        calls += 1
        out["tests"]["type_coupe"] = {"params": params, "status": code,
                                      "raw": data}
        if code != 200:
            print(f"    HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:300]}")
            print("    -> `type` REJECTS this value; not a body-style filter")
        else:
            summarize(data.get("data") or [], base,
                      f"type={candidate}", expect_lots=coupes or None)
        time.sleep(RATE_DELAY)

    # ---- TESTS 3-5: does `seller_type` filter, and how many buckets? ------
    for key, value in (("seller_insurance", "insurance"),
                       ("seller_dealer", "dealer"),
                       ("seller_other", "non_insurance")):
        if not RUN[key]:
            continue
        expect = insured if value == "insurance" else None
        print(f"\n[{3 + ('insurance dealer non_insurance'.split()).index(value)}] "
              f"GET /vehicles with seller_type={value}")
        params = {**PARAMS, "seller_type": value}
        code, data = get(api_key, "/vehicles", params)
        calls += 1
        out["tests"][key] = {"params": params, "status": code, "raw": data}
        if code != 200:
            print(f"    HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:300]}")
        else:
            rows = data.get("data") or []
            summarize(rows, base, f"seller_type={value}", expect_lots=expect)
            if value != "insurance" and rows:
                hits = [v.get("lot_number") for v in rows
                        if v.get("lot_number") in named_unknown]
                print(f"      of the {len(named_unknown)} named-but-untyped "
                      f"baseline lots (Turo / Alamo), this returned: "
                      f"{hits or 'none'}")
        time.sleep(RATE_DELAY)

    OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out_path = OUT_DIR / "apibara_filters_01.json"
    out["calls_used"] = calls
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(f"Done. {calls} API call(s) used. Raw JSON -> {out_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Edit**: /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker/analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py</summary>

*old_string*
```
    python analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py iaai sold \
        --make Audi --model S5 \
        --year-range 2018-2023 \
        --auction-date-range 2026-04-20 2026-05-11 \
        --seller insurance \
        --body-style -coupe \
        --engine-type V6

BUDGET: 1 API call per page, `--max-pages` pages (default 1) of your 100/month.
Use `--dry-run` to print the exact request URL and the resolved filters without
spending a call. Nothing else in this script hits the network.

OUTPUT (both written, same basename, into analytics/sold-data/):
    <basename>.json   raw pages + resolved filters + flattened rows
    <basename>.csv    flattened rows only — the analytics input

WHAT IS SERVER-SIDE vs CLIENT-SIDE
----------------------------------
server-side : platform, make, model, year_from/to, lot_sub_status,
              auction_date_from/to, per_page, cursor
client-side : body style, engine type, seller class, damage exclusion
              (Apibara has no param for any of them; `damage` exists but is an
              INCLUDE-only whitelist whose enum cannot express collision damage)

SELLER CLASSIFICATION  (`--seller insurance|dealer|any`)
-------------------------------------------------------
There is no single trustworthy field, so `seller_class()` cascades, and the
field that decided each lot is recorded in the `seller_class_source` column so
the classification stays auditable:

  1. seller.type == "insurance"                 -> insurance   (both platforms)
     seller.type == "non_insurance"             -> dealer      (Copart only)
  2. details.sale_information.SellerType         -> IAAI-only mirror of the above
  3. name keywords on seller.name / .Seller      -> insurance if it looks like a
     carrier, else dealer

Measured on the current test_run/ pulls:
  Copart 20/20 typed cleanly (11 insurance / 8 non_insurance / 1 unknown).
  IAAI   10/15 typed "insurance"; the other 5 come back seller.type="unknown"
         with SellerType absent — and their names ("Turo Inc", "Alamo Financial
         Group") are exactly the third-party/fleet sellers the dealer bucket is
         meant to catch. IAAI never emits "non_insurance", so on IAAI *dealer is
         inferred, not stated*: it means "named seller that is not a carrier".
         `--seller insurance` is the precise half of the filter; treat
         `--seller dealer` on IAAI as a lead list, not a fact.

ENGINE TYPE  (`--engine-type V4|V6|other`, repeatable)
-----------------------------------------------------
Matching is by CYLINDER COUNT, not literal layout — a transverse "V4" is
essentially a marketing fiction, real 4-cylinders are inline, so V4 == any
4-cylinder. V6/V8 likewise mean 6/8 cylinders. `other` = anything else,
including engines that could not be parsed (electric, unparseable strings).
Source is vehicle_specs.engine: IAAI is rich ("3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo,
354HP", layout "V"), Copart is bare ("3.0L 6", layout null) — hence the
count-first approach; layout-based matching would drop every Copart lot.

BODY STYLE  (`--body-style [-]<style>`, repeatable, IAAI ONLY)
-------------------------------------------------------------
Prefix with "-" to exclude, no prefix to include (mixing both = include-list
wins, then exclusions apply). vehicle_specs.body_style is populated on 100% of
IAAI records (Sedan / Sedan/Hatchback / Coupe / Convertible) and null on 100%
of Copart records. Passing --body-style with `copart` is refused rather than
silently returning nothing.

DAMAGE
------
```

```
BUDGET: 1 API call per page, `--max-pages` pages (default 1) of your 100/month.
Use `--dry-run` to print the exact request URL and the resolved filters without
spending a call. Nothing else in this script hits the network.

OUTPUT (both written, same basename, into analytics/sold-data/):
    <basename>.json   raw pages + resolved filters + flattened rows
    <basename>.csv    flattened rows only — the analytics input

WHAT IS SERVER-SIDE vs CLIENT-SIDE
----------------------------------
Server-side filtering is strictly better than client-side here: a lot rejected
client-side has already consumed one of the 20 rows the call returned, so the
same 1-call budget yields fewer usable rows. Everything that CAN go server-side
does. Verified live by test/test_apibara_filters_01.py (see that file for the
raw evidence; test_run/apibara_filters_01*.json holds the responses):

  server-side : platform, make, model, year_from/to, lot_sub_status,
                auction_date_from/to, seller_type, cylinders[], per_page, cursor
  client-side : damage exclusion (`damage` is an INCLUDE-only whitelist whose
                enum — Fire/Hail/Theft/Water/Chemical/Rollover/Mechanical/
                Vandalized/Repossession — cannot express the collision damage
                that is ~80% of lots, and there is no negation param);
                the "other" seller bucket; the "other" engine bucket.

BODY STYLE — NOT SUPPORTED, DELIBERATELY REMOVED
------------------------------------------------
There is a `type` param and /vehicles/filters advertises SEDAN / COUPE / SUV /
PICKUP / VAN / RV as values, which looks like a body-style filter. It is not.
`type` matches the record's vehicle-CLASS field, and every car is "AUTOMOBILE":

    type=AUTOMOBILE -> 15 of 15 control lots      (param works, matches class)
    type=COUPE      ->  0 of 15, including the 2 lots whose
                        vehicle_specs.body_style is literally "Coupe"

So COUPE is reachable in the enum but unreachable in the data, and asking for it
silently returns nothing. body_style is still emitted as an OUTPUT column (IAAI
populates it on 100% of records, Copart on 0%) — filter on it in pandas after
the pull. For the S5 specifically the server-side workaround is the model name:
Audi splits `S5` (coupe) from `S5 Sportback` (4-door), so `--model "S5
Sportback"` does the job at the API.

SELLER  (`--seller insurance|dealer|other|any`)
-----------------------------------------------
`seller_type` is a real server-side param, but only two of its four documented
values behave. Measured against the 15-lot control set:

    seller_type=insurance      -> 10 lots, EXACTLY the 10 whose seller.type
                                  says "insurance". Precise; use it.
    seller_type=dealer         ->  1 lot, "Alamo Financial Group" — whose own
                                  payload says seller.type="unknown". The server
                                  knows a classification it does not serialise.
    seller_type=non_insurance  -> all 15, insurance lots included. A no-op.
                                  NEVER SENT by this script.
    seller_type=finance        ->  0 lots.

So insurance and dealer go server-side; `--seller other` cannot (it would need
the no-op value or negation) and is computed client-side as "not insurance and
not carrier-named".

  CAVEAT — two taxonomies, not one. Apibara's `dealer` bucket contains "Alamo
  Financial Group", and "Turo Inc" lands in NO server bucket at all (absent from
  insurance, dealer and finance alike). Both are the third-party/fleet sellers
  that `--seller other` is meant to catch, so `other` and Apibara's `dealer` do
  overlap. `--seller other` is a lead list, not a partition. `--seller insurance`
  is the one that is exact, and it is exact on both platforms.

Client-side classification (`--seller-client`, and the `seller_class` column,
which is always computed so the two views can be diffed) cascades:
  1. seller.type "insurance" -> insurance;  "non_insurance"/"dealer" -> dealer
  2. details.sale_information.SellerType    (IAAI-only mirror of the above)
  3. seller.name: carrier keywords -> insurance; any other name -> other;
     no name -> unknown
Copart types 20/20 cleanly (11 insurance / 8 non_insurance / 1 unknown); IAAI
types 10/15 and leaves the rest "unknown", which is why step 3 exists.

ENGINE TYPE  (`--engine-type V4|V6|V8|other`, repeatable)
---------------------------------------------------------
Sent server-side as `cylinders[]`, whose /vehicles/filters enum is
1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12. Matching is by CYLINDER COUNT, not literal layout — a
transverse "V4" is essentially a marketing fiction, real 4-cylinders are inline,
so V4 == any 4-cylinder. `other` has no server-side expression (it would need
negation) and falls back to client-side matching on vehicle_specs.engine, which
is rich on IAAI ("3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo, 354HP") and bare on Copart
("3.0L 6", layout null) — hence count-first parsing; layout-based matching would
drop every Copart lot.

DAMAGE
------
```

```
def seller_class(v):
    """-> (class, source). class in {insurance, dealer, other, unknown}.

    A named seller that is not a carrier lands in `other`, not `dealer`: on IAAI
    those are fleet/rental/finance sellers (Turo Inc, Alamo Financial Group) and
    nothing in the payload distinguishes them from an actual dealership. Only a
    platform that states `non_insurance`/`dealer` outright yields `dealer`.
    """
    stype = ((v.get("seller") or {}).get("type") or "").strip().lower()
    if stype == "insurance":
        return "insurance", "seller.type"
    if stype in ("non_insurance", "non-insurance", "dealer"):
        return "dealer", "seller.type"

    itype = str(sale_info(v).get("SellerType") or "").strip().lower()
    if itype:
        if "insur" in itype:
            return "insurance", "sale_information.SellerType"
        return "dealer", "sale_information.SellerType"

    name = str((v.get("seller") or {}).get("name")
               or sale_info(v).get("Seller") or "").strip().lower()
    if not name or name == "unknown":
        return "unknown", "none"
    if any(n in name for n in _INSURER_NEEDLES):
        return "insurance", "seller.name"
    return "other", "seller.name~inferred"
```

*new_string*

```
def keep(v, f):
    """Apply the client-side half of the filters. -> (bool, reason).

    Filters already pushed server-side are absent here by design — re-checking
    `seller_type=insurance` client-side would reject the very lots the server
    classified from data it does not serialise (see the module docstring).
    """
    if f["engine_client"] and engine_class(v) not in f["engine_client"]:
        return False, f"engine={engine_class(v)}"

    if f["seller_client"]:
        cls, _ = seller_class(v)
        if cls != f["seller_client"]:
            return False, f"seller={cls}"

    hit = next((n for n in f["exclude_damage"] if n in damage_text(v)), None)
    if hit:
        return False, f"damage~{hit}"

    return True, ""
```

```
# options whose value may legitimately start with "-" (e.g. "-coupe"), which
# argparse would otherwise read as the next flag
_MINUS_VALUE_OPTS = {"--body-style"}


def glue_minus_values(argv):
    """Rewrite `--body-style -coupe` into `--body-style=-coupe` so the exclude
    syntax works without shell-hostile quoting."""
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if (tok in _MINUS_VALUE_OPTS and i + 1 < len(argv)
                and argv[i + 1].startswith("-")):
            out.append(f"{tok}={argv[i + 1]}")
            i += 2
            continue
        out.append(tok)
        i += 1
    return out
```

Done. 9 API calls used total (5 + 2 + 2); everything else was offline replay against saved pulls.

**Yes, I read [.cc-discussion/Analyze car API architecture and endpoint flow.md](.cc-discussion/Analyze%20car%20API%20architecture%20and%20endpoint%20flow.md).** It's what pointed me at the answer — line 574 lists `seller_type` and `cylinders` as server-side params that no script had ever sent, and lines 535–545 already suspected `type` was a vehicle class rather than a body style. The log had the hypothesis; this session tested it.

## 1. Body style server-side: no. Dropped.

`/vehicles/filters` does advertise `SEDAN / COUPE / SUV / PICKUP / VAN / RV` under `type`, which looks exactly like what you wanted. It isn't:

| request | returned |
|---|---|
| `type=AUTOMOBILE` | **15 of 15** — param works, matches the vehicle-*class* field |
| `type=COUPE` | **0 of 15** — including the 2 lots whose `body_style` literally says "Coupe" |

The positive control is what makes this conclusive: `type` is applied, it just reads the record's `type` field, which is `"AUTOMOBILE"` on every car. `COUPE` is reachable in the enum and unreachable in the data — it fails *silently*, returning nothing rather than erroring.

So `--body-style` is gone, per your instruction. Two things preserved on the way out: `body_style` is still an **output column** (IAAI populates it 100%, so you can filter in pandas post-pull), and the docstring records the server-side workaround that does work — Audi splits `S5` from `S5 Sportback`, so `--model "S5 Sportback"` filters 4-doors at the API.

## 2. Seller: the 3-way split is half server-side

`seller_type` is real, but only two of its four documented values behave:

| value | result on the 15-lot control set |
|---|---|
| `insurance` | **10 lots — exactly the 10** whose payload says insurance. Precise. |
| `dealer` | **1 lot** — "Alamo Financial Group", whose own payload says `seller.type="unknown"`. The server knows a classification it doesn't serialize. |
| `non_insurance` | **all 15**, insurance included. A no-op — the script never sends it. |
| `finance` | 0 lots. |

So: `--seller insurance` and `--seller dealer` now go server-side (no wasted page slots); `--seller other` stays client-side.

**The catch worth knowing before you rely on it:** Apibara's taxonomy isn't yours. Its `dealer` bucket *contains* Alamo Financial Group, and **Turo Inc appears in no server bucket at all** — absent from insurance, dealer, and finance alike. Both are precisely the third-party sellers your "other" was meant to catch, so `other` and Apibara's `dealer` overlap. `--seller insurance` is the exact one, on both platforms. `--seller other` is a lead list, not a clean partition. `--seller-client` forces client-side classification so you can diff the two views.

## 3. Two things fell out for free

Mining the already-paid-for `/vehicles/filters` response, no extra calls:

- **`cylinders[]` accepts 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12** — so `--engine-type` moved server-side. I verified the bracket syntax in both directions rather than trusting it (`cylinders[]=6` → all 15, `cylinders[]=4` → 0), specifically because `type=COUPE` had just demonstrated the silent-zero failure mode. `other` still needs negation the API lacks, so it stays client-side.
- **`lot_sub_status` is `Open | Live | Ended`** — my `live` mode had been sending a guessed `lot_status=All` plus a client-side drop. Now it sends `lot_sub_status=Open`.

Net effect on a `--seller insurance --engine-type V6` pull: everything but damage exclusion is now server-side, so all 20 rows of a call come back usable.
