*old_string*
```
WHAT IS SERVER-SIDE vs CLIENT-SIDE
----------------------------------
Server-side filtering is strictly better than client-side here: a lot rejected
client-side has already consumed one of the 20 rows the call returned, so the
same 1-call budget yields fewer usable rows. Everything that CAN go server-side
does. Verified live by test/test_apibara_filters_01.py (see that file for the
raw evidence; test_run/apibara_filters_01*.json holds the responses):

  server-side : platform, make, model, year_from/to, lot_sub_status,
                auction_date_from/to, seller_type, cylinders[], per_page, cursor
  client-side : damage exclusion (`damage` is an INCLUDE-only whitelist whose
                enum — Fire/Hail/Theft/Water/Chemical/Rollover/Mechanical/
                Vandalized/Repossession — cannot express the collision damage
                that is ~80% of lots, and there is no negation param);
                the "other" seller bucket; the "other" engine bucket.
```
*new_string*
```
DESIGN RULE: EVERY FILTER MIRRORS A SERVER-SIDE PARAM
-----------------------------------------------------
Each CLI filter maps 1:1 onto an Apibara query param and takes that param's own
enum — no invented vocabulary, no client-side approximation of something the
API already does. Client-side filtering is strictly worse here: a lot rejected
locally has already consumed one of the 20 rows the call returned, so the same
1-call budget yields fewer usable rows.

    positional 2   -> lot_sub_status   {open|live|ended}
    --seller       -> seller_type      {insurance|dealer}
    --cylinders    -> cylinders[]      {1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12}
    --make/--model -> make/model
    --year-range   -> year_from/year_to
    --auction-date-range -> auction_date_from/auction_date_to

Every enum above came from GET /vehicles/filters and was then verified against
live data by test/test_apibara_filters_01.py — worth doing, because a bad value
fails SILENTLY here (`type=COUPE` returns 0 rows rather than an error). Raw
responses are in test_run/apibara_filters_01.json.

The ONE exception is damage exclusion, which cannot be server-side: `damage` is
an INCLUDE-only whitelist whose enum (Fire/Hail/Theft/Water/Chemical/Rollover/
Mechanical/Vandalized/Repossession) cannot express the collision damage that is
~80% of lots, and there is no negation param.

DERIVED COLUMNS ARE NOT FILTERS
-------------------------------
`seller_class` (insurance/dealer/other/unknown) and the parsed engine columns
are still computed and written to every row, but nothing filters on them. They
exist so a later stage can draw distinctions the API cannot — notably splitting
Apibara's `dealer` bucket, which lumps in fleet/rental/finance sellers (Turo
Inc, Alamo Financial Group). That differentiation is deliberately deferred.
```

```
SELLER  (`--seller insurance|dealer|other|any`)
-----------------------------------------------
`seller_type` is a real server-side param, but only two of its four documented
values behave. Measured against the 15-lot control set:

    seller_type=insurance      -> 10 lots, EXACTLY the 10 whose seller.type
                                  says "insurance". Precise; use it.
    seller_type=dealer         ->  1 lot, "Alamo Financial Group" — whose own
                                  payload says seller.type="unknown". The server
                                  knows a classification it does not serialise.
    seller_type=non_insurance  -> all 15, insurance lots included. A no-op.
                                  NEVER SENT by this script.
    seller_type=finance        ->  0 lots.

So insurance and dealer go server-side; `--seller other` cannot (it would need
the no-op value or negation) and is computed client-side as "not insurance and
not carrier-named".

  CAVEAT — two taxonomies, not one. Apibara's `dealer` bucket contains "Alamo
  Financial Group", and "Turo Inc" lands in NO server bucket at all (absent from
  insurance, dealer and finance alike). Both are the third-party/fleet sellers
  that `--seller other` is meant to catch, so `other` and Apibara's `dealer` do
  overlap. `--seller other` is a lead list, not a partition. `--seller insurance`
  is the one that is exact, and it is exact on both platforms.

Client-side classification (`--seller-client`, and the `seller_class` column,
which is always computed so the two views can be diffed) cascades:
  1. seller.type "insurance" -> insurance;  "non_insurance"/"dealer" -> dealer
  2. details.sale_information.SellerType    (IAAI-only mirror of the above)
  3. seller.name: carrier keywords -> insurance; any other name -> other;
     no name -> unknown
Copart types 20/20 cleanly (11 insurance / 8 non_insurance / 1 unknown); IAAI
types 10/15 and leaves the rest "unknown", which is why step 3 exists.

ENGINE TYPE  (`--engine-type V4|V6|V8|other`, repeatable)
---------------------------------------------------------
Sent server-side as `cylinders[]`, whose /vehicles/filters enum is
1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12. Matching is by CYLINDER COUNT, not literal layout — a
transverse "V4" is essentially a marketing fiction, real 4-cylinders are inline,
so V4 == any 4-cylinder. `other` has no server-side expression (it would need
negation) and falls back to client-side matching on vehicle_specs.engine, which
is rich on IAAI ("3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo, 354HP") and bare on Copart
("3.0L 6", layout null) — hence count-first parsing; layout-based matching would
drop every Copart lot.
```
*new_string*
```
SELLER  (`--seller insurance|dealer`)
-------------------------------------
`seller_type` documents four values; only two behave, so only two are offered.
Measured against the 15-lot control set:

    seller_type=insurance      -> 10 lots, EXACTLY the 10 whose seller.type
                                  says "insurance". Precise; use it.
    seller_type=dealer         ->  1 lot, "Alamo Financial Group" — whose own
                                  payload says seller.type="unknown". The server
                                  knows a classification it does not serialise,
                                  which is why this filter cannot be reproduced
                                  locally and must be sent to the API.
    seller_type=non_insurance  -> all 15, insurance lots included. A no-op,
                                  NOT offered by this script.
    seller_type=finance        ->  0 lots. Not offered.

Note what `dealer` is NOT: "Turo Inc" appears in no server bucket at all —
absent from insurance, dealer and finance alike — so `dealer` is not the
complement of `insurance`, and the two together do not cover the data. Omit
--seller to get everything.

CYLINDERS  (`--cylinders N`, repeatable or comma-separated)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Sent as `cylinders[]`; enum is 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12 (note: no 7, 9 or 11).
Verified in both directions on the all-V6 control set — `cylinders[]=6` returned
all 15, `cylinders[]=4` returned 0 — which is what distinguishes a working
filter from a silently-ignored param name.
```

```
def engine_class(v):
    """-> 'V4' / 'V6' / 'V8' / 'other'. Cylinder count drives it."""
    cyl, _, _ = engine_info(v)
    if cyl in (4, 6, 8):
        return f"V{cyl}"
    return "other"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# client-side filtering
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def keep(v, f):
    """Apply the client-side half of the filters. -> (bool, reason).

    Filters already pushed server-side are absent here by design — re-checking
    `seller_type=insurance` client-side would reject the very lots the server
    classified from data it does not serialise (see the module docstring).
    """
    if f["engine_client"] and engine_class(v) not in f["engine_client"]:
        return False, f"engine={engine_class(v)}"

    if f["seller_client"]:
        cls, _ = seller_class(v)
        if cls != f["seller_client"]:
            return False, f"seller={cls}"

    hit = next((n for n in f["exclude_damage"] if n in damage_text(v)), None)
    if hit:
        return False, f"damage~{hit}"

    return True, ""
```
*new_string*
```
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# client-side filtering — damage only; everything else is server-side
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def keep(v, f):
    """-> (bool, reason).

    Only damage lands here, because only damage has no server-side expression.
    Nothing re-checks a filter the API already applied: `seller_type=dealer`
    matched a lot whose own payload says "unknown", so re-testing it locally
    would throw away the server's better answer.
    """
    hit = next((n for n in f["exclude_damage"] if n in damage_text(v)), None)
    if hit:
        return False, f"damage~{hit}"
    return True, ""
```

All four changes applied and verified offline (no API calls — stubbed HTTP plus dry-runs).

## What changed

**i) `--body-style` — gone.** Rejected as an unrecognized argument. `body_style` survives as an output column.

**ii) `--seller {insurance|dealer}`** — always server-side as `seller_type`, no client-side path, `--seller-client` removed. Omit it for all sellers. `other` and `non_insurance` are now rejected at the parser.

**iii) `--engine-type` → `--cylinders {1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12}`** — repeatable or comma-separated (`--cylinders 4,6`), sent as `cylinders[]`. Validated against the API's own enum, so `7` and `V6` are both rejected with the allowed list in the message.

**iv) `{live|sold}` → `{open|live|ended}`** — the positional now maps straight onto `lot_sub_status` (`Open`/`Live`/`Ended`). The old client-side "drop finished lots" hack is gone with it.

```
pull_apibara_01.py iaai ended --make Audi --model S5 --seller insurance --cylinders 6
  -> lot_sub_status=Ended, seller_type=insurance, cylinders[]=6, make=Audi, model=S5
```

Client-side filtering is now **damage only** — the one filter with no server-side expression. Every other CLI value is drawn from `LOT_SUB_STATUS` / `CYLINDERS` constants lifted verbatim from `/vehicles/filters`, so anything the script accepts is something the API accepts. That closes the silent-zero trap: a rejected value now fails at the parser instead of returning an empty page.

**Deferred, as you asked:** `seller_class` and `seller_class_source` are still computed on every row and printed in the audit table (Turo Inc and Alamo Financial Group → `other` via name inference), but nothing filters on them. That's the raw material for splitting Apibara's `dealer` bucket later in the pipe, sitting in the CSV rather than shaping the pull. 44 columns now (`engine_class` dropped, `engine_cylinders` retained).

One thing to expect on a real run: my stubbed test replayed the saved *unfiltered* page, so it showed 15 kept. Live, `seller_type=insurance` returns 10 rows from the server — and all 10 are usable, which is the point of the move.

## 1. The damage filter

**Yes, it's a script parameter** — two of them, at [pull_apibara_01.py:406-409](analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py#L406-L409):

```bash
--exclude-damage water,flood,fire    # replace the default needle list
--no-damage-filter                   # keep every damage type
```

Omit both and you get a per-platform default. For IAAI: `water, flood, burn, fire, rollover, storm`. For Copart it's a different list (`all over`, `mechanical` instead of `storm`) because the two platforms use different damage vocabularies — Copart says "Rear end", IAAI says "Rear".

**How it works** — it is applied to the raw API response, in memory, after the call returns:

```python
text = (primary_damage + " " + secondary_damage).lower()
drop if any(needle in text)          # plain substring, both damage fields
```

It's a lowercase **substring** test, not a regex and not a code mapping — so `water` catches `"Water/Flood"`, and both the primary and secondary damage fields are searched (a lot with primary `Front end` + secondary `Water` is dropped).

**It creates no calculated field.** It decides which rows are written:

| where | excluded lot appears? |
|---|---|
| `.csv` | **no** — dropped |
| `.json` → `rows` | **no** — dropped |
| `.json` → `dropped_rows` | **yes** — `{"lot_number": "...", "reason": "damage~water"}` |
| `.json` → `pages[].raw` | **yes** — the untouched API response is preserved (unless `--no-raw`) |
| `.json` → `counts` | counted in `dropped` |

So nothing is lost: the raw payload stays in the JSON, and you can always re-derive a different cut from it without spending another call. The CSV is the filtered analytics view.

**The cost that matters:** this runs *after* the row was paid for. An excluded lot still consumed one of the 20 slots that call returned. That's exactly why every other filter was moved server-side — damage is the only one the API can't express (`damage` is include-only, and its enum has no value for collision).

## 2. Your example

Verified with `--dry-run` (no call spent):

```bash
python analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py iaai ended \
    --make Audi --model S5 \
    --year-range 2018-2023 \
    --auction-date-range 2025-08-01 2026-08-09 \
    --seller insurance \
    --max-pages 12
```

Resolves to `lot_sub_status=Ended`, `seller_type=insurance`, `make/model`, `year_from/to`, `auction_date_from/to` — all server-side. Drop `--max-pages 12` and you get **20 lots and nothing more**, which brings us to your third question.

## 3. No, it does not page until exhausted — and that's deliberate

`--max-pages` defaults to **1**. The loop stops at whichever comes first: `max_pages` reached, or `next_cursor` null. With a 100-call/month budget, a script that silently paged to completion could eat a third of your month on one command.

**`--max-pages` is a cap, not a target.** Setting 12 doesn't spend 12 calls — the loop exits the moment the cursor runs out. So overestimating is free; underestimating silently truncates your dataset. Note there is **no total count in the response** — `meta` carries only `per_page`, `next_cursor`, `prev_cursor` — so the only way to learn how many lots match is to page through them.

## 4. Estimate: ~9 calls (range 6–13)

Extrapolating from the control window, which is the same query on a known-complete result (15 lots, `next_cursor: null`, so nothing was cut off):

| | |
|---|---|
| control: 2026-04-20 → 2026-05-11 | 22 days, **15 lots**, all sellers |
| rate | **0.68 lots/day** |
| your window: 2025-08-01 → 2026-08-09 | **374 days** → ~255 lots, all sellers |
| × insurance share (10/15 = 67%) | **~170 lots** |
| ÷ 20 per page | **~9 calls** |

Because `seller_type=insurance` is server-side, the non-insurance lots never occupy page slots — that filter is what takes this from ~13 calls to ~9.

Two caveats on that number, one of them significant:

- **Small sample.** 15 lots in one 22-day window; Poisson noise alone puts the range around 190–320 lots all-sellers, i.e. **6–13 calls**. `--max-pages 12` covers the upper end safely.
- **Data retention is the real unknown.** Your window reaches back **12+ months**, while every observation I have is from Apr–May 2026. If Apibara prunes ended lots after some horizon, the early months return nothing and the real count lands well under the estimate. I'd treat ~9 as an upper-middle guess and expect fewer.

One practical note: the raw JSON runs ~30KB per lot, so ~170 lots would produce a **~5MB** JSON. Add `--no-raw` if you only want the flattened rows and CSV — but keep the raw on the first real pull, since re-deriving from disk is free and re-pulling is not.

```
Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Copart and IAAI sold auction history API and multi-year historical data:

## API Solutions for Auction History Data

Several services provide API access to Copart and IAAI auction history:

1. **API Auto Auctions (apiauctions.io)** - Offers trading history on Copart and IAAI insurance car auctions with a large database since 2020.

2. **Auction Data (auction-data.info)** - Provides access to all current lots and sales history of Copart and IAAI by API, with requests to their server via API.

3. **Auction API (auction-api.app)** - Offers access to sold vehicles from Copart and IAAI auctions for the past 3 years by VIN or search filters.

## Free Historical Data Platforms

If you're looking for historical data without API integration:

- BidHistory.org provides a free auction price history service for Copart and IAAI where you can check sold car prices, bid history, auction results and final sale prices.
- AutoAstat offers sales history with prices and images from Copart and IAAI auctions.

The search results didn't include specific Reddit discussions, but these are the main platforms currently offering multi-year historical data access through APIs or web interfaces for Copart and IAAI auctions.
```

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Write**: /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker/analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py</summary>

```
"""
Apibara pull — stage 1 of the analytics pipeline. RAW JSON ONLY.

    pull_apibara_01.py  ->  raw .json  ->  apibara_json2csv_<platform>_01.py  ->  .csv

This script does exactly two things: build a server-side query, and archive the
untouched responses. It applies NO filtering and derives NO fields — every
judgement call (damage exclusion, body style, seller classification, column
selection) belongs to the json2csv stage, where it can be re-run any number of
times against the saved JSON without spending API calls.

That split matters because of what the data is: Apibara's active database holds
roughly the last ~10 months (docs, 2026-07-27), and an observed Audi S5 IAAI
pull reached only ~5.5 months back. Lots age out. A raw archive pulled today is
the ONLY copy of that window you will ever have, so it must be stored unfiltered
and unreshaped — a filter applied at pull time destroys data permanently, while
a filter applied at convert time costs nothing.

Run (from anywhere; paths resolve off this file's location):

    python analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py iaai ended \
        --make Audi --model S5 \
        --year-range 2018-2023 \
        --auction-date-range 2025-08-01 2026-08-09 \
        --seller insurance \
        --max-pages 20

BUDGET: 1 API call per page, `--max-pages` pages (default 1) of your 100/month.
--max-pages is a CAP, not a target: paging stops as soon as the cursor runs out,
so overestimating is free while underestimating silently truncates the archive.
`--dry-run` prints the request URL and resolved params without spending a call.

DESIGN RULE: EVERY FILTER MIRRORS A SERVER-SIDE PARAM
-----------------------------------------------------
Each CLI filter maps 1:1 onto an Apibara query param and takes that param's own
enum — no invented vocabulary, no client-side approximation. Client-side
filtering would be strictly worse here anyway: a lot rejected locally has
already consumed one of the 20 rows the call returned.

    positional 2   -> lot_sub_status   {open|live|ended}
    --seller       -> seller_type      {insurance|dealer}
    --cylinders    -> cylinders[]      {1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12}
    --make/--model -> make/model
    --year-range   -> year_from/year_to
    --auction-date-range -> auction_date_from/auction_date_to

Every enum came from GET /vehicles/filters and was then verified against live
data by test/test_apibara_filters_01.py — worth doing, because a bad value fails
SILENTLY (`type=COUPE` returns 0 rows rather than an error). Raw evidence is in
test_run/apibara_filters_01.json.

NOT AVAILABLE, DELIBERATELY ABSENT
----------------------------------
body style   `type` looks like a body filter and /vehicles/filters advertises
             SEDAN/COUPE/SUV/..., but it matches the vehicle-CLASS field, which
             is "AUTOMOBILE" on every car: type=AUTOMOBILE returned 15/15 of a
             control set, type=COUPE returned 0/15 including the two lots whose
             body_style literally says "Coupe". Filter body style at the
             json2csv stage instead (IAAI populates it on 100% of records).
damage       `damage` is an INCLUDE-only whitelist whose enum (Fire/Hail/Theft/
             Water/Chemical/Rollover/Mechanical/Vandalized/Repossession) cannot
             express the collision damage that is ~80% of lots, and there is no
             negation param. Also a json2csv-stage concern.
seller       only insurance and dealer work. non_insurance is a no-op that
             returns everything; finance returns nothing. Neither is offered.
             The two that work are not complements — omit --seller for all.

Reads APIBARA_API_KEY from the repo-root .env. Writes to analytics/sold-data/.
"""
import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]          # repo root
ENV_PATH = ROOT / ".env"
OUT_DIR = ROOT / "analytics" / "sold-data"

BASE = "https://apibara.tech/api/v1/vehicle-auction"
RATE_DELAY = 1.5                                    # free plan = 1 req/sec

# Enums taken verbatim from GET /vehicles/filters — see the probe artifact
# test_run/apibara_filters_01.json. CLI choices are generated from these, so a
# value this script accepts is always a value the API accepts.
LOT_SUB_STATUS = {"open": "Open", "live": "Live", "ended": "Ended"}
CYLINDERS = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12}          # note: no 7, 9 or 11


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# env + transport
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def read_env_key(path=ENV_PATH, name="APIBARA_API_KEY"):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return ""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
                continue
            k, _, v = line.partition("=")
            if k.strip() == name:
                return v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return ""


def build_url(path, params):
    return f"{BASE}{path}?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True)


def get(api_key, path, params):
    req = urllib.request.Request(build_url(path, params), headers={
        "Accept": "application/json", "X-API-Key": api_key})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            return resp.getcode(), json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, {"error_body": e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return 0, {"error": str(e)}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def parse_year_range(s):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d{4})\s*(?:[-:]\s*(\d{4}))?\s*", s or "")
    if not m:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"--year-range wants YYYY-YYYY or YYYY, got {s!r}")
    lo = int(m.group(1))
    hi = int(m.group(2) or m.group(1))
    if hi < lo:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"--year-range {lo}-{hi} is backwards")
    return lo, hi


def parse_date(s):
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(s.strip())
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"dates must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {s!r}") from None


def build_arg_parser():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="pull_apibara_01.py",
        description="Pull raw Apibara auction JSON into analytics/sold-data/. "
                    "No filtering, no derived fields — see apibara_json2csv_*.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="Each page costs 1 call of the 100/month free plan. "
               "Use --dry-run to see the request without spending one.")
    ap.add_argument("platform", choices=["iaai", "copart"],
                    type=str.lower, help="auction platform")
    ap.add_argument("mode", choices=list(LOT_SUB_STATUS), type=str.lower,
                    help="lot_sub_status: open = biddable, live = auction "
                         "running now, ended = sold/finished")
    ap.add_argument("--make")
    ap.add_argument("--model")
    ap.add_argument("--year-range", type=parse_year_range, metavar="YYYY-YYYY")
    ap.add_argument("--auction-date-range", nargs="+", type=parse_date,
                    metavar="YYYY-MM-DD",
                    help="one date = today..that date; two = from..to")
    ap.add_argument("--seller", choices=["insurance", "dealer"], type=str.lower,
                    help="seller_type. Omit for all sellers; the two values "
                         "are not complements — see module docstring")
    ap.add_argument("--cylinders", action="append", default=[], metavar="N",
                    help=f"cylinders[]; repeatable or comma-separated. "
                         f"Allowed: {','.join(map(str, sorted(CYLINDERS)))}")
    ap.add_argument("--max-pages", type=int, default=1,
                    help="page cap; EACH PAGE IS ONE API CALL (default 1). "
                         "Paging stops early when the cursor runs out")
    ap.add_argument("--per-page", type=int, default=20,
                    help="lots per page, API max 20 (default 20)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="output basename or path (default: auto-named)")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                    help="print the resolved request, make no call")
    return ap


def resolve_params(args):
    """CLI args -> the exact query params sent to /vehicles."""
    params = {"platform": args.platform, "per_page": min(args.per_page, 20)}
    if args.make:
        params["make"] = args.make
    if args.model:
        params["model"] = args.model
    if args.year_range:
        params["year_from"], params["year_to"] = args.year_range
    params["lot_sub_status"] = LOT_SUB_STATUS[args.mode]
    if args.auction_date_range:
        d = args.auction_date_range
        if len(d) == 1:
            lo, hi = dt.date.today(), d[0]
        elif len(d) == 2:
            lo, hi = sorted(d)
        else:
            raise SystemExit("--auction-date-range takes one or two dates")
        params["auction_date_from"] = lo.isoformat()
        params["auction_date_to"] = hi.isoformat()

    cyl = set()
    for raw in args.cylinders:
        for tok in str(raw).split(","):
            tok = tok.strip()
            if not tok:
                continue
            if not tok.isdigit() or int(tok) not in CYLINDERS:
                raise SystemExit(
                    f"--cylinders must be one of "
                    f"{','.join(map(str, sorted(CYLINDERS)))}, got {tok!r}")
            cyl.add(int(tok))
    if cyl:
        params["cylinders[]"] = sorted(cyl)

    if args.seller:
        params["seller_type"] = args.seller
    return params


def default_basename(args, params):
    bits = ["apibara", args.platform, args.mode]
    bits += [str(x).lower().replace(" ", "-")
             for x in (args.make, args.model) if x]
    if args.year_range:
        bits.append(f"{args.year_range[0]}-{args.year_range[1]}")
    if "auction_date_from" in params:
        bits.append(f"{params['auction_date_from']}_{params['auction_date_to']}")
    bits.append(dt.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S"))
    return "_".join(bits)


def resolve_out_path(args, params):
    if args.out:
        p = Path(args.out)
        if not p.is_absolute():
            p = OUT_DIR / p
        return p.with_suffix(".json")
    return (OUT_DIR / default_basename(args, params)).with_suffix(".json")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def summarize(records):
    """Coverage report. The date span is the point: it shows how far back the
    archive actually reaches, which is shorter than most requested windows."""
    if not records:
        print("  no records returned")
        return
    days = sorted(filter(None, ((r.get("auction") or {}).get("last_sold_day")
                                or (r.get("ad") or "")[:10] for r in records)))
    sellers, damage = {}, {}
    for r in records:
        s = (r.get("seller") or {}).get("type") or "—"
        sellers[s] = sellers.get(s, 0) + 1
        dmg = (r.get("condition") or {}).get("primary_damage") or "—"
        damage[dmg] = damage.get(dmg, 0) + 1
    print(f"\n  records:      {len(records)}")
    if days:
        print(f"  date span:    {days[0]} .. {days[-1]}")
    print(f"  seller.type:  {dict(sorted(sellers.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))}")
    top = dict(sorted(damage.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:6])
    print(f"  top damage:   {top}")


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.max_pages < 1:
        raise SystemExit("--max-pages must be >= 1")

    params = resolve_params(args)
    out_path = resolve_out_path(args, params)

    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"{args.platform.upper()} — lot_sub_status={LOT_SUB_STATUS[args.mode]}")
    print(f"  server-side: {params}")
    print(f"  budget:      up to {args.max_pages} call(s)")
    print("=" * 78)

    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"\n  DRY RUN — no call made.\n  GET {build_url('/vehicles', params)}")
        print(f"  would write -> {out_path}")
        return 0

    api_key = read_env_key()
    if not api_key:
        raise SystemExit(f"No APIBARA_API_KEY found in {ENV_PATH}")

    out = {
        "generated_at": dt.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "argv": argv,
        "platform": args.platform,
        "mode": args.mode,
        "server_params": params,
        "pages": [],
    }
    calls, cursor, records = 0, None, []

    while calls < args.max_pages:
        page_params = dict(params)
        if cursor:
            page_params["cursor"] = cursor
        code, data = get(api_key, "/vehicles", page_params)
        calls += 1
        out["pages"].append({"status": code, "raw": data})
        if code != 200:
            print(f"\n  HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:400]}")
            break
        rows = data.get("data") or []
        records.extend(rows)
        cursor = (data.get("meta") or {}).get("next_cursor")
        print(f"  page {calls}: {len(rows)} lot(s)   (more pages: {bool(cursor)})")
        if not cursor:
            break
        time.sleep(RATE_DELAY)

    if cursor:
        print(f"\n  *** TRUNCATED: --max-pages {args.max_pages} reached with a "
              f"live cursor. Re-run with a higher cap to get the rest. ***")

    out["counts"] = {"records": len(records), "calls_used": calls,
                     "truncated": bool(cursor)}
    summarize(records)

    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(f"Done. {calls} API call(s) used.")
    print(f"  JSON -> {out_path}")
    print(f"  next: python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_{args.platform}"
          f"_01.py {out_path.name}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```
```
"""
Stage 2 of the analytics pipeline — IAAI raw JSON -> analysis-ready CSV.

    pull_apibara_01.py  ->  raw .json  ->  THIS SCRIPT  ->  .csv

Reads the archives written by pull_apibara_01.py, flattens each IAAI record into
one row, and applies whatever filtering you ask for. No network, no API calls —
run it as often as you like, with different filters, against the same archive.

    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py                # newest archive
    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py FILE.json ...  # specific ones
    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py --all          # every IAAI archive

    --exclude-damage water,flood,fire   drop lots whose damage matches (OFF by default)
    --include-damage front,rear         keep ONLY lots whose damage matches
    --body-style coupe                  keep only these (repeatable/comma-separated)
    --exclude-body-style coupe          drop these
    --seller-class insurance            keep only these seller classes
    --min-photos 8                      drop thin listings
    --sold-only                         drop lots with no realised sale price
    --schema                            print the column mapping table and exit

IAAI ONLY. A Copart converter will be a separate script, because the two payload
shapes are not variations of one schema — they are different schemas. Copart
records carry `details: None`, which removes ActualCashValue, EstimatedRepairCost,
body style, storage coordinates and the entire attributes block in one go. Nearly
half the columns below simply do not exist on a Copart lot, so a shared converter
would be mostly null-handling.

SELLER CLASSIFICATION — READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE COLUMN
------------------------------------------------------------
IAAI masks seller identity on a meaningful slice of lots. Observed on a 68-lot
insurance-filtered pull: 12 records came back with

    sale_information.SellerType = "******"    (literally asterisks)
    seller.name                 = "unknown"
    seller.type                 = "unknown"

...while `attributes.Origin` said "Insurance" and `attributes.ProviderType` said
"INS" on all 68. The masking hides WHICH carrier, not WHETHER it is a carrier.
Reading SellerType naively classifies those 12 as non-insurance, which is simply
wrong — every one of them came from a `seller_type=insurance` server-side query.

So `seller_class` cascades, most reliable source first, and records which source
decided in `seller_class_source`. `seller_name_masked` flags the anonymised ones
so they can be excluded from carrier-level analysis without being miscounted as
dealers.

IMAGE / VIDEO COLUMNS
---------------------
IAAI thumb URLs look like:

    https://vis.iaai.com/resizer?imageKeys=46139013~SID~I1&width=400&height=300
                                           ^^^^^^^^        ^
                                           SalvageId       image key

`iaai_image_url_prefix` keeps everything up to and including the trailing "I",
and `iaai_image_keys` collects the numeric suffixes as a pipe-joined array
(1|2|...|115|116) — the keys are NOT contiguous, they jump from ~11 to ~115, so
they cannot be regenerated from a count and must be stored. Rebuild any URL as:

    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=845&height=633"      # large
    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=400&height=300"      # thumb

Note the image key is `attributes.SalvageId`, which is NOT the lot number
(lot 45640490 -> SalvageId 46139013). Do not build image URLs from lot_number.

vr360 is deliberately absent from the CSV — it carries no analytic signal and
one fixed URL shape per lot. It remains in the raw JSON if ever needed.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
IN_DIR = ROOT / "analytics" / "sold-data"

ARRAY_SEP = "|"          # pipe, so the CSV stays readable without nested quoting

# Insurance-carrier name fragments, used only as the LAST resort in the seller
# cascade (attributes.Origin and ProviderType are checked first).
_INSURER_NEEDLES = [
    "insurance", "insur", "casualty", "assurance", "indemnity", "underwrit",
    "mutual", "geico", "usaa", "state farm", "progressive", "allstate",
    "farmers", "nationwide", "esurance", "safeco", "travelers", "hartford",
    "amica", "erie", "aaa ", "auto club", "root ", "lemonade", "mapfre",
    "mercury", "arbella", "bluefire",
]

# A value IAAI redacted rather than omitted. Treated as "present but hidden",
# never as a real value.
_MASKED = re.compile(r"^\*+$")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# accessors — every one tolerates a missing/None parent block
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def g(d, *path, default=None):
    """Nested get: g(rec, 'details', 'attributes', 'Origin')."""
    cur = d
    for k in path:
        if not isinstance(cur, dict):
            return default
        cur = cur.get(k)
    return default if cur is None else cur


def attrs(v):
    return g(v, "details", "attributes", default={}) or {}


def sale_info(v):
    return g(v, "details", "sale_information", default={}) or {}


def veh_desc(v):
    return g(v, "details", "vehicle_description", default={}) or {}


def is_masked(x):
    return bool(_MASKED.match(str(x or "").strip()))


def clean(x):
    """Normalise API sentinels to None: '', 'unknown', 'None', '******'."""
    s = str(x).strip() if x is not None else ""
    if not s or s.lower() in ("unknown", "none", "n/a") or is_masked(s):
        return None
    return x


def money_num(v):
    """'$29,240 USD' / 29240 / '' -> 29240.0 / None."""
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return float(v) or None
    m = re.search(r"-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?", str(v or ""))
    return float(m.group(0).replace(",", "")) if m else None


def as_bool(x):
    if isinstance(x, bool):
        return x
    s = str(x or "").strip().lower()
    return True if s == "true" else False if s == "false" else None


def ratio(num, den):
    return round(num / den, 4) if num and den else None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derived: seller
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def seller_class(v):
    """-> (class, source). class in {insurance, dealer, other, unknown}.

    Ordered by how much the field can be trusted. attributes.Origin /
    ProviderType survive IAAI's seller masking; SellerType and seller.name do
    not (see module docstring).
    """
    origin = str(g(v, "details", "attributes", "Origin", default="") or "").lower()
    ptype = str(g(v, "details", "attributes", "ProviderType", default="") or "").lower()
    if "ins" in ptype or "insurance" in origin:
        return "insurance", "attributes.Origin/ProviderType"
    if origin in ("dealer", "dealership"):
        return "dealer", "attributes.Origin"

    stype = str(g(v, "seller", "type", default="") or "").strip().lower()
    if stype == "insurance":
        return "insurance", "seller.type"
    if stype in ("non_insurance", "non-insurance", "dealer"):
        return "dealer", "seller.type"

    itype = str(sale_info(v).get("SellerType") or "").strip()
    if itype and not is_masked(itype):
        return (("insurance", "sale_information.SellerType")
                if "insur" in itype.lower()
                else ("dealer", "sale_information.SellerType"))

    name = str(clean(g(v, "seller", "name")) or clean(sale_info(v).get("Seller"))
               or "").lower()
    if not name:
        return "unknown", "none"
    if any(n in name for n in _INSURER_NEEDLES):
        return "insurance", "seller.name"
    return "other", "seller.name~inferred"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derived: media
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
_IMG_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<prefix>.*imageKeys=[^&]*?~SID~I)(?P<key>\d+)")


def image_fields(v):
    """-> (prefix, [keys], count). See module docstring for the URL anatomy."""
    thumbs = g(v, "media", "thumbs", default=[]) or []
    prefix, keys = None, []
    for url in thumbs:
        m = _IMG_RE.match(str(url))
        if not m:
            continue
        prefix = prefix or m.group("prefix")
        keys.append(int(m.group("key")))
    return prefix, keys, len(thumbs)


def video_fields(v):
    """-> (count, first_url). vr360 items are ignored on purpose."""
    items = g(v, "media", "items", default=[]) or []
    urls = [it.get("url") for it in items
            if isinstance(it, dict) and it.get("type") == "video" and it.get("url")]
    return len(urls), (urls[0] if urls else None)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE SCHEMA — single source of truth for the CSV
#   (column, source, kind)   kind: "raw" = copied as-is, "calc" = derived here
# Adding a column means adding one line here and nothing else.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEMA = [
    # --- identity -------------------------------------------------------
    ("platform",            lambda v: v.get("platform"),                      "raw"),
    ("lot_number",          lambda v: v.get("lot_number"),                    "raw"),
    ("salvage_id",          lambda v: attrs(v).get("SalvageId"),              "raw"),
    ("vin",                 lambda v: v.get("vin"),                           "raw"),
    ("year",                lambda v: v.get("year"),                          "raw"),
    ("make",                lambda v: v.get("make"),                          "raw"),
    ("model",               lambda v: v.get("model"),                         "raw"),
    ("series",              lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("Series")),          "raw"),
    ("title_desc",          lambda v: v.get("title"),                         "raw"),
    ("lot_url",             lambda v: f"https://www.iaai.com/VehicleDetail/{v.get('lot_number')}"
                            if v.get("lot_number") else None,                 "calc"),

    # --- body / specs ---------------------------------------------------
    ("body_style",          lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "body_style"),    "raw"),
    ("body_style_name",     lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("BodyStyleName")),   "raw"),
    ("vehicle_class",       lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("VehicleClass")),    "raw"),
    ("engine_raw",          lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "engine", "raw"), "raw"),
    ("engine_size_l",       lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "engine", "size_l"), "raw"),
    ("engine_hp",           lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "engine", "hp"),  "raw"),
    ("engine_layout",       lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "engine", "layout"), "raw"),
    ("cylinders",           lambda v: attrs(v).get("Cylinders"),              "raw"),
    ("displacement_ci",     lambda v: attrs(v).get("CubicInchDisplacement"),  "raw"),
    ("transmission",        lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "transmission"),  "raw"),
    ("drive_type",          lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "drive_type"),    "raw"),
    ("fuel_type",           lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "fuel_type"),     "raw"),
    ("exterior_color",      lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "exterior_color"), "raw"),
    ("interior_color",      lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("InteriorColor")),   "raw"),
    ("wheel_type",          lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("WheelType")),       "raw"),
    ("options",             lambda v: clean(veh_desc(v).get("Options")),      "raw"),
    ("country_of_origin",   lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("CountryOfOrigin")), "raw"),

    # --- condition ------------------------------------------------------
    ("primary_damage",      lambda v: g(v, "condition", "primary_damage"),    "raw"),
    ("secondary_damage",    lambda v: g(v, "condition", "secondary_damage"),  "raw"),
    ("primary_damage_code", lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("PrimaryDamageCode")), "raw"),
    ("secondary_damage_code", lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("SecondaryDamageCode")), "raw"),
    ("loss_type",           lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("LossTypeDesc")),    "raw"),
    ("run_condition",       lambda v: g(v, "condition", "run_condition", "value"), "raw"),
    ("runs_and_drives",     lambda v: as_bool(attrs(v).get("RunAndDrive")),   "calc"),
    ("start_code",          lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("StartsDesc")),      "raw"),
    ("has_key",             lambda v: g(v, "condition", "has_key"),           "raw"),
    ("key_fob",             lambda v: as_bool(attrs(v).get("KeyFOB")),        "raw"),
    ("airbags",             lambda v: g(v, "vehicle_specs", "airbags"),       "raw"),
    ("vehicle_condition",   lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("VehicleCondition")), "raw"),
    ("vehicle_grade",       lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("VehicleGrade")),    "raw"),
    ("odometer_mi",         lambda v: g(v, "odometer", "mi"),                 "raw"),
    ("odometer_brand",      lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("ODOBrand")),        "raw"),

    # --- title / documents ----------------------------------------------
    ("sale_document",       lambda v: g(v, "sale_document", "name"),          "raw"),
    ("sale_document_group", lambda v: g(v, "sale_document", "sale_document_group"), "raw"),
    ("title_code",          lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("TitleCode")),       "raw"),
    ("title_brand",         lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("TitleBrand")),      "raw"),
    ("title_state",         lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("TitleState")),      "raw"),
    ("title_notes",         lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("TitleNotes")),      "raw"),
    ("export_ok",           lambda v: g(v, "sale_document", "export"),        "raw"),

    # --- money ----------------------------------------------------------
    ("last_sold_price_usd", lambda v: money_num(g(v, "pricing", "last_sold_price_usd")), "calc"),
    ("current_bid_usd",     lambda v: money_num(g(v, "pricing", "current_bid_usd")), "calc"),
    ("buy_now_usd",         lambda v: money_num(g(v, "pricing", "buy_now_usd")), "calc"),
    ("min_bid_usd",         lambda v: money_num(attrs(v).get("MinimumBidAmount")), "calc"),
    ("bid_increment_usd",   lambda v: money_num(g(v, "details", "bid_increment")), "calc"),
    ("acv_usd",             lambda v: money_num(sale_info(v).get("ActualCashValue")), "calc"),
    ("acv_raw",             lambda v: sale_info(v).get("ActualCashValue"),    "raw"),
    ("est_repair_usd",      lambda v: money_num(attrs(v).get("EstRepairCost")
                                                or sale_info(v).get("EstimatedRepairCost")), "calc"),
    ("est_repair_raw",      lambda v: sale_info(v).get("EstimatedRepairCost"), "raw"),
    ("est_cost_from_usd",   lambda v: g(v, "pricing", "estimated_cost", "from"), "raw"),
    ("est_cost_to_usd",     lambda v: g(v, "pricing", "estimated_cost", "to"), "raw"),
    ("repair_to_acv",       lambda v: ratio(money_num(attrs(v).get("EstRepairCost")),
                                            money_num(sale_info(v).get("ActualCashValue"))), "calc"),
    ("sold_to_acv",         lambda v: ratio(money_num(g(v, "pricing", "last_sold_price_usd")),
                                            money_num(sale_info(v).get("ActualCashValue"))), "calc"),

    # --- auction --------------------------------------------------------
    ("auction_state",       lambda v: g(v, "auction", "state"),               "raw"),
    ("auction_at",          lambda v: g(v, "auction", "auction_at") or v.get("ad"), "raw"),
    ("last_sold_day",       lambda v: g(v, "auction", "last_sold_day"),       "raw"),
    ("last_sold_status",    lambda v: g(v, "auction", "last_sold_status"),    "raw"),
    ("sold_buy_now",        lambda v: g(v, "auction", "sold_buy_now"),        "raw"),
    ("lane",                lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("Lane")),            "raw"),
    ("slot",                lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("Slot")),            "raw"),

    # --- seller ---------------------------------------------------------
    ("seller_name",         lambda v: clean(g(v, "seller", "name"))
                            or clean(sale_info(v).get("Seller")),             "raw"),
    ("seller_provider_name", lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("ProviderName")),   "raw"),
    ("seller_provider_group", lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("ProviderGroup")), "raw"),
    ("seller_origin",       lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("Origin")),          "raw"),
    ("seller_provider_type", lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("ProviderType")),   "raw"),
    ("seller_type_raw",     lambda v: g(v, "seller", "type"),                 "raw"),
    ("seller_type_iaai",    lambda v: sale_info(v).get("SellerType"),         "raw"),
    ("seller_name_masked",  lambda v: is_masked(sale_info(v).get("SellerType"))
                            or not clean(g(v, "seller", "name")),             "calc"),
    ("seller_class",        lambda v: seller_class(v)[0],                     "calc"),
    ("seller_class_source", lambda v: seller_class(v)[1],                     "calc"),

    # --- location -------------------------------------------------------
    ("selling_branch",      lambda v: sale_info(v).get("SellingBranch"),      "raw"),
    ("branch_number",       lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("BranchNumber")),    "raw"),
    ("branch_city",         lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("City")),            "raw"),
    ("branch_state",        lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("BranchState")),     "raw"),
    ("branch_zip",          lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("Zip")),             "raw"),
    ("branch_lat",          lambda v: attrs(v).get("StorageLocationLatitude"), "raw"),
    ("branch_lng",          lambda v: attrs(v).get("StorageLocationLongitude"), "raw"),
    ("location_display",    lambda v: g(v, "location", "display"),            "raw"),

    # --- media ----------------------------------------------------------
    ("image_count",         lambda v: image_fields(v)[2],                     "calc"),
    ("iaai_image_url_prefix", lambda v: image_fields(v)[0],                   "calc"),
    ("iaai_image_keys",     lambda v: ARRAY_SEP.join(str(k) for k in image_fields(v)[1])
                            or None,                                          "calc"),
    ("video_count",         lambda v: video_fields(v)[0],                     "calc"),
    ("iaai_video_url",      lambda v: video_fields(v)[1],                     "calc"),

    # --- provenance -----------------------------------------------------
    ("source_file",         lambda v: v.get("_source_file"),                  "calc"),
    ("pulled_at",           lambda v: v.get("_pulled_at"),                    "calc"),
]

COLUMNS = [c for c, _, _ in SCHEMA]


def flatten(v):
    return {col: fn(v) for col, fn, _ in SCHEMA}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# filtering
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def damage_text(v):
    c = v.get("condition") or {}
    return f"{c.get('primary_damage') or ''} {c.get('secondary_damage') or ''}".lower()


def norm_style(s):
    return re.sub(r"[\s_-]+", "/", str(s or "").strip().lower())


def keep(v, f):
    """-> (bool, reason). All filters are opt-in; default keeps everything."""
    if f["exclude_damage"]:
        hit = next((n for n in f["exclude_damage"] if n in damage_text(v)), None)
        if hit:
            return False, f"damage~{hit}"
    if f["include_damage"]:
        if not any(n in damage_text(v) for n in f["include_damage"]):
            return False, f"damage!~{'/'.join(f['include_damage'])}"

    if f["body_styles"] or f["exclude_body_styles"]:
        bs = norm_style(g(v, "vehicle_specs", "body_style"))
        if f["body_styles"] and bs not in f["body_styles"]:
            return False, f"body_style={bs or 'null'}"
        if bs in f["exclude_body_styles"]:
            return False, f"body_style={bs} excluded"

    if f["seller_classes"] and seller_class(v)[0] not in f["seller_classes"]:
        return False, f"seller_class={seller_class(v)[0]}"

    if f["min_photos"] and (g(v, "media", "thumbs_count") or 0) < f["min_photos"]:
        return False, f"photos={g(v, 'media', 'thumbs_count') or 0}"

    if f["sold_only"] and not money_num(g(v, "pricing", "last_sold_price_usd")):
        return False, "no sold price"

    return True, ""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# input
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_records(paths):
    """-> [record], each tagged with its provenance."""
    out = []
    for p in paths:
        doc = json.loads(Path(p).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        plat = doc.get("platform")
        if plat and plat != "iaai":
            print(f"  !! skipping {Path(p).name}: platform={plat}, this "
                  f"converter is IAAI-only")
            continue
        pulled = doc.get("generated_at")
        n = 0
        for page in doc.get("pages", []):
            if page.get("status") != 200:
                continue
            for rec in (page.get("raw", {}).get("data") or []):
                rec["_source_file"] = Path(p).name
                rec["_pulled_at"] = pulled
                out.append(rec)
                n += 1
        print(f"  loaded {n:>4} record(s) from {Path(p).name}")
    return out


def resolve_inputs(args):
    if args.files:
        return [Path(f) if Path(f).is_absolute() else IN_DIR / f
                for f in args.files]
    pool = sorted(IN_DIR.glob("*iaai*.json"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
    if not pool:
        raise SystemExit(f"no IAAI archives found in {IN_DIR} — run "
                         f"pull_apibara_01.py first")
    return pool if args.all else [pool[-1]]


def print_schema():
    print(f"{'csv column':<24} {'kind':<5} source")
    print("-" * 100)
    src = {c: (fn, k) for c, fn, k in SCHEMA}
    for col, fn, kind in SCHEMA:
        code = fn.__code__
        try:
            line = code.co_consts, None
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            line = None
        print(f"{col:<24} {kind:<5} {_source_hint(col)}")
    print(f"\n{len(COLUMNS)} columns.  raw = copied from JSON as-is, "
          f"calc = derived by this script.")
    print("Full field-by-field mapping: analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md")


def _source_hint(col):
    """Human-readable JSON path per column, kept next to the schema doc."""
    return SOURCE_HINTS.get(col, "")


# JSON path per column, for --schema and the docs. Kept in one place so the
# markdown table and the CLI never drift apart.
SOURCE_HINTS = {
    "platform": "platform", "lot_number": "lot_number",
    "salvage_id": "details.attributes.SalvageId  (image key, != lot_number)",
    "vin": "vin", "year": "year", "make": "make", "model": "model",
    "series": "details.attributes.Series", "title_desc": "title",
    "lot_url": "built from lot_number",
    "body_style": "vehicle_specs.body_style",
    "body_style_name": "details.attributes.BodyStyleName",
    "vehicle_class": "details.attributes.VehicleClass",
    "engine_raw": "vehicle_specs.engine.raw",
    "engine_size_l": "vehicle_specs.engine.size_l",
    "engine_hp": "vehicle_specs.engine.hp",
    "engine_layout": "vehicle_specs.engine.layout",
    "cylinders": "details.attributes.Cylinders",
    "displacement_ci": "details.attributes.CubicInchDisplacement",
    "transmission": "vehicle_specs.transmission",
    "drive_type": "vehicle_specs.drive_type",
    "fuel_type": "vehicle_specs.fuel_type",
    "exterior_color": "vehicle_specs.exterior_color",
    "interior_color": "details.attributes.InteriorColor",
    "wheel_type": "details.attributes.WheelType",
    "options": "details.vehicle_description.Options",
    "country_of_origin": "details.attributes.CountryOfOrigin",
    "primary_damage": "condition.primary_damage",
    "secondary_damage": "condition.secondary_damage",
    "primary_damage_code": "details.attributes.PrimaryDamageCode",
    "secondary_damage_code": "details.attributes.SecondaryDamageCode",
    "loss_type": "details.attributes.LossTypeDesc",
    "run_condition": "condition.run_condition.value",
    "runs_and_drives": "details.attributes.RunAndDrive -> bool",
    "start_code": "details.attributes.StartsDesc",
    "has_key": "condition.has_key", "key_fob": "details.attributes.KeyFOB",
    "airbags": "vehicle_specs.airbags",
    "vehicle_condition": "details.attributes.VehicleCondition",
    "vehicle_grade": "details.attributes.VehicleGrade",
    "odometer_mi": "odometer.mi", "odometer_brand": "details.attributes.ODOBrand",
    "sale_document": "sale_document.name",
    "sale_document_group": "sale_document.sale_document_group",
    "title_code": "details.attributes.TitleCode",
    "title_brand": "details.attributes.TitleBrand",
    "title_state": "details.attributes.TitleState",
    "title_notes": "details.attributes.TitleNotes",
    "export_ok": "sale_document.export",
    "last_sold_price_usd": "pricing.last_sold_price_usd -> number",
    "current_bid_usd": "pricing.current_bid_usd -> number",
    "buy_now_usd": "pricing.buy_now_usd -> number",
    "min_bid_usd": "details.attributes.MinimumBidAmount -> number",
    "bid_increment_usd": "details.bid_increment -> number",
    "acv_usd": "details.sale_information.ActualCashValue -> number",
    "acv_raw": "details.sale_information.ActualCashValue (text)",
    "est_repair_usd": "details.attributes.EstRepairCost (fallback sale_information) -> number",
    "est_repair_raw": "details.sale_information.EstimatedRepairCost (text)",
    "est_cost_from_usd": "pricing.estimated_cost.from",
    "est_cost_to_usd": "pricing.estimated_cost.to",
    "repair_to_acv": "est_repair_usd / acv_usd",
    "sold_to_acv": "last_sold_price_usd / acv_usd",
    "auction_state": "auction.state",

    "last_sold_day": "auction.last_sold_day",
    "last_sold_status": "auction.last_sold_status",
    "sold_buy_now": "auction.sold_buy_now",
    "lane": "details.attributes.Lane", "slot": "details.attributes.Slot",
    "seller_name": "seller.name (fallback sale_information.Seller)",
    "seller_provider_name": "details.attributes.ProviderName",
    "seller_provider_group": "details.attributes.ProviderGroup",
    "seller_origin": "details.attributes.Origin",
    "seller_provider_type": "details.attributes.ProviderType",
    "seller_type_raw": "seller.type",
    "seller_type_iaai": "details.sale_information.SellerType (may be '******')",
    "seller_name_masked": "true when SellerType is masked or name is 'unknown'",
    "seller_class": "cascade: Origin/ProviderType > seller.type > SellerType > name",
    "seller_class_source": "which field decided seller_class",
    "selling_branch": "details.sale_information.SellingBranch",

    "video_count": "count of media.items[type=video]",
    "iaai_video_url": "first media.items[type=video].url",
    "source_file": "archive filename this row came from",
    "pulled_at": "archive generated_at",
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_arg_parser():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py",
        description="Flatten IAAI Apibara archives into an analysis CSV. "
                    "Offline — no API calls.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="*",
                    help="archive .json files (default: newest IAAI archive)")
    ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                    help="use every IAAI archive in analytics/sold-data/")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-damage", metavar="a,b,c",
                    help="drop lots whose primary/secondary damage contains any "
                         "of these (case-insensitive substrings)")
    ap.add_argument("--include-damage", metavar="a,b,c",
                    help="keep ONLY lots whose damage contains one of these")
    ap.add_argument("--body-style", action="append", default=[], metavar="STYLE",
                    help="keep only these body styles (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-body-style", action="append", default=[],
                    metavar="STYLE", help="drop these body styles (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--seller-class", action="append", default=[],
                    choices=["insurance", "dealer", "other", "unknown"],
                    help="keep only these seller classes (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--min-photos", type=int, default=0,
                    help="drop lots with fewer thumbnails than this")
    ap.add_argument("--sold-only", action="store_true",
                    help="drop lots with no realised sale price")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="output .csv path (default: alongside input)")
    ap.add_argument("--schema", action="store_true",
                    help="print the column mapping table and exit")
    return ap


def csv_list(s):
    return [x.strip().lower() for x in (s or "").split(",") if x.strip()]


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)

    if args.schema:
        print_schema()
        return 0

    paths = resolve_inputs(args)
    print("=" * 78)
    print("IAAI raw JSON -> CSV")
    print("=" * 78)
    records = load_records(paths)
    if not records:
        raise SystemExit("no IAAI records found in the given archive(s)")

    filters = {
        "exclude_damage": csv_list(args.exclude_damage),
        "include_damage": csv_list(args.include_damage),
        "body_styles": {norm_style(x) for raw in args.body_style
                        for x in str(raw).split(",") if x.strip()},
        "exclude_body_styles": {norm_style(x) for raw in args.exclude_body_style
                                for x in str(raw).split(",") if x.strip()},
        "seller_classes": set(args.seller_class),
        "min_photos": args.min_photos,
        "sold_only": args.sold_only,
    }
    active = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if v}
    print(f"\n  filters: {active or 'none (keeping every record)'}")

    # de-dupe across archives: the same lot can appear in overlapping pulls
    seen, kept, dropped, dupes = set(), [], [], 0
    for v in records:
        key = (v.get("platform"), v.get("lot_number"), v.get("vin"))
        if key in seen:
            dupes += 1
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        ok, why = keep(v, filters)
        (kept if ok else dropped).append((v, why))

    print(f"  unique lots: {len(seen)}   (dropped {dupes} duplicate row(s) "
          f"across archives)")
    print(f"  kept {len(kept)}   filtered out {len(dropped)}")
    if dropped:
        reasons = {}
        for _, why in dropped:
            reasons[why] = reasons.get(why, 0) + 1
        for why, n in sorted(reasons.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            print(f"      {n:>4}  {why}")

    rows = [flatten(v) for v, _ in kept]

    # seller audit — the column most likely to be wrong, so show the evidence
    audit = {}
    for r in rows:
        k = (r["seller_class"], r["seller_class_source"], r["seller_origin"],
             r["seller_type_iaai"], r["seller_name"])
        audit[k] = audit.get(k, 0) + 1
    print("\n  --- seller classification audit ---")
    print(f"      {'n':>4}  {'class':<10} {'origin':<10} {'SellerType':<12} "
          f"{'source':<34} name")
    for (cls, src, origin, styp, name), n in sorted(audit.items(),
                                                    key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:15]:
        print(f"      {n:>4}  {cls:<10} {str(origin or '—'):<10} "
              f"{str(styp or '—'):<12} {src:<34} {name or '—'}")

    out_path = (Path(args.out) if args.out
                else paths[-1].with_name(paths[-1].stem + "_iaai.csv"))
    if not out_path.is_absolute():
        out_path = IN_DIR / out_path
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=COLUMNS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(f"Done. {len(rows)} row(s) x {len(COLUMNS)} column(s)")
    print(f"  CSV -> {out_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

````bash
{ cat <<'HEAD'
# IAAI CSV schema — Apibara raw JSON → analysis CSV

Produced by [`analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py`](../scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py)
from archives written by [`pull_apibara_01.py`](../scripts/pull_apibara_01.py).
Run `python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py --schema` to print the
same mapping from the code itself — the script's `SCHEMA` list is the single
source of truth, and this document is generated from it.

**IAAI ONLY.** Copart gets its own schema and its own converter. This is not
tidiness — Copart records carry `details: None`, which deletes `ActualCashValue`,
`EstimatedRepairCost`, body style, storage coordinates and the whole `attributes`
block at once. Roughly half the columns below cannot exist on a Copart lot.

## Reading the table

- **kind = `raw`** — copied out of the JSON unchanged (only `None`/`""`/`"unknown"`/
  `"******"` normalised to empty).
- **kind = `calc`** — computed by the converter: parsed numbers, ratios,
  classifications, media decomposition.
- **filled** — coverage on the reference pull (68 IAAI Audi S5 lots,
  `apibara_iaai_ended_audi_s5_2018-2023_2025-08-01_2026-08-09`). A low number
  means the field is genuinely sparse in IAAI's data, not that mapping is broken.

## Three things that will bite you

**1. `salvage_id` is the image key, and it is NOT `lot_number`.**
Lot `45640490` has `SalvageId` `46139013`. Build image URLs from `salvage_id`
(or better, from `iaai_image_url_prefix`), never from the lot number.

**2. Image keys are not contiguous.** A 16-photo lot has keys
`1|2|…|11|115|116|117|118|119` — they jump. They cannot be regenerated from
`image_count`, which is why the full array is stored. Rebuild a URL as:

```
{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=845&height=633    # large
{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=400&height=300    # thumb
```

**3. IAAI masks seller identity on some lots — `SellerType` comes back as
`******`.** On the reference pull that was 12 of 68. Those records also have
`seller.name = "unknown"` and `seller.type = "unknown"`, while
`attributes.Origin = "Insurance"` and `attributes.ProviderType = "INS"`. The
masking hides *which* carrier, not *whether* it is one. Classifying from
`SellerType` alone puts those 12 in the wrong bucket — they were all returned by
a `seller_type=insurance` server-side query. Hence `seller_class` reads
`Origin`/`ProviderType` first, and `seller_name_masked` flags them so they can be
excluded from carrier-level analysis without being miscounted as dealers.

## Deliberately excluded

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `media.items[type=vr360]` | One fixed URL shape per lot, no analytic signal. Stays in the raw JSON. |
| `media.has_360` | Same. |
| `details.auction_information.prebidInformation.*` | Session/UI state — login errors, popup text, "you are not logged in". Reflects the API client, not the vehicle. |
| `details.attributes.Synonyms`, `EmailTextForShare`, `LocationHours`, `PickupInstructions` | Marketing/branch boilerplate, identical across lots. |
| `$id`, `$values` | .NET serialiser artifacts. |

Nothing is lost by exclusion: the raw archive keeps every field, so a new column
is one line in `SCHEMA` plus a re-run — no API calls.

## Columns
HEAD
cat /tmp/claude-1000/-home-striker-projects-car-bid-tracker/1de5f512-27cc-4a6f-a0ee-152360548399/scratchpad/schema_body.md
cat <<'FOOT'

## Copart differences (for the future `apibara_json2csv_copart_01.py`)

Measured on a 20-lot Copart pull:

| Column group | IAAI | Copart |
|---|---|---|
| `details` block entirely | present | **`None` on 20/20** |
| `acv_usd`, `est_repair_usd` | 68/68 | **absent** — no ACV, no repair estimate |
| `body_style` | 68/68 | **0/20** — null on every record |
| `branch_lat` / `branch_lng` | 68/68 | absent (use `facility.*`, sparse) |
| `seller_type_raw` | `insurance` / `unknown` | `insurance` / `non_insurance` / `unknown` — cleaner |
| `engine_raw` | `"3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo, 354HP"` | `"3.0L 6"` — no layout, no HP |
| damage vocabulary | positional (`Left rear`, `Front & rear`) | coarse (`Rear end`, `Side`, `All over`) |

The practical consequence: **IAAI lots are self-pricing and Copart lots are not.**
`acv_usd` is the insurer's own clean-value figure and `est_repair_usd` its repair
estimate, so an IAAI row carries everything the max-bid calculation needs without
a MarketCheck call. A Copart row needs an external clean value.
FOOT
} > analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md && wc -l analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md && head -20 analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md
````

Done — all six changes, verified against your real 68-lot archive.

## The ~6-month wall: real, and no pull request gets around it

Your read is right, and it's slightly worse than 6 months. Requested 374 days, got **163** — oldest lot `2026-02-24`, and the monthly histogram shows a hard floor, not a fading tail (Feb: 3, Mar: 21, Apr: 13 … Aug: 3).

Apibara's own docs are explicit: *"As of 2026-07-27, the active database generally contains approximately **10 months** of collected records, while coverage for an individual VIN or lot can be shorter, longer or unavailable."* Coverage varies by "VIN, Lot, Auction source, Vehicle category, Collection date, Retention and migration status." Your Audi S5 slice landed at ~5.5 of that nominal ~10.

**No different endpoint or parameter reaches further back.** `/vehicles/{vin}/history` returns prior runs for a VIN you already know, one call each — useful for enrichment, useless for backfill. There's no archive param, and the docs' own remedy is to *"contact Apibara.tech"* for "multi-year data requirements or custom historical access." No plan tier is documented as changing this, so upgrading from the free tier buys you call volume, not history depth.

Two consequences worth acting on:

1. **Your archive is now the long-term asset, not their database.** The window rolls forward; the Feb–Aug 2026 lots you just pulled will age out of Apibara but stay in your JSON. Running this pull on a schedule (monthly, ~9 calls) accumulates multi-year history that you cannot otherwise buy. That's exactly why I made stage 1 archive raw and unfiltered.
2. If you need multi-year *now*, it's a different vendor: [apiauctions.io](https://apiauctions.io/copart-iaai) claims data since 2020, [auction-api.app](https://auction-api.app/en/) claims 3 years, [vehicledatabases.com](https://vehicledatabases.com/api/auction-history) sells auction history by VIN. I haven't verified any of those claims.

I found no Reddit discussion of Apibara specifically — it's a small vendor with little community footprint.

## A real bug the new schema exposed

Your terminal output had **12 lots classified `dealer`** in a query that was `seller_type=insurance` server-side. That was my classifier's fault: IAAI **masks seller identity** on some lots, returning `SellerType = "******"` with `seller.name = "unknown"`, and I read a non-insurance string as "dealer."

But `attributes.Origin = "Insurance"` and `attributes.ProviderType = "INS"` on **68/68**. The masking hides *which* carrier, not *whether* it's one. `seller_class` now reads `Origin`/`ProviderType` first — all 68 classify as insurance, and `seller_name_masked` flags the anonymised ones so they can be dropped from carrier-level analysis without being miscounted.

## The changes

**i + iii) `pull_apibara_01.py` is now raw-JSON-only** — no damage filter, no CSV, no derived fields. Given that lots age out permanently, a filter at pull time destroys data; a filter at convert time costs nothing. It also now warns when `--max-pages` truncates with a live cursor, and prints the date span so the retention wall is visible on every run.

**ii) Schema + mapping table:** [analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) — **94 columns, 73 raw / 21 calculated**, every one with its JSON path and real coverage (`68/68`, `46/68`, …). Generated from the script's `SCHEMA` list, so `--schema` and the doc can't drift. It documents what's excluded and why, and closes with a Copart-differences table for the future converter.

**iv) [apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py](analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py)** — offline, re-runnable, all filters opt-in: `--exclude-damage`, `--include-damage`, `--body-style`, `--exclude-body-style`, `--seller-class`, `--min-photos`, `--sold-only`. It de-dupes across archives by (platform, lot, VIN), so overlapping monthly pulls merge cleanly with `--all`. Verified: `--exclude-body-style coupe --exclude-damage water,flood,burn,fire,rollover --sold-only` → 45 kept, with a per-reason breakdown (19 coupe, 2 no-sale, 1 rollover, 1 burn).

**v) Image columns** — `iaai_image_url_prefix` (`…imageKeys=46139013~SID~I`) + `iaai_image_keys` (`1|2|…|11|115|116|117|118|119`) + `image_count`. I round-tripped all 68 rows: **0 mismatches** rebuilding every original URL. Two traps now documented: the key is `SalvageId` (`46139013`), **not** the lot number (`45640490`); and the keys are non-contiguous, so they can't be regenerated from a count.

**vi) Video columns** — `video_count` + `iaai_video_url` (45 of 68 have one). `vr360` and `has_360` are absent from the CSV, retained in the JSON.

One housekeeping note: `analytics/sold-data/..._20260810T120049.csv` (32KB) is the stale 45-column output from the old code path. The new one is `..._20260810T120049_iaai.csv` (94 columns). Say the word and I'll delete the stale one — I left your data alone.

*new_string*
```
def summarize(records):
    """Coverage report. The date span is the point: it shows how far back the
    archive actually reaches, which is shorter than most requested windows."""
    if not records:
        print("  no records returned")
        return
    days = sorted(filter(None, ((r.get("auction") or {}).get("last_sold_day")
                                or (r.get("ad") or "")[:10] for r in records)))
    sellers, origins, damage = {}, {}, {}
    for r in records:
        s = (r.get("seller") or {}).get("type") or "—"
        sellers[s] = sellers.get(s, 0) + 1
        o = ((r.get("details") or {}).get("attributes") or {}).get("Origin") or "—"
        origins[o] = origins.get(o, 0) + 1
        dmg = (r.get("condition") or {}).get("primary_damage") or "—"
        damage[dmg] = damage.get(dmg, 0) + 1

    print(f"\n  records:      {len(records)}")
    if days:
        print(f"  date span:    {days[0]} .. {days[-1]}")
    print(f"  seller.type:  {dict(sorted(sellers.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))}")
    if origins != {"—": len(records)}:
        print(f"  seller Origin:{dict(sorted(origins.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))}"
              f"   <- IAAI's own field; trust this one")
    # seller.type is Apibara's normalisation and it under-reports: it says
    # "unknown" for lots IAAI itself labels Insurance (26% of one observed
    # pull). Flag the gap here so it never again looks like the server-side
    # seller_type filter leaked non-insurance lots.
    unknown = sellers.get("unknown", 0)
    if unknown and origins.get("Insurance"):
        print(f"  note: {unknown} lot(s) have seller.type='unknown' but "
              f"Origin='Insurance' — Apibara's field is incomplete, not the "
              f"filter. json2csv resolves this into seller_class.")
    top = dict(sorted(damage.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:6])
    print(f"  top damage:   {top}")
```

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Edit**: /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker/analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py</summary>

*old_string*
```
    # de-dupe across archives: the same lot can appear in overlapping pulls
    seen, kept, dropped, dupes = set(), [], [], 0
    for v in records:
        key = (v.get("platform"), v.get("lot_number"), v.get("vin"))
        if key in seen:
            dupes += 1
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        ok, why = keep(v, filters)
        (kept if ok else dropped).append((v, why))
```
*new_string*
```
    # De-dupe across archives: overlapping pulls repeat lots (two pulls a day
    # apart shared 68 of 70). Keep the NEWEST copy — on `open`/`live` archives
    # the bid, status and photo count all move between pulls, so the freshest
    # record is the correct one. Ties fall back to file order.
    by_key = {}
    dupes = 0
    for v in records:
        key = (v.get("platform"), v.get("lot_number"), v.get("vin"))
        prev = by_key.get(key)
        if prev is None:
            by_key[key] = v
            continue
        dupes += 1
        if (v.get("_pulled_at") or "") >= (prev.get("_pulled_at") or ""):
            by_key[key] = v

    kept, dropped = [], []
    for v in by_key.values():
        ok, why = keep(v, filters)
        (kept if ok else dropped).append((v, why))
    seen = by_key
```

```
def resolve_one(f):
    """Accept an absolute path, a path relative to the shell's cwd, or a bare
    filename living in analytics/sold-data/ (what pull_apibara_01 prints)."""
    p = Path(f)
    if p.is_absolute() or p.exists():
        return p
    if (IN_DIR / f).exists():
        return IN_DIR / f
    raise SystemExit(f"input not found: {f}\n  looked in ./{f} and {IN_DIR / f}")


def resolve_inputs(args):
    if args.files:
        return [resolve_one(f) for f in args.files]
```
