````bash
{ cat <<'HEAD'
# IAAI CSV schema — Apibara raw JSON → analysis CSV

Produced by [`analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py`](../scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py)
from archives written by [`pull_apibara_01.py`](../scripts/pull_apibara_01.py).
Run `python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py --schema` to print the
same mapping from the code itself — the script's `SCHEMA` list is the single
source of truth, and this document is generated from it.

**IAAI ONLY.** Copart gets its own schema and its own converter. This is not
tidiness — Copart records carry `details: None`, which deletes `ActualCashValue`,
`EstimatedRepairCost`, body style, storage coordinates and the whole `attributes`
block at once. Roughly half the columns below cannot exist on a Copart lot.

## Reading the table

- **kind = `raw`** — copied out of the JSON unchanged (only `None`/`""`/`"unknown"`/
  `"******"` normalised to empty).
- **kind = `calc`** — computed by the converter: parsed numbers, ratios,
  classifications, media decomposition.
- **filled** — coverage on the reference pull (70 IAAI Audi S5 lots,
  `apibara_iaai_ended_audi_s5_2018-2023_2025-08-01_2026-08-10`). A low number
  means the field is genuinely sparse in IAAI's data, not that mapping is broken.

## Four things that will bite you

**1. `salvage_id` is the image key, and it is NOT `lot_number`.**
Lot `45640490` has `SalvageId` `46139013`. Build image URLs from `salvage_id`
(or better, from `iaai_image_url_prefix`), never from the lot number.

**2. Image keys are not contiguous.** A 16-photo lot has keys
`1|2|…|11|115|116|117|118|119` — they jump. They cannot be regenerated from
`image_count`, which is why the full array is stored. Rebuild a URL as:

```
{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=845&height=633    # large
{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=400&height=300    # thumb
```

**3. `seller.type` under-reports — do not filter on it.** On the reference pull
it said `insurance` for 52 lots and `unknown` for 18, while IAAI's own
`attributes.Origin` said `Insurance` for **all 70** and `ProviderType` said `INS`
for all 70. Several of those "unknown" lots name an obvious carrier outright
(*Mapfre Usa*, *American Access Casualty Group*, *Aaa So California*). Apibara's
normalisation is simply incomplete. This is why `seller_class` reads
`Origin`/`ProviderType` first, and why `seller_type_incomplete` exists: it flags
the ~26% of rows where the two disagree.

**4. IAAI masks seller identity on some lots — `SellerType` comes back as
`******`** (13 of 70 on the reference pull), with `seller.name = "unknown"`. The
masking hides *which* carrier, not *whether* it is one. `seller_name_masked`
flags these so they can be excluded from carrier-level analysis without being
miscounted as dealers.

## Deliberately excluded

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `media.items[type=vr360]` | One fixed URL shape per lot, no analytic signal. Stays in the raw JSON. |
| `media.has_360` | Same. |
| `details.auction_information.prebidInformation.*` | Session/UI state — login errors, popup text, "you are not logged in". Reflects the API client, not the vehicle. |
| `details.attributes.Synonyms`, `EmailTextForShare`, `LocationHours`, `PickupInstructions` | Marketing/branch boilerplate, identical across lots. |
| `$id`, `$values` | .NET serialiser artifacts. |

Nothing is lost by exclusion: the raw archive keeps every field, so a new column
is one line in `SCHEMA` plus a re-run — no API calls.

## Columns
HEAD
cat /tmp/claude-1000/-home-striker-projects-car-bid-tracker/1de5f512-27cc-4a6f-a0ee-152360548399/scratchpad/schema_body.md
cat <<'FOOT'

## Copart differences (for the future `apibara_json2csv_copart_01.py`)

Measured on a 20-lot Copart pull:

| Column group | IAAI | Copart |
|---|---|---|
| `details` block entirely | present | **`None` on 20/20** |
| `acv_usd`, `est_repair_usd` | 70/70 | **absent** — no ACV, no repair estimate |
| `body_style` | 70/70 | **0/20** — null on every record |
| `branch_lat` / `branch_lng` | 70/70 | absent (use `facility.*`, sparse) |
| `seller_type_raw` | `insurance` / `unknown` | `insurance` / `non_insurance` / `unknown` — cleaner |
| `engine_raw` | `"3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo, 354HP"` | `"3.0L 6"` — no layout, no HP |
| damage vocabulary | positional (`Left rear`, `Front & rear`) | coarse (`Rear end`, `Side`, `All over`) |

The practical consequence: **IAAI lots are self-pricing and Copart lots are not.**
`acv_usd` is the insurer's own clean-value figure and `est_repair_usd` its repair
estimate, so an IAAI row carries everything the max-bid calculation needs without
a MarketCheck call. A Copart row needs an external clean value.

Note the Copart converter will need its own seller logic, not a copy of this one:
Copart has no `attributes.Origin`, so the cascade that fixes IAAI's `seller.type`
gap has nothing to fall back on — but Copart's `seller.type` is already clean
(`non_insurance` is populated, never blank-by-omission).
FOOT
````

Both fixed and verified. Also found two more bugs while reviewing.

## a) Date range — fixed

Root cause: for a single date I wrote `lo, hi = today, d[0]` with no sort. Your `2025-08-01` is in the past, so it produced `from=2026-08-10, to=2025-08-01` — an inverted range. Apibara doesn't reject that; it just matches nothing, which is why one lot came back and one call was burned. Both endpoints are now sorted, so a single date means "between today and that date" in whichever direction it lies:

| input | resolved |
|---|---|
| `--auction-date-range 2025-08-01` | `from=2025-08-01 to=2026-08-10` ← your case, now correct |
| `--auction-date-range 2026-12-25` | `from=2026-08-10 to=2026-12-25` (future date → forwards) |
| `--auction-date-range 2026-08-10 2025-08-01` | `from=2025-08-01 to=2026-08-10` (backwards pair also sorted) |

## b) `--seller insurance` — clean, no leakage

The `seller.type: {'insurance': 52, 'unknown': 18}` line in your terminal output was **my summary being misleading, not the filter failing**. Checking the underlying IAAI fields on all 70 records:

```
attributes.Origin  : {'Insurance': 70}      ← IAAI's own field
ProviderType       : {'INS': 70}
seller.type        : {'insurance': 52, 'unknown': 18}   ← Apibara's normalization
```

All 18 "unknown" lots are insurance. Several name the carrier outright — *Mapfre Usa*, *American Access Casualty Group*, *Aaa So California*, *Auto Club Of Southern Ca* — while `seller.type` still says unknown. **Apibara's `seller.type` is incomplete; the server-side `seller_type` filter is not.** The filter reads the same underlying data the `Origin` field exposes.

The pull summary now shows both and says so explicitly, so this never reads as leakage again:

```
seller.type:  {'insurance': 52, 'unknown': 18}
seller Origin:{'Insurance': 70}   <- IAAI's own field; trust this one
note: 18 lot(s) have seller.type='unknown' but Origin='Insurance' — Apibara's
      field is incomplete, not the filter. json2csv resolves this into seller_class.
```

## Converter changes — three, one of which was a real bug

**1. De-dupe kept the *oldest* copy of a repeated lot.** Your two archives share 68 of 70 lots. On `ended` archives this is harmless (sold prices are frozen — I verified 0 of 68 changed). On `open`/`live` archives it would be actively wrong: bids, status and photo counts move between pulls, and the stale row would win. Now the newest `pulled_at` wins. Verified merging both archives: 70 unique rows, **all** from the newer file.

**2. Path resolution.** Relative paths were forced under `analytics/sold-data/`, so pasting `analytics/sold-data/foo.json` from the repo root produced `analytics/sold-data/analytics/sold-data/foo.json`. Now it accepts an absolute path, a cwd-relative path, or a bare filename — with an error that names both places it looked.

**3. New column `seller_type_incomplete`** (95 columns now) — true where Apibara's `seller.type` is `unknown` but IAAI's `Origin` is set. 18 of 70 on your pull. That makes the disagreement queryable instead of a footnote, and lets you sanity-check any future seller analysis.

[analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) is regenerated against the 70-lot pull, with the `seller.type` trap promoted into the "things that will bite you" section, and a note that `filled` on a boolean column means *present*, not *true*.

Current CSV: 70 rows × 95 columns, all classified `insurance`, 14 flagged `seller_name_masked`.

One leftover: `apibara_iaai_ended_audi_s5_2018-2023_2026-08-10_2025-08-01_20260810T133857.json` (928 bytes) is the empty result from the inverted-range run — safe to delete whenever you like.

```bash
rows=list(csv.DictReader(open('analytics/sold-data/apibara_iaai_ended_audi_s5_2018-2023_2025-08-01_2026-08-10_20260810T133939_iaai.csv')))

# exact duplicates
vals={c:[r[c] for r in rows] for c in cols}
nvals={c:[norm(r[c]) for r in rows] for c in cols}
print("=== IDENTICAL columns (same value every row) ===")
seen=set()
for a,b in itertools.combinations(cols,2):
    if vals[a]==vals[b]: print(f"  {a}  ==  {b}")
print("\n=== EQUIVALENT after normalising case/punctuation ===")
for a,b in itertools.combinations(cols,2):
    if vals[a]!=vals[b] and nvals[a]==nvals[b]: print(f"  {a}  ~=  {b}")
print("\n=== CONSTANT columns (one distinct value) ===")
for c in cols:
    d=set(vals[c])
    if len(d)==1: print(f"  {c:<26} = {list(d)[0]!r}")
print("\n=== EMPTY / near-empty (<25% filled) ===")

    f=sum(1 for v in vals[c] if v)
    if f < len(rows)*0.25: print(f"  {c:<26} {f}/{len(rows)}")
print("\n=== one-way derivable (A determines B) ===")
for a,b in itertools.permutations(cols,2):
    if a==b: continue
    m=collections.defaultdict(set)
    for r in rows: m[r[a]].add(r[b])

        m2=collections.defaultdict(set)
        for r in rows: m2[r[b]].add(r[a])
        if all(len(s)==1 for s in m2.values()):
            print(f"  {a} <-> {b}  (1:1, {len(m)} distinct)")
```

```
"""
Slim IAAI CSV — the analysis-ready subset of apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py.

    pull_apibara_01.py  ->  raw .json  ->  THIS SCRIPT  ->  slim .csv

Same inputs, same filters, same derivations — 45 columns instead of 95, with
every duplicate and near-duplicate removed. NOTE the name: despite "pull", this
script makes NO API calls. It reads archives off disk, exactly like
apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py does. The only thing that ever spends quota is
pull_apibara_01.py.

    python analytics/scripts/iaai_pull_01.py                    # newest archive
    python analytics/scripts/iaai_pull_01.py FILE.json ...      # specific ones
    python analytics/scripts/iaai_pull_01.py --all              # every archive
    python analytics/scripts/iaai_pull_01.py --dropped          # what was cut, and why

All filters from the full converter still work: --exclude-damage, --include-damage,
--body-style, --exclude-body-style, --seller-class, --min-photos, --sold-only.

WHY THIS EXISTS ALONGSIDE THE FULL CONVERTER
--------------------------------------------
The 95-column CSV is the archive-grade flattening: it keeps IAAI's raw text
alongside parsed numbers, keeps every seller field so the classification can be
audited, and keeps codes alongside their descriptions. That is the right shape
for verifying a mapping, and the wrong shape for analysis — half of it is the
same fact written twice.

This script keeps one representative of each fact. It does not re-implement
anything: it imports apibara_json2csv_iaai_01 and selects from its SCHEMA, so
the two can never disagree about what a column means. Add a column to the full
converter and it is available here by name; nothing else changes.

WHAT WAS REMOVED, AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE
--------------------------------------
Measured across the 70-lot reference pull, not assumed:

  identical values in every row      vehicle_class == body_style
                                     key_fob == has_key
                                     location_display == selling_branch
  identical after case/punctuation   seller_provider_name ~= seller_name
                                     seller_origin ~= seller_class
  1:1 with a column that is kept     primary_damage_code <-> primary_damage
                                     secondary_damage_code <-> secondary_damage
                                     est_repair_raw <-> est_repair_usd
                                     acv_raw <-> acv_usd
                                     body_style_name <-> body_style
                                     runs_and_drives <-> run_condition

Note the direction of each choice. Where a code and a description are 1:1, the
description survives — codes are IAAI-internal ("AO", "LR") and mean nothing in
a spreadsheet. Where raw text and a parsed number are 1:1, the NUMBER survives:
"$29,240 USD" does not sort or average. Where a boolean and a multi-valued field
are 1:1, the MULTI-VALUED one survives: `runs_and_drives` collapsed to true/false
here only because this pull happened to contain two of IAAI's three run states —
`run_condition` keeps "ENGINE START PROGRAM" distinct from "STATIONARY", which a
boolean cannot.

Nothing is lost permanently. The raw JSON keeps every field, and the full
converter still emits all 95 columns whenever the detail is wanted.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import apibara_json2csv_iaai_01 as full  # noqa: E402

IN_DIR = full.IN_DIR

# The kept subset, in output order. Validated against full.SCHEMA at import, so
# a typo or a renamed upstream column fails loudly instead of silently vanishing.
SLIM_COLUMNS = [
    # identity
    "lot_number", "vin", "year", "make", "model", "series", "lot_url",
    # body / specs
    "body_style", "cylinders", "engine_size_l", "engine_hp",
    "drive_type", "transmission", "fuel_type", "exterior_color",
    # condition
    "primary_damage", "secondary_damage", "loss_type", "run_condition",
    "has_key", "airbags", "odometer_mi", "vehicle_grade",
    # title
    "sale_document", "sale_document_group", "title_state",
    # money
    "last_sold_price_usd", "current_bid_usd", "buy_now_usd",
    "acv_usd", "est_repair_usd", "repair_to_acv", "sold_to_acv",
    # auction
    "auction_at", "last_sold_day", "last_sold_status",
    # seller
    "seller_name", "seller_class", "seller_name_masked",
    # location
    "selling_branch", "branch_state", "branch_zip", "branch_lat", "branch_lng",
    # media
    "image_count", "iaai_image_url_prefix", "iaai_image_keys",
    "video_count", "iaai_video_url",
    # provenance
    "source_file", "pulled_at",
]

# Why each dropped column was dropped. Printed by --dropped; also the record of
# the analysis, so the next person does not have to re-derive it.
DROPPED = {
    "vehicle_class": "identical to body_style on 70/70",
    "body_style_name": "1:1 with body_style, uppercase variant",
    "key_fob": "identical to has_key on 70/70",
    "location_display": "identical to selling_branch on 70/70",
    "seller_provider_name": "same as seller_name once case is normalised",
    "seller_provider_group": "carrier group, redundant with seller_name",
    "seller_origin": "same information as seller_class",
    "seller_provider_type": "'INS' — same information as seller_class",
    "seller_type_raw": "Apibara's incomplete normalisation; seller_class supersedes it",
    "seller_type_iaai": "may be masked '******'; seller_name_masked carries the signal",
    "seller_class_source": "audit trail, not analysis",
    "seller_type_incomplete": "audit trail, not analysis",
    "primary_damage_code": "1:1 with primary_damage; the code is IAAI-internal",
    "secondary_damage_code": "1:1 with secondary_damage",
    "runs_and_drives": "boolean collapse of run_condition, which has 3 states",
    "start_code": "restates run_condition",
    "acv_raw": "text form of acv_usd ('$29,240 USD')",
    "est_repair_raw": "text form of est_repair_usd",
    "engine_raw": "engine_size_l + engine_hp + cylinders carry it, parsed",
    "engine_layout": "constant per engine; implied by engine_raw",
    "displacement_ci": "1/70 filled, and engine_size_l says the same in litres",
    "title_desc": "concatenation of year + make + model + series",
    "salvage_id": "embedded verbatim in iaai_image_url_prefix",
    "platform": "always 'iaai' in this converter",
    "auction_state": "implied by the archive's lot_sub_status",
    "sold_buy_now": "implied by buy_now_usd == last_sold_price_usd",
    "min_bid_usd": "reserve mechanics, not outcome",
    "bid_increment_usd": "reserve mechanics, not outcome",
    "est_cost_from_usd": "shipping estimate band, not vehicle data",
    "est_cost_to_usd": "shipping estimate band, not vehicle data",
    "lane": "yard logistics",
    "slot": "yard logistics",
    "branch_number": "selling_branch names it",
    "branch_city": "selling_branch already contains city (state)",
    "interior_color": "21/70 filled, cosmetic",
    "wheel_type": "21/70 filled, cosmetic",
    "options": "free-text trim list, needs its own parser to be useful",
    "country_of_origin": "constant per make",
    "odometer_brand": "ACTUAL/NOT ACTUAL — keep in the full CSV when auditing",
    "vehicle_condition": "20/70 filled",
    "title_code": "sale_document says it in words",
    "title_brand": "8/70 filled",
    "title_notes": "6/70 filled, free text",
    "export_ok": "export eligibility, not resale analysis",
    "displacement_ci ": "",
}

_unknown = [c for c in SLIM_COLUMNS if c not in full.SOURCE_HINTS]
if _unknown:
    raise SystemExit(f"iaai_pull_01: unknown column(s) {_unknown} — "
                     f"apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.SCHEMA has changed")


def print_columns():
    kept = set(SLIM_COLUMNS)
    all_cols = [c for c, _, _ in full.SCHEMA]
    print(f"KEPT — {len(SLIM_COLUMNS)} columns\n")
    print(f"{'column':<24} {'kind':<5} source")
    print("-" * 100)
    kinds = {c: k for c, _, k in full.SCHEMA}
    for c in SLIM_COLUMNS:
        print(f"{c:<24} {kinds[c]:<5} {full.SOURCE_HINTS.get(c, '')}")
    dropped = [c for c in all_cols if c not in kept]
    print(f"\nDROPPED — {len(dropped)} columns\n")
    print(f"{'column':<24} reason")
    print("-" * 100)
    for c in dropped:
        print(f"{c:<24} {DROPPED.get(c, '(no reason recorded)')}")
    print(f"\n{len(all_cols)} full -> {len(SLIM_COLUMNS)} slim.  "
          f"Full mapping: analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md")


def build_arg_parser():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="iaai_pull_01.py",
        description="Slim IAAI CSV (45 columns) from raw Apibara archives. "
                    "Offline — makes no API calls despite the name.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="*",
                    help="archive .json files (default: newest IAAI archive)")
    ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                    help="use every IAAI archive in analytics/sold-data/")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-damage", metavar="a,b,c")
    ap.add_argument("--include-damage", metavar="a,b,c")
    ap.add_argument("--body-style", action="append", default=[], metavar="STYLE")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-body-style", action="append", default=[],
                    metavar="STYLE")
    ap.add_argument("--seller-class", action="append", default=[],
                    choices=["insurance", "dealer", "other", "unknown"])
    ap.add_argument("--min-photos", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--sold-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="output .csv path (default: alongside input)")
    ap.add_argument("--dropped", "--schema", action="store_true", dest="schema",
                    help="print kept + dropped columns with reasons, then exit")
    return ap


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)

    if args.schema:
        print_columns()
        return 0

    paths = full.resolve_inputs(args)
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"IAAI raw JSON -> slim CSV ({len(SLIM_COLUMNS)} columns)")
    print("=" * 78)
    records = full.load_records(paths)
    if not records:
        raise SystemExit("no IAAI records found in the given archive(s)")

    filters = {
        "exclude_damage": full.csv_list(args.exclude_damage),
        "include_damage": full.csv_list(args.include_damage),
        "body_styles": {full.norm_style(x) for raw in args.body_style
                        for x in str(raw).split(",") if x.strip()},
        "exclude_body_styles": {full.norm_style(x) for raw in args.exclude_body_style
                                for x in str(raw).split(",") if x.strip()},
        "seller_classes": set(args.seller_class),
        "min_photos": args.min_photos,
        "sold_only": args.sold_only,
    }
    active = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if v}
    print(f"\n  filters: {active or 'none (keeping every record)'}")

    # newest-wins de-dupe, same rule as the full converter
    by_key, dupes = {}, 0
    for v in records:
        key = (v.get("platform"), v.get("lot_number"), v.get("vin"))
        prev = by_key.get(key)
        if prev is None:
            by_key[key] = v
            continue
        dupes += 1
        if (v.get("_pulled_at") or "") >= (prev.get("_pulled_at") or ""):
            by_key[key] = v

    kept, dropped = [], []
    for v in by_key.values():
        ok, why = full.keep(v, filters)
        (kept if ok else dropped).append((v, why))

    print(f"  unique lots: {len(by_key)}   (dropped {dupes} duplicate row(s))")
    print(f"  kept {len(kept)}   filtered out {len(dropped)}")
    if dropped:
        reasons = {}
        for _, why in dropped:
            reasons[why] = reasons.get(why, 0) + 1
        for why, n in sorted(reasons.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            print(f"      {n:>4}  {why}")

    rows = [{c: full.flatten(v)[c] for c in SLIM_COLUMNS} for v, _ in kept]

    out_path = (Path(args.out) if args.out
                else paths[-1].with_name(paths[-1].stem + "_iaai_slim.csv"))
    if not out_path.is_absolute():
        out_path = IN_DIR / out_path
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=SLIM_COLUMNS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(f"Done. {len(rows)} row(s) x {len(SLIM_COLUMNS)} column(s)")
    print(f"  CSV -> {out_path}")
    print(f"  (full {len(full.COLUMNS)}-column version: "
          f"apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

Created [analytics/scripts/iaai_pull_01.py](analytics/scripts/iaai_pull_01.py) — **95 → 51 columns**, running on your archive: 70 rows, values identical to the full CSV (0 mismatches), and **no duplicate column pairs remaining**.

## What it drops, and on what evidence

I didn't eyeball this — I compared all 4,465 column pairs across your 70 rows:

| finding | columns |
|---|---|
| **identical every row** | `vehicle_class`=`body_style`, `key_fob`=`has_key`, `location_display`=`selling_branch` |
| **identical after case/punctuation** | `seller_provider_name`≈`seller_name`, `seller_origin`≈`seller_class` |
| **1:1 with a kept column** | `primary_damage_code`↔`primary_damage`, `secondary_damage_code`, `acv_raw`↔`acv_usd`, `est_repair_raw`, `body_style_name`, `runs_and_drives`↔`run_condition` |

The *direction* of each choice follows a rule worth stating:

- **code vs description → description wins.** `AO`/`LR` mean nothing in a spreadsheet.
- **raw text vs parsed number → number wins.** `"$29,240 USD"` doesn't sort or average.
- **boolean vs multi-valued → multi-valued wins.** `runs_and_drives` looked 1:1 with `run_condition` only because this pull happened to contain two of IAAI's three run states. Keeping the boolean would silently merge `ENGINE START PROGRAM` into `STATIONARY` on the next pull — a real information loss disguised as deduplication.

One caution I applied deliberately: several columns are *constant* here (`make`, `model`, `cylinders`, `transmission`, `fuel_type`) purely because this is a single-model pull. Those are kept — dropping them would break the moment you pull a second model.

It **imports** `apibara_json2csv_iaai_01` rather than copying it — `SLIM_COLUMNS` is just a name list selected from the full `SCHEMA`, validated at import so a renamed upstream column raises immediately instead of silently vanishing. All filters pass through unchanged (verified: `--exclude-body-style coupe --sold-only` → 47 kept, 21 coupe + 2 no-sale). `--dropped` prints all 44 removed columns with the reason for each.

Two things to flag, both your call:

**The name is misleading.** `iaai_pull_01.py` sits next to `pull_apibara_01.py` but makes no API calls — it reads archives off disk. I built it under the name you asked for and put a warning at the top of the docstring and in `--help`, but something like `iaai_csv_slim_01.py` would prevent someone burning quota-shaped assumptions on it later. Happy to rename.

**It landed at 51, not the ~45 I'd guessed.** I corrected the docs to the real number rather than cutting six more columns to hit a round target — everything left earns its place. If you want it genuinely tighter, the next candidates are the location block (`branch_lat`/`branch_lng`/`branch_zip`, useful only once you're computing transport distance) and `series`/`airbags`/`vehicle_grade`.

```
=== tier.py ===
"""
Car want-list tier classification for the image-archive pipeline.

Tier 1 -- the target buys:
    Audi S4 / S5, 2018-2022
    Lexus IS300 / IS350, 6-cylinder (3.5L V6), 2016-2020
Tier 2 -- close alternates:
    Lexus IS300, 4-cylinder (2.0L turbo I4)
    Audi A4 / A5
    Infiniti Q50
Tier 3 -- everything else worth archiving:
    Honda / Toyota / Mazda sedans

Unmatched make/model returns None -- caller decides whether to skip it from
the tiered archive (see app/image_pipeline.py).
"""
import re

TIER_1 = "Tier 1"
TIER_2 = "Tier 2"
TIER_3 = "Tier 3"


def _is_six_cylinder(engine_raw: str) -> bool:
    text = (engine_raw or "").upper()
    if "V-6" in text or "V6" in text:
        return True
    if "I-4" in text or "I4" in text or " L4" in text:
        return False
    m = re.search(r"(\d\.\d)\s*L", text)
    if m:
        return float(m.group(1)) >= 3.0
    return False


def classify(make: str, model: str, year, engine_raw: str = "") -> str | None:
    make_n = (make or "").strip().lower()
    model_n = (model or "").strip().lower().replace(" ", "")
    try:
        y = int(year) if year else None
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        y = None

    if make_n == "audi" and model_n in ("s4", "s5") and y and 2018 <= y <= 2022:
        return TIER_1
    if make_n == "lexus" and model_n in ("is300", "is350") and y and 2016 <= y <= 2020:
        return TIER_1 if _is_six_cylinder(engine_raw) else TIER_2
    if make_n == "audi" and model_n in ("a4", "a5"):
        return TIER_2
    if make_n == "infiniti" and model_n == "q50":
        return TIER_2
    if make_n in ("honda", "toyota", "mazda"):
        return TIER_3
    return None
```

```
    "north", "south", "east", "west", "central", "nw", "ne", "sw", "se", "metro",
}
_DISPLAY_RE = re.compile(r"^(.*?)\s*\(([A-Za-z]{2})\)\s*$")


def _strip_directional(city_words: list) -> list:
    while city_words and city_words[-1].lower().strip(".,") in _DIRECTIONAL_SUFFIXES:
        city_words = city_words[:-1]
    while city_words and city_words[-1].isdigit():
        city_words = city_words[:-1]
    return city_words


def _lookup_city(city_raw: str, state: str):
    words = _strip_directional(city_raw.split())
    while words:
        key = (" ".join(words).lower(), state)
        if key in CITY_COORDS:
            return CITY_COORDS[key]
        words = words[:-1]
    return None


def coords_for_location(location_display: str):
    """(lat, lng) for a location.display string, or None if unresolvable."""
    if not location_display:
        return None
    m = _DISPLAY_RE.match(location_display.strip())
    if not m:
        return None
    city_raw, state = m.group(1), m.group(2).upper()
    hit = _lookup_city(city_raw, state)
    if hit:
        return hit
    return STATE_CENTROIDS.get(state)


def haversine_mi(lat: float, lng: float) -> float:
    R = 3958.8
    p1, l1, p2, l2 = map(math.radians, (DEST_LAT, DEST_LNG, lat, lng))
    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(
        math.sin((p2 - p1) / 2) ** 2
        + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin((l2 - l1) / 2) ** 2))


def distance_miles(location_display: str):
    """Approximate road-distance miles from Federal Way, WA, or None."""
    c = coords_for_location(location_display)
    if c is None:
        return None
    return haversine_mi(*c) * ROAD_FACTOR


def distance_bucket(location_display: str) -> str:
    """'250mi' / '500mi' / ... (rounded up to BUCKET_STEP), or 'unknown'."""
    miles = distance_miles(location_display)
    if miles is None:
        return "unknown"
    bucket = max(BUCKET_STEP, int(math.ceil(miles / BUCKET_STEP) * BUCKET_STEP))
    return f"{bucket}mi"
```

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'analytics/scripts')
import iaai_pull_01 as slim
KEEP=set(slim.SLIM_COLUMNS)
p='analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py'
src=open(p).read().splitlines(True)

def prune(lines, start, end, pat):
    """Drop entries whose column name isn't in KEEP. Entries begin at a line
    matching `pat` and run until the next entry or the block end."""
    out, i, cur, curkeep = [], start, [], True
    for idx in range(start, end):
        m = pat.match(src[idx])
        if m:
            if cur: out.extend(cur if curkeep else [])
            cur, curkeep = [src[idx]], m.group(1) in KEEP
        else:
            if cur: cur.append(src[idx])
            else: out.append(src[idx])
    if cur: out.extend(cur if curkeep else [])
    return out

# SCHEMA block: lines 226..350 (0-indexed 225..350)
s0, s1 = 225, 350            # between 'SCHEMA = [' and the closing ']'
h0, h1 = 460, 547            # between 'SOURCE_HINTS = {' and '}'
sch_pat = re.compile(r'^    \("([a-z0-9_]+)",')
hint_pat = re.compile(r'^    "([a-z0-9_]+)":')

new = src[:s0+1] + prune(src, s0+1, s1, sch_pat) + src[s1:h0+1] \
    + prune(src, h0+1, h1, hint_pat) + src[h1:]
open(p,'w').writelines(new)
print("rewrote", p)
```

```
`vehicle_class` was identical to `body_style` on every row, `key_fob` to

`acv_raw`, `est_repair_raw`, `body_style_name` and `runs_and_drives` were each
1:1 with a column that survived. Where a code and a description were 1:1 the
description won (codes like "AO"/"LR" mean nothing in a spreadsheet); where raw
text and a parsed number were 1:1 the number won ("$29,240 USD" does not sort);
where a boolean and a multi-valued field were 1:1 the multi-valued one won
(`run_condition` keeps IAAI's three run states, which a boolean flattens).

Nothing is lost: every dropped field is still in the raw JSON archive, and
adding a column back is one line in SCHEMA plus a re-run — no API calls.
```

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Write**: /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker/analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py</summary>

```
"""
Stage 3 of the analytics pipeline — filtered, enriched CSV for one make/model.

    pull_apibara_01.py  ->  raw .json
                              |
                        apibara_json2csv_{iaai|copart}_01.py   (flatten, 51 key fields)
                              |
                        THIS SCRIPT  ->  enriched .csv

Offline. Makes no API calls — only pull_apibara_01.py ever spends quota.

    python analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py iaai                     # newest archive
    python analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py iaai FILE.json ...       # specific ones
    python analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py iaai --all --tier 1      # every archive
    python analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py iaai --columns           # show the schema

The platform argument selects which flattener to use. Each platform has its own,
because the payloads are different schemas rather than variants of one: Copart
records carry `details: None`, which removes ACV, repair estimate, body style and
storage coordinates in one go.

    iaai    -> apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py
    copart  -> apibara_json2csv_copart_01.py   (not written yet)

FILTERS (all opt-in, all inherited from the flattener)
------------------------------------------------------
    --exclude-damage water,flood,fire   drop lots whose damage matches
    --include-damage front,rear         keep ONLY lots whose damage matches
    --body-style coupe                  keep only these body styles
    --exclude-body-style coupe          drop these
    --seller-class insurance            keep only these seller classes
    --min-photos 8                      drop thin listings
    --sold-only                         drop lots with no realised sale price

ADDED COLUMNS
-------------
`tier`            Want-list tier from app/tier.py. Because one archive is one
                  make/model, `--tier 1|2|3` sets it for the whole file. Left
                  off, each row is classified from make/model/year/engine, which
                  yields None for anything not on the want-list — so an explicit
                  --tier is the way to label a model the table does not know yet.
`tier_source`     `cli` or `auto`, so an override is never mistaken for a match.
`sold_period`     `YYYY-MM` of last_sold_day. Same convention as the month
                  folder in app/image_pipeline.py, so rows join to the photo
                  archive path.
`distance_mi`     Road-ish miles from Federal Way WA 98003 (great-circle x1.2).
`distance_bucket` `250mi` / `500mi` / `750mi` ... rounded UP to the next 250.
`distance_source` `branch_coords` or `city_table` — see the caveat below.

DISTANCE IS MORE ACCURATE HERE THAN IN app/branch_geo.py
---------------------------------------------------------
branch_geo works off `location.display` and a hand-curated city table, because
when it was written the per-lot coordinates looked unusable — `facility.lat` was
populated on only 3 of 75 records. That is still true of `facility.lat`, but
IAAI's OWN `details.attributes.StorageLocationLatitude/Longitude` is populated on
**68 of 68** records in the reference pull, and the flattener already exposes it
as `branch_lat`/`branch_lng`.

So this script prefers the real coordinates and falls back to the city table only
when they are missing, recording which in `distance_source`. Consequence worth
knowing: a lot's `distance_bucket` here can differ by one bucket from the folder
app/image_pipeline.py filed its photos under, since that pipeline still uses the
city table for every lot. Same lot, two estimates — this one is closer to true.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import importlib
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))                      # for app.*
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))   # for the flatteners

from app import branch_geo                          # noqa: E402
from app.tier import TIER_1, TIER_2, TIER_3, classify  # noqa: E402

FLATTENERS = {
    "iaai": "apibara_json2csv_iaai_01",
    "copart": "apibara_json2csv_copart_01",
}

TIERS = {"1": TIER_1, "2": TIER_2, "3": TIER_3,
         "tier1": TIER_1, "tier2": TIER_2, "tier3": TIER_3,
         "tier 1": TIER_1, "tier 2": TIER_2, "tier 3": TIER_3}

# Appended after the flattener's own columns, in this order.
ENRICHED_COLUMNS = ["tier", "tier_source", "sold_period",
                    "distance_mi", "distance_bucket", "distance_source"]


def load_flattener(platform):
    mod = FLATTENERS[platform]
    try:
        return importlib.import_module(mod)
    except ModuleNotFoundError as e:
        if e.name != mod:
            raise
        raise SystemExit(
            f"No flattener for {platform!r}: analytics/scripts/{mod}.py does "
            f"not exist yet.\n"
            f"  Copart needs its own because its payload has `details: None` "
            f"— no ACV, no repair estimate, no body style, no branch "
            f"coordinates. See the Copart section of "
            f"analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md.") from None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# enrichment
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def engine_hint(v, flat):
    """A string app.tier._is_six_cylinder can read.

    The flattener no longer emits `engine_raw` (it was 1:1 with the parsed
    columns), so rebuild just enough of it from the record. Cylinder count is
    the stronger signal; displacement is the fallback the tier table also uses.
    """
    raw = flat.g(v, "vehicle_specs", "engine", "raw")
    if raw:
        return str(raw)
    cyl = flat.attrs(v).get("Cylinders")
    if cyl:
        return f"V-{cyl}"
    size = flat.g(v, "vehicle_specs", "engine", "size_l")
    return f"{size}L" if size else ""


def row_tier(v, flat, forced):
    if forced:
        return forced, "cli"
    t = classify(v.get("make"), v.get("model"), v.get("year"),
                 engine_hint(v, flat))
    return (t or ""), ("auto" if t else "auto:unclassified")


def sold_period(row):
    """'2026-08' from last_sold_day. Matches image_pipeline's month folder."""
    d = str(row.get("last_sold_day") or "")
    return d[:7] if len(d) >= 7 else ""


def distance(row):
    """-> (miles, bucket, source). Real branch coordinates when present."""
    lat, lng = row.get("branch_lat"), row.get("branch_lng")
    miles, source = None, "unknown"
    if lat not in (None, "") and lng not in (None, ""):
        try:
            miles = branch_geo.haversine_mi(float(lat), float(lng)) \
                * branch_geo.ROAD_FACTOR
            source = "branch_coords"
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            miles = None
    if miles is None:
        miles = branch_geo.distance_miles(row.get("selling_branch") or "")
        source = "city_table" if miles is not None else "unknown"
    if miles is None:
        return None, "unknown", source
    step = branch_geo.BUCKET_STEP
    bucket = max(step, int(math.ceil(miles / step) * step))
    return round(miles), f"{bucket}mi", source


def enrich(v, row, flat, forced_tier):
    tier, tier_source = row_tier(v, flat, forced_tier)
    miles, bucket, dsource = distance(row)
    return {**row,
            "tier": tier,
            "tier_source": tier_source,
            "sold_period": sold_period(row),
            "distance_mi": miles,
            "distance_bucket": bucket,
            "distance_source": dsource}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def parse_tier(s):
    key = str(s).strip().lower()
    if key in ("", "auto"):
        return None
    if key not in TIERS:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"--tier wants 1, 2, 3 or 'Tier 1'/'Tier 2'/'Tier 3', got {s!r}")
    return TIERS[key]


def build_arg_parser():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="data_pull_01.py",
        description="Filtered, enriched CSV from raw Apibara archives. "
                    "Offline — no API calls.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("platform", choices=list(FLATTENERS), type=str.lower)
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="*",
                    help="archive .json files (default: newest for the platform)")
    ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                    help="use every archive for this platform")
    ap.add_argument("--tier", type=parse_tier, default=None, metavar="{1|2|3}",
                    help="label every row with this tier (one archive = one "
                         "make/model). Omit to classify per row via app/tier.py")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-damage", metavar="a,b,c")
    ap.add_argument("--include-damage", metavar="a,b,c")
    ap.add_argument("--body-style", action="append", default=[], metavar="STYLE")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-body-style", action="append", default=[],
                    metavar="STYLE")
    ap.add_argument("--seller-class", action="append", default=[],
                    choices=["insurance", "dealer", "other", "unknown"])
    ap.add_argument("--min-photos", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--sold-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="output .csv path (default: alongside input)")
    ap.add_argument("--columns", "--schema", action="store_true", dest="columns",
                    help="print the output columns and exit")
    return ap


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)
    flat = load_flattener(args.platform)
    columns = list(flat.COLUMNS) + ENRICHED_COLUMNS

    if args.columns:
        print(f"{len(columns)} columns = {len(flat.COLUMNS)} from "
              f"{FLATTENERS[args.platform]} + {len(ENRICHED_COLUMNS)} added here\n")
        for c in flat.COLUMNS:
            print(f"  {c:<24} {flat.SOURCE_HINTS.get(c, '')}")
        print()
        for c in ENRICHED_COLUMNS:
            print(f"  {c:<24} ** added by data_pull_01 **")
        return 0

    paths = flat.resolve_inputs(args)
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"{args.platform.upper()} raw JSON -> enriched CSV")
    print("=" * 78)
    records = flat.load_records(paths)
    if not records:
        raise SystemExit(f"no {args.platform} records in the given archive(s)")

    filters = {
        "exclude_damage": flat.csv_list(args.exclude_damage),
        "include_damage": flat.csv_list(args.include_damage),
        "body_styles": {flat.norm_style(x) for raw in args.body_style
                        for x in str(raw).split(",") if x.strip()},
        "exclude_body_styles": {flat.norm_style(x) for raw in args.exclude_body_style
                                for x in str(raw).split(",") if x.strip()},
        "seller_classes": set(args.seller_class),
        "min_photos": args.min_photos,
        "sold_only": args.sold_only,
    }
    active = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if v}
    print(f"\n  filters: {active or 'none (keeping every record)'}")
    print(f"  tier:    {args.tier or 'auto (per-row via app/tier.py)'}")

    # newest-wins de-dupe across overlapping archives
    by_key, dupes = {}, 0
    for v in records:
        key = (v.get("platform"), v.get("lot_number"), v.get("vin"))
        prev = by_key.get(key)
        if prev is None:
            by_key[key] = v
            continue
        dupes += 1
        if (v.get("_pulled_at") or "") >= (prev.get("_pulled_at") or ""):
            by_key[key] = v

    kept, dropped = [], []
    for v in by_key.values():
        ok, why = flat.keep(v, filters)
        (kept if ok else dropped).append((v, why))

    print(f"  unique lots: {len(by_key)}   (dropped {dupes} duplicate row(s))")
    print(f"  kept {len(kept)}   filtered out {len(dropped)}")
    if dropped:
        reasons = {}
        for _, why in dropped:
            reasons[why] = reasons.get(why, 0) + 1
        for why, n in sorted(reasons.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
            print(f"      {n:>4}  {why}")

    rows = [enrich(v, flat.flatten(v), flat, args.tier) for v, _ in kept]

    # what the enrichment actually produced — a silent 'unknown' bucket or an
    # empty tier column is the failure mode worth surfacing every run
    def tally(col):
        out = {}
        for r in rows:
            out[r[col] or "(none)"] = out.get(r[col] or "(none)", 0) + 1
        return dict(sorted(out.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))

    print(f"\n  tier:            {tally('tier')}")
    print(f"  tier_source:     {tally('tier_source')}")
    print(f"  sold_period:     {tally('sold_period')}")
    print(f"  distance_bucket: {tally('distance_bucket')}")
    print(f"  distance_source: {tally('distance_source')}")

    out_path = (Path(args.out) if args.out
                else paths[-1].with_name(paths[-1].stem + "_data.csv"))
    if not out_path.is_absolute():
        out_path = flat.IN_DIR / out_path
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=columns)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(f"Done. {len(rows)} row(s) x {len(columns)} column(s)")
    print(f"  CSV -> {out_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Bash**: Rewrite schema doc and refresh stage-2 CSV</summary>

````bash
{ cat <<'HEAD'
# IAAI CSV schema — Apibara raw JSON → analysis CSV

```
pull_apibara_01.py  ->  raw .json          (stage 1, the only thing that spends API quota)
        |
apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py  ->  .csv      (stage 2, flatten to 51 key fields)
        |
data_pull_01.py {iaai|copart} ->  .csv     (stage 3, filter + enrich: tier, period, distance)
```

Stage 2 is documented here. Run
`python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py --schema` to print the same
mapping from the code — the script's `SCHEMA` list is the single source of truth
and this document is generated from it. Stage 3 adds six more columns, listed at
the bottom.

**IAAI ONLY.** Copart gets its own flattener. Not tidiness — Copart records carry
`details: None`, which deletes `ActualCashValue`, `EstimatedRepairCost`, body
style, storage coordinates and the whole `attributes` block at once.

## Key fields only

51 columns, one per fact. Duplicates were removed after measuring them across the
70-lot reference pull, not by eye — `vehicle_class` was identical to `body_style`
on every row, `key_fob` to `has_key`, `location_display` to `selling_branch`,
while `primary_damage_code`, `acv_raw`, `est_repair_raw`, `body_style_name` and
`runs_and_drives` were each 1:1 with a column that survived.

Three rules decided which side of a 1:1 pair survives:

- **code vs description → description.** `AO`/`LR` mean nothing in a spreadsheet.
- **raw text vs parsed number → number.** `"$29,240 USD"` does not sort or average.
- **boolean vs multi-valued → multi-valued.** `runs_and_drives` looked 1:1 with
  `run_condition` only because this pull contained two of IAAI's three run states;
  the boolean would silently merge `ENGINE START PROGRAM` into `STATIONARY`.

Nothing is lost — the raw JSON archive keeps every field, so restoring a column is
one line in `SCHEMA` plus a re-run, with no API calls.

## Reading the table

- **kind = `raw`** — copied out of the JSON unchanged (only `None`/`""`/`"unknown"`/
  `"******"` normalised to empty).
- **kind = `calc`** — computed by the converter: parsed numbers, ratios,
  classifications, media decomposition.
- **filled** — coverage on the reference pull (70 IAAI Audi S5 lots,
  `apibara_iaai_ended_audi_s5_2018-2023_2025-08-01_2026-08-10`). A low number
  means the field is genuinely sparse in IAAI's data, not that mapping is broken.
  For boolean columns, filled means *present* — `70/70` on a flag says every row
  has a true/false value, not that every row is true.

## Four things that will bite you

**1. `iaai_image_url_prefix` embeds `SalvageId`, which is NOT `lot_number`.**
Lot `45640490` has `SalvageId` `46139013`. Never build image URLs from the lot
number.

**2. Image keys are not contiguous.** A 16-photo lot has keys
`1|2|…|11|115|116|117|118|119` — they jump. They cannot be regenerated from
`image_count`, which is why the full array is stored. Rebuild a URL as:

```
{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=845&height=633    # large
{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=400&height=300    # thumb
```

**3. `seller.type` under-reports — which is why it is not a column.** On the
reference pull it said `insurance` for 52 lots and `unknown` for 18, while IAAI's
own `attributes.Origin` said `Insurance` for **all 70**. Several "unknown" lots
name an obvious carrier outright (*Mapfre Usa*, *American Access Casualty Group*,
*Aaa So California*). `seller_class` reads `Origin`/`ProviderType` first and is
the column to trust.

**4. IAAI masks seller identity on some lots** — `SellerType` comes back as
`******` (13 of 70), with `seller.name = "unknown"`. The masking hides *which*
carrier, not *whether* it is one. `seller_name_masked` flags these so they can be
excluded from carrier-level analysis without being miscounted as dealers.

## Deliberately excluded

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `media.items[type=vr360]`, `media.has_360` | One fixed URL shape per lot, no analytic signal. |
| `details.auction_information.prebidInformation.*` | Session/UI state — login errors, popup text. Reflects the API client, not the vehicle. |
| `details.attributes.Synonyms`, `EmailTextForShare`, `LocationHours`, `PickupInstructions` | Marketing/branch boilerplate, identical across lots. |
| `$id`, `$values` | .NET serialiser artifacts. |
| codes duplicating descriptions, raw text duplicating parsed numbers | See "Key fields only" above. |

## Columns

cat <<'FOOT'

## Stage 3 — columns added by `data_pull_01.py`

| Column | Source |
|---|---|
| `tier` | `--tier 1\|2\|3`, else per-row `app/tier.py` classification |
| `tier_source` | `cli` / `auto` / `auto:unclassified` |
| `sold_period` | `YYYY-MM` of `last_sold_day` — same convention as the month folder in `app/image_pipeline.py` |
| `distance_mi` | road-ish miles from Federal Way WA 98003 (great-circle × 1.2) |
| `distance_bucket` | `250mi` / `500mi` / … rounded **up** to the next 250 |
| `distance_source` | `branch_coords` or `city_table` |

**Distance is computed differently — and better — than in `app/branch_geo.py`.**
That module works off `location.display` plus a hand-curated city table because
`facility.lat` was populated on only 3 of 75 records when it was written. Still
true of `facility.lat` — but IAAI's own
`details.attributes.StorageLocationLatitude/Longitude` is populated on **70/70**
and surfaces here as `branch_lat`/`branch_lng`. Stage 3 prefers those and falls
back to the city table only when missing.

On the reference pull that changed the bucket for **22 of 70 lots** (31%),
always by one step, because the city table lacks entries for branches like
*Fontana (CA)*, *ACE - Carson (CA)* and *Kansas City (KS)* and falls back to a
state centroid. Consequence: a lot's `distance_bucket` here can differ from the
folder `app/image_pipeline.py` filed its photos under, since that pipeline still
uses the city table for every lot. Same lot, two estimates — this one is closer.

## Copart differences (for the future `apibara_json2csv_copart_01.py`)

Measured on a 20-lot Copart pull:

| Column group | IAAI | Copart |
|---|---|---|
| `details` block entirely | present | **`None` on 20/20** |
| `acv_usd`, `est_repair_usd` | 70/70 | **absent** — no ACV, no repair estimate |
| `body_style` | 70/70 | **0/20** — null on every record |
| `branch_lat` / `branch_lng` | 70/70 | absent (use `facility.*`, sparse) — so Copart distance must fall back to the city table |
| `seller_class` inputs | `Origin`/`ProviderType` | absent; but `seller.type` is clean (`non_insurance` populated) |
| engine | `"3.0L V-6 DI, DOHC, VVT, turbo, 354HP"` | `"3.0L 6"` — no layout, no HP |
| damage vocabulary | positional (`Left rear`, `Front & rear`) | coarse (`Rear end`, `Side`, `All over`) |

The practical consequence: **IAAI lots are self-pricing and Copart lots are not.**
`acv_usd` is the insurer's own clean-value figure and `est_repair_usd` its repair
estimate, so an IAAI row carries everything the max-bid calculation needs without
a MarketCheck call. A Copart row needs an external clean value.
````

Done. The pipeline is now three stages, and `app/tier.py` + `app/branch_geo.py` are reused rather than reimplemented.

```
pull_apibara_01.py            -> raw .json    (the only stage that spends API quota)
apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py   -> .csv         (flatten, 51 key fields)
data_pull_01.py {iaai|copart} -> .csv         (filter + enrich, 57 columns)
```

## 1) Converter trimmed to key fields — 95 → 51

Same removals as the slim script, decided by measurement. Everything dropped remains in the raw JSON, so restoring a column is one line in `SCHEMA` plus a re-run — no API calls.

One thing that broke and is fixed: the seller audit printed `seller_class_source` / `seller_origin` / `seller_type_iaai`, which are no longer columns. It now reads those back off the *record* — so the classification evidence still prints in full while staying out of the CSV.

## 2) `data_pull_01.py` — platform dispatch + enrichment

`--tier 1|2|3` (or `"Tier 1"`) labels the whole file, since one archive is one make/model. Omit it and each row is classified by `app/tier.py`. That difference is visible and useful on your data:

| | result |
|---|---|
| `--tier 1` | `{'Tier 1': 70}`, source `cli` |
| auto | `{'Tier 1': 69, '(none)': 1}` — the **2023** S5 is unclassified, because the want-list covers Audi S5 2018–2022 |

`tier_source` (`cli` / `auto` / `auto:unclassified`) keeps an override from ever being mistaken for a match.

`sold_period` → `2026-03`, `2026-07`, … deliberately the same `YYYY-MM` convention as the month folder in `app/image_pipeline.py`, so rows join to the photo archive path.

`copart` is wired but has no flattener yet, so it exits with a message explaining *why* it needs its own (`details: None` → no ACV, no repair estimate, no body style, no branch coords) rather than a bare `ModuleNotFoundError`.

## Distance — I deviated from `app/branch_geo.py`, deliberately

`branch_geo` resolves location through a hand-curated city table because per-lot coordinates looked unusable — `facility.lat` was populated on only 3 of 75 records when it was written. That's still true of `facility.lat`, **but IAAI's own `StorageLocationLatitude/Longitude` is populated on 70/70**, and stage 2 already exposes it as `branch_lat`/`branch_lng`.

So stage 3 prefers the real coordinates, falls back to the city table, and records which in `distance_source`. All 70 lots resolved via `branch_coords`. Sanity check: Seattle 18 mi, Miami-North 3,242 mi.

**This changes the bucket for 22 of 70 lots (31%)** — always by one step, because the city table has no entry for branches like *Fontana (CA)*, *ACE - Carson (CA)* or *Kansas City (KS)* (it has Kansas City **MO**, not KS) and falls back to a state centroid. `Fontana (CA)` → city table 1000mi, real coords 1250mi.

Worth knowing: a lot's `distance_bucket` here can now differ from the folder `app/image_pipeline.py` filed its photos under, since that pipeline still uses the city table for every lot. Same lot, two estimates — this one is closer to true. If you want them consistent, the fix is to teach `branch_geo` to accept coordinates when available; I left `app/` untouched since it's outside what you asked for.

[analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) is regenerated: 51-column table with live coverage, the three dedup rules, and a stage-3 section documenting the six added columns and the distance caveat.

Two leftovers in `sold-data/`, both yours to delete: `..._iaai_slim.csv` (orphaned — its script is now `data_pull_01.py`) and the 928-byte `..._2026-08-10_2025-08-01_...json` from the inverted-date run.

```
1	"""

10	one row, and applies whatever filtering you ask for. No network, no API calls —
11	run it as often as you like, with different filters, against the same archive.
12	
13	KEY FIELDS ONLY — 55 columns, one per fact
14	------------------------------------------
15	Duplicates were removed after measuring them across a 70-lot pull, not by eye:

30	inspected the car and recorded secondary damage as UNKNOWN, a state a blank
31	description cannot be distinguished from "nothing recorded at all". Dropping it
32	would have silently merged two different facts.

49	
50	IAAI ONLY. A Copart converter will be a separate script, because the two payload
51	shapes are not variations of one schema — they are different schemas. Copart
52	records carry `details: None`, which removes ActualCashValue, EstimatedRepairCost,
53	body style, storage coordinates and the entire attributes block in one go. Nearly
54	half the columns below simply do not exist on a Copart lot, so a shared converter
55	would be mostly null-handling.
56	
57	SELLER CLASSIFICATION — READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE COLUMN
58	------------------------------------------------------------
59	IAAI masks seller identity on a meaningful slice of lots. Observed on a 68-lot
60	insurance-filtered pull: 12 records came back with
61	
62	    sale_information.SellerType = "******"    (literally asterisks)
63	    seller.name                 = "unknown"
64	    seller.type                 = "unknown"
65	
66	...while `attributes.Origin` said "Insurance" and `attributes.ProviderType` said
67	"INS" on all 68. The masking hides WHICH carrier, not WHETHER it is a carrier.
68	Reading SellerType naively classifies those 12 as non-insurance, which is simply
69	wrong — every one of them came from a `seller_type=insurance` server-side query.
70	
71	So `seller_class` cascades, most reliable source first, and records which source
72	decided in `seller_class_source`. `seller_name_masked` flags the anonymised ones
73	so they can be excluded from carrier-level analysis without being miscounted as
74	dealers.
75	
76	IMAGE / VIDEO COLUMNS
77	---------------------
78	IAAI thumb URLs look like:
79	
80	    https://vis.iaai.com/resizer?imageKeys=46139013~SID~I1&width=400&height=300
81	                                           ^^^^^^^^        ^
82	                                           SalvageId       image key
83	
84	`iaai_image_url_prefix` keeps everything up to and including the trailing "I",
85	and `iaai_image_keys` collects the numeric suffixes as a pipe-joined array
86	(1|2|...|115|116) — the keys are NOT contiguous, they jump from ~11 to ~115, so
87	they cannot be regenerated from a count and must be stored. Rebuild any URL as:
88	
89	    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=845&height=633"      # large
90	    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=400&height=300"      # thumb
91	
92	Note the image key is `attributes.SalvageId`, which is NOT the lot number
93	(lot 45640490 -> SalvageId 46139013). Do not build image URLs from lot_number.
94	
95	vr360 is deliberately absent from the CSV — it carries no analytic signal and
96	one fixed URL shape per lot. It remains in the raw JSON if ever needed.
```

## On the damage codes — the two are not the same case

You asked whether they add context. **`primary_damage_code` does not** — 14 descriptions ↔ 14 codes, strictly paired, both 70/70. `F`/`LR`/`AO` is just a shorter way of writing `Front end`/`Left rear`/`All over`, so it stays out.

**`secondary_damage_code` does**, and it's a genuine trap I'd have missed by reasoning from the primary case:

```
desc blank + code blank  -> no secondary damage recorded   (30 lots)
desc blank + code "UK"   -> inspected, damage unknown      (10 lots)
desc set   + code set    -> the damage itself              (30 lots)
```

The description is populated on 30/70 but the code on 40/70. Those 10 extra rows carry `UK`, whose `SecondaryDamageDesc` spells out `UNKNOWN` — IAAI looked at the car and recorded the secondary damage as unknown. That is not the same as no secondary damage, and the blank description can't tell you which. **Filtering on `secondary_damage == ""` merges 30 "clean" lots with 10 "unknown" ones** — a 33% contamination of that group. Keeping the code is what makes them separable.

I left `secondary_damage` itself untouched rather than back-filling it with `"Unknown"`, since you want raw values kept as-is. If you'd rather the distinction live in the description column so a plain read isn't misleading, that's a one-line fallback to `attributes.SecondaryDamageDesc` — say the word.

Both scripts re-run clean (70 rows), and [analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) is regenerated: 55-column table with live coverage, plus a new subsection documenting the primary-vs-secondary asymmetry with the decode table above. The dedup rules now carry it as the stated exception — the reason each pair gets measured rather than assumed by symmetry.

One stale reference cleaned up while I was in there: the docstring still promised a `seller_class_source` column, which was dropped two steps ago. It now says the rule that fired is printed in the audit table each run rather than stored per row.

```
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derived: distance from Federal Way, WA 98003
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def branch_coords(v):
    """(lat, lng) from IAAI's own StorageLocation fields, or (None, None)."""
    a = attrs(v)
    try:
        return (float(a["StorageLocationLatitude"]),
                float(a["StorageLocationLongitude"]))
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        return None, None


def distance_mi(v):
    """Road-ish miles to the transport destination, or None.

    No city-table fallback, unlike app/branch_geo.py. That module resolves
    `location.display` through a hand-curated lookup because `facility.lat` was
    populated on only 3 of 75 records when it was written — still true of
    `facility.lat`, but IAAI's own StorageLocationLatitude/Longitude is a
    different field and is populated on 154/154 records across four independent
    pulls, all inside the continental US. So this uses the real coordinates and
    nothing else; a lot missing them yields an empty distance and is counted in
    the run summary rather than being quietly approximated from a state
    centroid.
    """
    lat, lng = branch_coords(v)
    if lat is None:
        return None
    return round(haversine_mi(lat, lng) * ROAD_FACTOR)


def distance_bucket(v):
    """'250mi' / '500mi' / ... rounded UP to the next BUCKET_STEP, or None."""
    miles = distance_mi(v)
    if miles is None:
        return None
    return f"{max(BUCKET_STEP, int(math.ceil(miles / BUCKET_STEP) * BUCKET_STEP))}mi"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derived: media
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

*old_string*
```
ADDED COLUMNS
-------------
`tier`            Want-list tier from app/tier.py. Because one archive is one
                  make/model, `--tier 1|2|3` sets it for the whole file. Left
                  off, each row is classified from make/model/year/engine, which
                  yields None for anything not on the want-list — so an explicit
                  --tier is the way to label a model the table does not know yet.
`tier_source`     `cli` or `auto`, so an override is never mistaken for a match.
`sold_period`     `YYYY-MM` of last_sold_day. Same convention as the month
                  folder in app/image_pipeline.py, so rows join to the photo
                  archive path.
`distance_mi`     Road-ish miles from Federal Way WA 98003 (great-circle x1.2).
`distance_bucket` `250mi` / `500mi` / `750mi` ... rounded UP to the next 250.
`distance_source` `branch_coords` or `city_table` — see the caveat below.

DISTANCE IS MORE ACCURATE HERE THAN IN app/branch_geo.py
---------------------------------------------------------
branch_geo works off `location.display` and a hand-curated city table, because
when it was written the per-lot coordinates looked unusable — `facility.lat` was
populated on only 3 of 75 records. That is still true of `facility.lat`, but
IAAI's OWN `details.attributes.StorageLocationLatitude/Longitude` is populated on
**68 of 68** records in the reference pull, and the flattener already exposes it
as `branch_lat`/`branch_lng`.

So this script prefers the real coordinates and falls back to the city table only
when they are missing, recording which in `distance_source`. Consequence worth
knowing: a lot's `distance_bucket` here can differ by one bucket from the folder
app/image_pipeline.py filed its photos under, since that pipeline still uses the
city table for every lot. Same lot, two estimates — this one is closer to true.
"""
```

```
def distance(row):
    """-> (miles, bucket, source). Real branch coordinates when present."""
    lat, lng = row.get("branch_lat"), row.get("branch_lng")
    miles, source = None, "unknown"
    if lat not in (None, "") and lng not in (None, ""):
        try:
            miles = branch_geo.haversine_mi(float(lat), float(lng)) \
                * branch_geo.ROAD_FACTOR
            source = "branch_coords"
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            miles = None
    if miles is None:
        miles = branch_geo.distance_miles(row.get("selling_branch") or "")
        source = "city_table" if miles is not None else "unknown"
    if miles is None:
        return None, "unknown", source
    step = branch_geo.BUCKET_STEP
    bucket = max(step, int(math.ceil(miles / step) * step))
    return round(miles), f"{bucket}mi", source


def enrich(v, row, flat, forced_tier):
    tier, tier_source = row_tier(v, flat, forced_tier)
    miles, bucket, dsource = distance(row)
    return {**row,
            "tier": tier,
            "tier_source": tier_source,
            "sold_period": sold_period(row),
            "distance_mi": miles,
            "distance_bucket": bucket,
            "distance_source": dsource}
```

```bash
centroid. Sanity check on the coordinate path: Seattle 18 mi, Miami-North
3,242 mi.

One consequence to keep in mind: `app/image_pipeline.py` still files photos using
the city table, so a lot's folder can sit in a different bucket than its CSV row.
Same lot, two estimates — the CSV one is closer.

"""
```

Both changes are in, and your hope about the fallback held up.

## Distance moved to stage 2 — coords only, no fallback

I checked the coverage claim before removing the fallback, across **four independent pulls** rather than just the current one:

| archive | coords |
|---|---|
| `..._2026-08-09` (68 lots) | 68/68 |
| `..._2026-08-10` (70 lots) | 70/70 |
| `test_run/apibara_sold_iaai_01` | 15/15 |
| `test_run/apibara_sold_iaai_02` | 1/1 |
| **total** | **154/154 — 100%** |

Values are real, not placeholders: lat 26.0–47.7, lng −122.3 to −71.0, zero `0,0` entries, nothing outside the continental US. So `distance_mi` and `distance_bucket` are now flattener columns computed straight from `StorageLocationLatitude/Longitude`, with **no city-table fallback at all**.

The one thing I added rather than removed: if a lot ever *does* arrive without coordinates, the run prints a loud warning naming the lots instead of leaving a silently blank cell. That's the cost of dropping the fallback — an absence has to be visible, since nothing quietly fills it in. Zero triggered on your data.

Worth noting what this fixes, since `facility.lat` (sparse, 3/75) and `StorageLocationLatitude` (154/154) are *different fields* — the original sparsity finding was about the former, and it's still true. Using the latter disagrees with `app/branch_geo.py`'s city table on **22 of 70 lots**, always by one bucket, because the table has no *Fontana (CA)* or *ACE - Carson (CA)* and holds Kansas City **MO** but not **KS**, so those fall back to a state centroid. Sanity check: Seattle 18 mi → `250mi`, Miami-North 3,242 mi → `3250mi`.

## Tier stays in stage 3

`--tier 1|2|3` (or `"Tier 1"`) still labels the whole archive, with `tier_source` recording `cli` vs `auto`. The split now has a clean rule behind it: **distance needs no decision** — the coordinates are always there, so it belongs with the raw flattening. **Tier is a judgment call per archive** — one file is one make/model, and the automatic classifier returns nothing for models outside the want-list (your 2023 S5 falls past its 2018–2022 window). That's why it stays where an operator can set it.

Column counts: stage 2 **57**, stage 3 **60** (`tier`, `tier_source`, `sold_period`).

[analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) regenerated — distance now sits in a "Location & distance" section of the stage-2 table, with a dedicated section explaining the coordinate evidence and why there's no fallback. The Copart section flags the flip side: Copart has no `attributes` block, so when that converter gets written its distance *will* need the city table.

```
def parse_year_range(s):
```

*new_string*
```
def multiword(value):
    """argparse nargs='+' value -> one string.

    Model names contain spaces ("ES 350", "IS 300"), so `--model ES 350` has to
    work without quoting — unquoted it arrives as ['ES', '350'] and, before
    nargs, argparse rejected the '350' as an unrecognised positional.
    """
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value.strip()
    return " ".join(str(x) for x in value).strip()


def parse_year_range(s):
```

*new_string*
```
def multiword(value):
    """argparse nargs='+' value -> one string, tolerating a plain str too."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value.strip()
    return " ".join(str(x) for x in value).strip()


def csv_list(s):
    """Comma-separated needles. Spaces are part of a value, commas split them,
    so `--exclude-damage front & rear,water` is two needles, not four."""
    return [x.strip().lower() for x in multiword(s).split(",") if x.strip()]


def style_set(values):
    """Repeatable, multi-word, comma-separated body styles -> normalised set.

    Real IAAI values include "Compact Luxury Car" and "Sedan/Hatchback", so the
    same rule as everywhere else applies: spaces join a value, commas separate
    values. `--body-style Compact Luxury Car` is one style;
    `--body-style coupe,sedan` is two; repeating the flag adds more.
    """
    out = set()
    for occurrence in values or []:
        for token in multiword(occurrence).split(","):
            if token.strip():
                out.add(norm_style(token))
    return out
```

I checked before changing anything: its CSV is **57 columns with no `tier` column**. `tier`/`tier_source` only exist in `data_pull_01.py`'s output (columns 58–60), which is where you asked them to live last turn.

The one place the word appeared was a stale docstring diagram claiming the downstream script adds "tier, sold period, **distance**" — outdated since distance moved into the converter. That line now reads:

```
data_pull_01.py  ->  + tier, sold_period

This script owns everything derivable from the record alone, distance included.
`tier` and `sold_period` are NOT emitted here — tier takes an operator decision
per archive, so it belongs to data_pull_01.py.
```

If you actually wanted `tier_source` dropped from the *stage-3* CSV, say so and I'll remove it — it's one line.

## 2) The bug is in `pull_apibara_01.py`, not `data_pull_01.py`

Your terminal shows `pull_apibara_01.py` failing on `--model ES 350`: argparse took `ES` as the value and choked on `350` as a stray positional. Nothing to do with `data_pull_01.py`.

Fixed with one rule across all three scripts — **spaces join a value, commas separate values**:

```bash
--model ES 350                    # one value: "ES 350"
--body-style Compact Luxury Car   # one value
--body-style coupe,convertible    # two values
```

Your exact command now resolves correctly (dry-run, no quota spent):

```
-> apibara_iaai_ended_lexus_es-350_2019-2023_2025-08-01_2026-08-10_...json
```

| `--exclude-damage front end,rollover` | 39 |

Quoting still works everywhere — it's just no longer required. The rule is documented in [analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md).

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the Apibara sold-lot probe scripts.
#
#   ./test/run_sold.sh iaai      # 1 call  — sold IAAI lots + IAAI-only filters
#   ./test/run_sold.sh copart    # 1 call  — sold Copart lots
#   ./test/run_sold.sh generic   # 2 calls — ended lots (both platforms) + one /history
#   ./test/run_sold.sh all       # 4 calls — all three, in that order
#
# EVERY RUN SPENDS LIVE API QUOTA (free plan = 100 requests/month).
# Raw JSON lands in test_run/. Requires APIBARA_API_KEY in the repo-root .env.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

PY="${PYTHON:-python}"

declare -A SCRIPTS=(
  [iaai]="test/test_apibara_sold_iaai_01.py"
  [copart]="test/test_apibara_sold_copart_01.py"
  [generic]="test/test_apibara_sold01.py"
)
declare -A COST=( [iaai]=1 [copart]=1 [generic]=2 )

target="${1:-}"
case "$target" in
  iaai|copart|generic) order=("$target") ;;
  all)                 order=(iaai copart generic) ;;
  *)
    sed -n '2,10p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

total=0
for k in "${order[@]}"; do total=$(( total + COST[$k] )); done

if [[ ! -f .env ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: no .env at $ROOT/.env — copy .env.example and set APIBARA_API_KEY" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "About to spend ~${total} Apibara API call(s) of your monthly quota."
read -r -p "Continue? [y/N] " reply
[[ "$reply" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]] || { echo "Aborted — no calls made."; exit 0; }

for k in "${order[@]}"; do
  echo
  echo "### ${SCRIPTS[$k]}  (~${COST[$k]} call(s))"
  "$PY" "${SCRIPTS[$k]}"
done

echo
echo "Done. Output written to $ROOT/test_run/"
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the full analytics pipeline for ONE make/model, end to end.
#
#   ./analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh                     # DRY RUN (default) — 0 API calls
#   ./analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh --go                # spend quota and run for real
#   ./analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh --make Audi --model S5 --years 2018-2023 --tier 1 --go
#
# Defaults pull 2019-2023 Lexus ES 350, IAAI, ended (sold) lots, insurance
# sellers, from 2025-08-01 to today.
#
# Stages:
#   1. pull_apibara_01.py           raw .json    <- THE ONLY STEP THAT SPENDS QUOTA
#   2. apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py  .csv         (57 key fields incl. distance)
#   3. data_pull_01.py              _data.csv    (+ tier, tier_source, sold_period)
#
# Stages 2 and 3 are offline and re-runnable: change a filter, re-run them, and
# the raw archive is untouched. Only stage 1 costs anything.
#
# Free plan = 100 requests/month. Each page is 1 call and returns 20 lots, so
# MAX_PAGES is a CAP, not a target — paging stops as soon as the cursor runs
# out, which makes over-estimating free and under-estimating lossy (a truncated
# pull is flagged loudly by stage 1).
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
PY="${PYTHON:-python}"

PLATFORM=iaai
MODE=ended
MAKE="Lexus"
MODEL="ES 350"
YEARS="2019-2023"
SINCE="2025-08-01"
SELLER="insurance"
MAX_PAGES=20
TIER=""            # empty -> stage 3 classifies per row via app/tier.py
GO=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --make)      MAKE="$2";      shift 2 ;;
    --model)     MODEL="$2";     shift 2 ;;
    --years)     YEARS="$2";     shift 2 ;;
    --since)     SINCE="$2";     shift 2 ;;
    --seller)    SELLER="$2";    shift 2 ;;
    --platform)  PLATFORM="$2";  shift 2 ;;
    --mode)      MODE="$2";      shift 2 ;;
    --max-pages) MAX_PAGES="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --tier)      TIER="$2";      shift 2 ;;
    --go)        GO=1;           shift ;;
    -h|--help)   sed -n '2,20p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

if [[ ! -f .env ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: no .env at $ROOT/.env — copy .env.example and set APIBARA_API_KEY" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "=============================================================================="
echo "  ${MAKE} ${MODEL}  ${YEARS}   ${PLATFORM}/${MODE}   seller=${SELLER}"
echo "  window: ${SINCE} .. today        page cap: ${MAX_PAGES}  (<= ${MAX_PAGES} API calls)"
echo "=============================================================================="

# --- stage 1: the only step that spends quota -------------------------------
# MAKE/MODEL are passed unquoted on purpose: pull_apibara_01.py takes nargs='+'
# for both, so "ES 350" survives as one value either way. Quoting them here is
# what actually matters -- word splitting happens in THIS shell, not in python.
PULL_ARGS=("$PLATFORM" "$MODE"
           --make "$MAKE" --model "$MODEL"
           --year-range "$YEARS"
           --auction-date-range "$SINCE"
           --seller "$SELLER"
           --max-pages "$MAX_PAGES")

if [[ $GO -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo
  echo "DRY RUN — no API calls. Re-run with --go to pull for real."
  echo
  "$PY" analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py "${PULL_ARGS[@]}" --dry-run
  echo
  echo "Then stages 2 and 3 would run:"
  echo "  $PY analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py <archive>"
  echo "  $PY analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py $PLATFORM <archive>${TIER:+ --tier $TIER}"
  exit 0
fi

echo
echo "About to spend up to ${MAX_PAGES} Apibara API call(s) of your monthly quota."
read -r -p "Continue? [y/N] " reply
[[ "$reply" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]] || { echo "Aborted — no calls made."; exit 0; }

echo
echo "### stage 1 — pull"
PULL_LOG="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$PULL_LOG"' EXIT
"$PY" analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py "${PULL_ARGS[@]}" | tee "$PULL_LOG"

ARCHIVE="$(grep -oE '  JSON -> .*\.json' "$PULL_LOG" | sed 's|  JSON -> ||' | tail -1)"
if [[ -z "$ARCHIVE" || ! -f "$ARCHIVE" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: could not determine the archive stage 1 wrote — stopping before" >&2
  echo "       stages 2/3 so nothing silently converts the wrong file." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo
echo "### stage 2 — flatten  ($(basename "$ARCHIVE"))"
"$PY" analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py "$ARCHIVE"

echo
echo "### stage 3 — filter + enrich"
"$PY" analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py "$PLATFORM" "$ARCHIVE" ${TIER:+--tier "$TIER"}

echo
echo "Done. Raw archive kept at:"
echo "  $ARCHIVE"
echo "Re-run stages 2/3 with different filters any time — they cost nothing."

```

*new_string*
```
# --make and --model swallow every following token up to the next --flag, so
# `--make Land Rover --model Range Rover Sport` works here exactly as it does in
# pull_apibara_01.py. Word splitting happens in bash long before python sees the
# arguments, so the python-side nargs fix alone would not cover this wrapper.
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --make)
      shift; MAKE=""
      while [[ $# -gt 0 && "$1" != --* ]]; do MAKE="${MAKE:+$MAKE }$1"; shift; done ;;
    --model)
      shift; MODEL=""
      while [[ $# -gt 0 && "$1" != --* ]]; do MODEL="${MODEL:+$MODEL }$1"; shift; done ;;
```
