## The runner: [analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh](analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh)

Defaults to exactly your target — 2019-2023 Lexus ES 350, IAAI, ended, insurance sellers, back to 2025-08-01:

```bash
./analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh              # DRY RUN — 0 API calls
./analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh --go         # pull for real
./analytics/scripts/run_pipeline.sh --tier 2 --go
```

It runs all three stages, capturing the archive path from stage 1 so stages 2 and 3 operate on *that* file rather than guessing "newest". Following `test/run_sold.sh`, it's **dry-run by default** and prompts before spending quota. If it can't determine which archive stage 1 wrote, it stops rather than silently converting the wrong file.

Overrides: `--make`, `--model`, `--years`, `--since`, `--seller`, `--platform`, `--mode`, `--max-pages`, `--tier`.

## One bug I introduced and fixed

My first version of the wrapper broke on `--make Land Rover` — bash splits arguments long before Python sees them, so the `nargs` fix in `pull_apibara_01.py` doesn't reach a shell script. The wrapper now swallows tokens up to the next `--flag` itself, so unquoted multi-word values work at both layers.

## Heads-up before you run it: ES 350 has no tier

`app/tier.py`'s want-list covers Audi S4/S5 and Lexus **IS300/IS350** — not the ES 350:

```
Lexus ES 350 2019 -> None
Lexus IS 350 2019 -> Tier 1
```

Without `--tier`, every row comes out `tier_source=auto:unclassified`. That's the classifier behaving correctly — it won't invent a tier it has no rule for — but it means you want either `--tier 2` (or 3) on the command, or an ES 350 entry added to `app/tier.py` if it belongs on the want-list permanently. I didn't guess a tier for it.

## Cost estimate

Unknown until you run it, but the ES 350 is a far more common car than the S5 (which gave 70 lots / 4 calls over the same window), so expect noticeably more pages. `--max-pages 20` caps it at 20 calls; paging stops early when the cursor runs out, and stage 1 shouts if it hits the cap with data remaining. If you'd rather scout first, `--max-pages 1 --go` costs one call and tells you whether more pages exist.

## A real bug this caught

The output path came out as `analytics/sold-data/analytics/sold-data/...`. The derived default filename is already a full path next to its input, but the code then prefixed `IN_DIR` again — so passing a repo-relative input path (exactly what the pull script prints as the "next:" hint) wrote into a nested duplicate directory. Present in both stage 2 and stage 3.

Fixed: only a user-supplied `--out` is resolved against `IN_DIR`. Stray directory removed, both stages re-run clean.

## Two things worth noting

**The distance decision held on new data.** 310/310 have `StorageLocationLatitude/Longitude` — now **464/464 across five pulls and two different models**. Removing the city-table fallback remains correct, and no missing-coordinate warning fired.

**Tier is unclassified, as predicted.** All 310 rows came out `tier_source=auto:unclassified`, because `app/tier.py` covers Lexus IS300/IS350 but not the ES 350. Two ways forward, your call:

- one-off label: re-run stage 3 with `--tier 2` (or 3) — free, no re-pull
- permanent: add an ES 350 rule to `app/tier.py`, which also makes `app/image_pipeline.py` file its photos under a real tier instead of `Unclassified`

Quota used this session: 16 here + 9 earlier probes = **25**. `run_pipeline.sh` is ready for next time — it does all three stages and captures the archive path automatically.

## The 4-cyl / 6-cyl split matters on this model

The IS 300 is the one car where your tier table already draws a distinction, and the data backs it — the split is clean and sizeable:

| | n | median sold | median ACV | sold/ACV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **4-cyl** (2.0T, RWD) | 145 | $7,050 | $24,043 | 0.29 |
| **6-cyl** (3.5 V6, AWD) | 33 | $5,950 | $24,332 | **0.24** |

Same ACV, but the V6 sells for ~$1,100 *less* — a 0.24 ratio against 0.29. Cylinder count maps perfectly onto drivetrain here (145 RWD / 33 AWD, 144 × 2.0L / 33 × 3.5L), so it's a genuine sub-model split rather than noise. On these numbers the V6 AWD is the better buy of the two, contrary to it being the tier-1 variant.

Worth treating as a lead rather than a finding: n=33 on the V6 side, and I haven't controlled for damage severity or mileage, either of which could explain the gap.

## Three models side by side

| model | n | median sold | median ACV | sold/ACV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lexus ES 350 | 310 | — | — | — |
| Lexus IS 350 | 128 | $11,912 | $37,634 | 0.33 |
| Lexus IS 300 | 178 | $6,762 | $24,069 | 0.29 |

```
def resolve_one(f):
    """Accept an absolute path, a path relative to the shell's cwd, or a bare
    filename living in analytics/sold-data/ (what pull_apibara_01 prints)."""
    p = Path(f)
    if p.is_absolute() or p.exists():
        return p
    if (IN_DIR / f).exists():
        return IN_DIR / f
    raise SystemExit(f"input not found: {f}\n  looked in ./{f} and {IN_DIR / f}")


def resolve_inputs(args):
    if args.files:
        return [resolve_one(f) for f in args.files]
    pool = sorted(IN_DIR.glob("*iaai*.json"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
    if not pool:
        raise SystemExit(f"no IAAI archives found in {IN_DIR} — run "
                         f"pull_apibara_01.py first")
    return pool if args.all else [pool[-1]]
```

*new_string*
```
def resolve_one(f):
    """Accept an absolute path, a path relative to the shell's cwd, or a bare
    filename living in any SEARCH_DIRS entry (what pull_apibara_01 prints)."""
    p = Path(f)
    if p.is_absolute() or p.exists():
        return p
    for d in SEARCH_DIRS:
        if (d / f).exists():
            return d / f
    looked = "\n    ".join(str(d / f) for d in SEARCH_DIRS)
    raise SystemExit(f"input not found: {f}\n  looked in ./{f}\n    {looked}")


def resolve_inputs(args):
    if args.files:
        return [resolve_one(f) for f in args.files]
    pool = sorted(IN_DIR.glob("*iaai*.json"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
    if not pool:
        raise SystemExit(f"no IAAI archives found in {IN_DIR} — run "
                         f"pull_apibara_01.py first")
    return pool if args.all else [pool[-1]]
```

```
1	"""
2	Stage 2 of the analytics pipeline — IAAI raw JSON -> analysis-ready CSV.
3	
4	    pull_apibara_01.py  ->  raw .json  ->  THIS SCRIPT  ->  .csv
5	                                              |
6	                                        data_pull_01.py  ->  + tier, sold_period
7	
8	This script owns everything derivable from the record alone, distance included.
9	`tier` and `sold_period` are NOT emitted here — tier takes an operator decision
10	per archive, so it belongs to data_pull_01.py.
11	
12	Reads the archives written by pull_apibara_01.py, flattens each IAAI record into
13	one row, and applies whatever filtering you ask for. No network, no API calls —
14	run it as often as you like, with different filters, against the same archive.
15	
16	KEY FIELDS ONLY — 57 columns, one per fact
17	------------------------------------------
18	Duplicates were removed after measuring them across a 70-lot pull, not by eye:
19	`vehicle_class` was identical to `body_style` on every row, `key_fob` to
20	`has_key`, `location_display` to `selling_branch`; `primary_damage_code`,
21	`acv_raw`, `est_repair_raw`, `body_style_name` and `runs_and_drives` were each
22	1:1 with a column that survived. Where a code and a description were 1:1 the
23	description won (codes like "AO"/"LR" mean nothing in a spreadsheet); where raw
24	text and a parsed number were 1:1 the number won ("$29,240 USD" does not sort);
25	where a boolean and a multi-valued field were 1:1 the multi-valued one won
26	(`run_condition` keeps IAAI's three run states, which a boolean flattens).
27	
28	`secondary_damage_code` is the exception that proves the rule, and the reason
29	every pair was measured rather than assumed. It looks like the twin of
30	`primary_damage_code` and is not: the primary code is strictly 1:1 with its
31	description (14 values, both 70/70), while the secondary code is populated on
32	40/70 against the description's 30/70. Those extra 10 rows carry "UK" — IAAI
33	inspected the car and recorded secondary damage as UNKNOWN, a state a blank
34	description cannot be distinguished from "nothing recorded at all". Dropping it
35	would have silently merged two different facts.
36	
37	Nothing is lost: every dropped field is still in the raw JSON archive, and
38	adding a column back is one line in SCHEMA plus a re-run — no API calls.
39	
40	    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py                # newest archive
41	    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py FILE.json ...  # specific ones
42	    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py --all          # every IAAI archive
43	
44	    --exclude-damage water,flood,fire   drop lots whose damage matches (OFF by default)
45	    --include-damage front,rear         keep ONLY lots whose damage matches
46	    --body-style coupe                  keep only these (repeatable/comma-separated)
47	    --exclude-body-style coupe          drop these
48	    --seller-class insurance            keep only these seller classes
49	    --min-photos 8                      drop thin listings
50	    --sold-only                         drop lots with no realised sale price
51	    --schema                            print the column mapping table and exit
52	
53	IAAI ONLY. A Copart converter will be a separate script, because the two payload
54	shapes are not variations of one schema — they are different schemas. Copart
55	records carry `details: None`, which removes ActualCashValue, EstimatedRepairCost,
56	body style, storage coordinates and the entire attributes block in one go. Nearly
57	half the columns below simply do not exist on a Copart lot, so a shared converter
58	would be mostly null-handling.
59	
60	SELLER CLASSIFICATION — READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE COLUMN
61	------------------------------------------------------------
62	IAAI masks seller identity on a meaningful slice of lots. Observed on a 68-lot
63	insurance-filtered pull: 12 records came back with
64	
65	    sale_information.SellerType = "******"    (literally asterisks)
66	    seller.name                 = "unknown"
67	    seller.type                 = "unknown"
68	
69	...while `attributes.Origin` said "Insurance" and `attributes.ProviderType` said
70	"INS" on all 68. The masking hides WHICH carrier, not WHETHER it is a carrier.
71	Reading SellerType naively classifies those 12 as non-insurance, which is simply
72	wrong — every one of them came from a `seller_type=insurance` server-side query.
73	
74	So `seller_class` cascades, most reliable source first. Which rule fired is not
75	a CSV column — it would be constant across a single-carrier pull — but every run
76	prints the full audit table, so the classification stays checkable.
77	`seller_name_masked` flags the anonymised ones so they can be excluded from
78	carrier-level analysis without being miscounted as dealers.
79	
80	IMAGE / VIDEO COLUMNS
81	---------------------
82	IAAI thumb URLs look like:
83	
84	    https://vis.iaai.com/resizer?imageKeys=46139013~SID~I1&width=400&height=300
85	                                           ^^^^^^^^        ^
86	                                           SalvageId       image key
87	
88	`iaai_image_url_prefix` keeps everything up to and including the trailing "I",
89	and `iaai_image_keys` collects the numeric suffixes as a pipe-joined array
90	(1|2|...|115|116) — the keys are NOT contiguous, they jump from ~11 to ~115, so
91	they cannot be regenerated from a count and must be stored. Rebuild any URL as:
92	
93	    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=845&height=633"      # large
94	    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=400&height=300"      # thumb
95	
96	Note the image key is `attributes.SalvageId`, which is NOT the lot number
97	(lot 45640490 -> SalvageId 46139013). Do not build image URLs from lot_number.
98
```

````
## Where files live

| folder | written by | contents | replaceable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sold-data/json-raw/` | stage 1 | untouched API responses | **No** — lots age out of Apibara's ~10-month window, so these are the only lasting copy |
| `sold-data/csv-raw/` | stage 2 | every lot in the archive, flattened | Yes — regenerate free from json-raw |
| `sold-data/csv-enriched/` | stage 3 | filtered + tier/sold_period | Yes — regenerate free |

Only the first is irreplaceable, which is the whole reason the layers are split:
back up `json-raw/`, and everything else can be rebuilt without touching the API.

`csv-raw/` means *unfiltered by definition*. Running stage 2 **with** filters
writes `_iaai_filtered.csv` instead of `_iaai.csv`, so a filtered run can never
overwrite the canonical extract. Persistent filtering belongs in stage 3.

Inputs are resolved by bare filename against `json-raw/` first, then the old flat
`sold-data/` and `sold-data-archive/`, so paths predating this layout still work.
````

Kitchen's clean. Zero API calls — everything here was filesystem work and offline re-runs.

## Layout

```
analytics/sold-data/
├── json-raw/       9 files   ← pull_apibara_01.py
├── csv-raw/        9 files   ← apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py
└── csv-enriched/   3 files   ← data_pull_01.py
```

**On the name:** I went with **`csv-enriched`** over `csv-filtered`. Stage 3 always *adds* columns (`tier`, `tier_source`, `sold_period`) but only *sometimes* filters — filtering is optional, enrichment isn't, so "filtered" names the accessory rather than the essence. `csv-curated` is the decent alternative if you prefer the connotation of human judgment. One-line change either way.

## Script changes

| script | reads | writes |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_apibara_01.py` | — | `json-raw/` |
| `apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py` | `json-raw/` | `csv-raw/` |
| `data_pull_01.py` | `json-raw/` | `csv-enriched/` |

Outputs now go to their folder **by destination, not by input location** — previously the default filename was derived next to the input file, so an archive passed by an odd path dragged its CSV along with it. Bare filenames still resolve: `json-raw/` is searched first, then the old flat `sold-data/` and `sold-data-archive/`, so any command or path you have from before still works.

## One thing I broke, and the flaw it revealed

While verifying stage 2 I re-ran it on the IS 350 archive and **overwrote your 2,305-byte filtered CSV** from Aug 12 with the full 128-row extract. It's regenerable in one command, but it was your file and I clobbered it.

The underlying flaw was worth more than the file: a *filtered* stage-2 run and an *unfiltered* one wrote the **same default filename**, so either could silently replace the other, leaving a CSV whose row count nobody could later explain. Now a filtered stage-2 run writes `_iaai_filtered.csv` and says so:

```
note: filters are active, so this is NOT the canonical csv-raw extract — writing
'_iaai_filtered' to keep the unfiltered file intact. Persistent filtering belongs
in csv-enriched/ via data_pull_01.py.
```

That makes `csv-raw/` mean *unfiltered by definition*, which is what gives the folder split its value.

## Backup boundary

The table in [analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) now states which layer is irreplaceable: **`json-raw/` only**. Lots age out of Apibara's ~10-month window, so those archives are the sole lasting copy — both CSV layers rebuild from them for free. If you ever add a backup or `.gitignore` rule, that's the line to draw.

`analytics/sold-data-archive/` I left untouched — it's yours, and it still resolves as a search path.

**One judgment call to flag:** I dropped `--auction-date-range`. Open lots auction in the *future*, so the `2025-08-01 → today` window your sold pulls use would have matched **zero** lots. Both results here are dated 2026-08-17/18 — next week.

I kept `--seller insurance` for comparability with your sold baseline. Dropping it would widen the net to dealer/other sellers, which for *buying* (rather than analysing) may be what you want — one flag away.

## The two lots

| | lot 45655991 | lot 45648652 |
|---|---|---|
| | 2019 S5 3.0T Premium, Sedan/Hatchback | 2018 S5 3.0T Premium Plus, **Convertible** |
| auction | Aug 17, Clearwater (FL) | Aug 18, Cleveland (OH) |
| damage | Front end, stationary | Rear, stationary |
| odometer | 40,359 mi | 47,511 mi |
| ACV | $37,152 | $30,797 |
| est. repair | $33,739 | $25,322 |
| **repair/ACV** | **0.91** | **0.82** |
| current bid | — | — |
| buy now | $7,400 | — |
| title | REBUILDABLE | SALVAGE |
| distance | 3,014 mi | 2,395 mi |

Both carry repair estimates at 82–91% of ACV — heavy hits, and both are non-runners. Against your sold data (median sold/ACV 0.33 for the S5 cohort), these are the kind of lots where the repair line eats the margin before transport from 2,400–3,000 miles is even counted. Worth running through `calculator.py` before treating the $7,400 buy-now as cheap.

## One thing the `open` mode exposes about the schema

Eight columns are empty on open lots, and the distinction matters:

- **structurally empty until the lot sells** — `last_sold_price_usd`, `last_sold_day`, `last_sold_status`, `sold_to_acv`
- **empty by coincidence** (n=2) — `secondary_damage`, `secondary_damage_code`, `iaai_video_url`
- **`current_bid_usd` is empty and shouldn't be assumed to stay that way** — these lots are pre-bid; it populates once bidding starts, which is exactly the field to watch if you re-pull closer to the sale date

So the CSV shape is identical across modes, but for open lots the *money* columns to read are `buy_now_usd` and `current_bid_usd`, not the `last_sold_*` family. Re-pulling this same query in a few days costs 1 call and would show bid movement — the newest-wins de-dupe in stage 3 already handles merging repeated pulls of the same lot.

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Bash**: Migrate files into data/{sold,open}/ layout</summary>

```bash
cd /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker/analytics && python3 - <<'PY'
import json, shutil
from pathlib import Path

OLD = Path("sold-data")
NEW = Path("data")
BUCKET = {"ended": "sold", "open": "open", "live": "open"}
LAYER = {"json-raw": "json-raw", "csv-raw": "csv-raw", "csv-enriched": "csv-cut"}

# stem -> bucket, learned from each archive's own `mode` field
mode_of = {}
for j in sorted((OLD / "json-raw").glob("*.json")):
    mode_of[j.stem] = BUCKET.get(json.loads(j.read_text()).get("mode", "ended"), "sold")

def bucket_for(path):
    stem = path.stem
    for suffix in ("_iaai_filtered", "_iaai", "_data"):
        if stem.endswith(suffix):
            stem = stem[: -len(suffix)]
            break
    if stem in mode_of:
        return mode_of[stem]
    return "open" if "_open_" in path.name or "_live_" in path.name else "sold"

moved = 0
for old_layer, new_layer in LAYER.items():
    for f in sorted((OLD / old_layer).glob("*")):
        if not f.is_file():
            continue
        dest_dir = NEW / bucket_for(f) / new_layer
        dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.move(str(f), str(dest_dir / f.name))
        moved += 1

# make sure every bucket/layer exists even when empty
for b in ("sold", "open"):
    for l in ("json-raw", "csv-raw", "csv-cut"):
        (NEW / b / l).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

print(f"moved {moved} file(s)")
PY
```

```
def resolve_inputs(args):
    """Explicit files, else the newest archive across both buckets.

    Auto-discovery spans sold/ and open/ so `--all` means every archive, not
    every archive of whichever bucket happened to be hardcoded.
    """
    if args.files:
        return [resolve_one(f) for f in args.files]
    pool = sorted((p for b in BUCKETS
                   for p in (DATA_DIR / b / "json-raw").glob("*iaai*.json")),
                  key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
    if not pool:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"no IAAI archives found under {DATA_DIR}/{{{'|'.join(BUCKETS)}}}"
            f"/json-raw — run pull_apibara_01.py first")
    return pool if args.all else [pool[-1]]
```

```
def load_records(paths):
    """-> [record], each tagged with its provenance."""
    out = []
    for p in paths:
        doc = json.loads(Path(p).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        plat = doc.get("platform")
        if plat and plat != "iaai":
            print(f"  !! skipping {Path(p).name}: platform={plat}, this "
                  f"converter is IAAI-only")
            continue
        pulled = doc.get("generated_at")
        n = 0
        for page in doc.get("pages", []):
            if page.get("status") != 200:
                continue
            for rec in (page.get("raw", {}).get("data") or []):
                rec["_source_file"] = Path(p).name
                rec["_pulled_at"] = pulled
                out.append(rec)
                n += 1
        print(f"  loaded {n:>4} record(s) from {Path(p).name}")
    return out
```

```
    # there too; an absolute one wins.
    out_dir = flat.layer_dir(records[-1].get("_mode", "ended"), "csv-cut")
```

*old_string*
````
```
pull_apibara_01.py           ->  sold-data/json-raw/*.json
        |                          stage 1 — the only thing that spends API quota
apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py  ->  sold-data/csv-raw/*_iaai.csv

data_pull_01.py {iaai|copart} ->  sold-data/csv-enriched/*_data.csv

```

## Where files live

| folder | written by | contents | replaceable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sold-data/json-raw/` | stage 1 | untouched API responses | **No** — lots age out of Apibara's ~10-month window, so these are the only lasting copy |
| `sold-data/csv-raw/` | stage 2 | every lot in the archive, flattened | Yes — regenerate free from json-raw |
| `sold-data/csv-enriched/` | stage 3 | filtered + tier/sold_period | Yes — regenerate free |

Only the first is irreplaceable, which is the whole reason the layers are split:
back up `json-raw/`, and everything else can be rebuilt without touching the API.

`csv-raw/` means *unfiltered by definition*. Running stage 2 **with** filters
writes `_iaai_filtered.csv` instead of `_iaai.csv`, so a filtered run can never
overwrite the canonical extract. Persistent filtering belongs in stage 3.

Inputs are resolved by bare filename against `json-raw/` first, then the old flat
`sold-data/` and `sold-data-archive/`, so paths predating this layout still work.
````
*new_string*
````
```
pull_apibara_01.py           ->  json-raw/*.json
        |                          stage 1 — the only thing that spends API quota
apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py  ->  csv-raw/*_iaai.csv
        |                          stage 2 — flatten + distance, 57 fields, unfiltered
data_pull_01.py {iaai|copart} ->  csv-cut/*_data.csv
                                   stage 3 — filter + tier + sold period
```

## Where files live

```
analytics/data/
├── sold/           lot_sub_status = ended        (auction history)
│   ├── json-raw/
│   ├── csv-raw/
│   └── csv-cut/
└── open/           lot_sub_status = open | live  (still biddable)
    ├── json-raw/
    ├── csv-raw/
    └── csv-cut/
```

| layer | written by | contents | replaceable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `json-raw/` | stage 1 | untouched API responses | **No** — lots age out of Apibara's ~10-month window, so these are the only lasting copy |
| `csv-raw/` | stage 2 | every lot in the archive, flattened | Yes — regenerate free from json-raw |
| `csv-cut/` | stage 3 | filtered + tier/sold_period | Yes — regenerate free |

Only `json-raw/` is irreplaceable, which is the whole reason the layers are
split: back that up and everything else rebuilds without touching the API.

**Bucketing is data-driven, not filename-driven.** Every archive records its own
`mode`, and each record is tagged `_mode` when loaded, so stages 2 and 3 write
into the same bucket their input came from — no path juggling, and an archive
moved by hand still converts into the right place. `open` and `live` share the
open bucket since both are still biddable; the filename keeps them apart
(`apibara_iaai_open_...` vs `_live_...`).

`csv-raw/` means *unfiltered by definition*. Running stage 2 **with** filters
writes `_iaai_filtered.csv` instead of `_iaai.csv`, so a filtered run can never
overwrite the canonical extract. Persistent filtering belongs in stage 3.

Bare filenames resolve against both `json-raw/` folders first, then the
pre-reorganisation trees, so older paths and commands still work.

### Reading open lots

The CSV shape is identical across buckets, but the money columns that matter
differ. On `open` lots the `last_sold_*` family and `sold_to_acv` are
structurally empty — nothing has sold yet — and the live figures are
`current_bid_usd` and `buy_now_usd`. `current_bid_usd` is also empty before
bidding opens, so re-pulling an open query closer to the sale date is how bid
movement gets captured; stage 3's newest-wins de-dupe merges repeat pulls of the
same lot automatically.
````

```
34	description cannot be distinguished from "nothing recorded at all". Dropping it
35	would have silently merged two different facts.
```

```
15	the ONLY copy of that window you will ever have, so it must be stored unfiltered
16	and unreshaped — a filter applied at pull time destroys data permanently, while
17	a filter applied at convert time costs nothing.

29	--max-pages is a CAP, not a target: paging stops as soon as the cursor runs out,
30	so overestimating is free while underestimating silently truncates the archive.
31	`--dry-run` prints the request URL and resolved params without spending a call.
```

## Bucketing is data-driven, not filename-driven

This is the part worth knowing. Every archive already records its own `mode`, so I used **that** rather than parsing filenames:

- **Migration** read `mode` out of each of the 10 archives to decide sold vs open — no guessing from `_ended_` / `_open_` substrings.
- **Stage 1** routes by `args.mode` → `data/{sold|open}/json-raw/`.
- **Stages 2 and 3** tag each record `_mode` at load time and write into the bucket their *input* came from.

So an archive converts into the correct place regardless of the path it was passed by — and if you ever move a file by hand, its CSV still lands correctly. The load line now shows the mode it detected:

```
loaded   70 record(s) from apibara_iaai_ended_audi_s5_..._20260810T133939.json  [ended]
   -> data/sold/csv-raw/..._iaai.csv
   -> data/sold/csv-cut/..._data.csv

loaded    2 record(s) from apibara_iaai_open_audi_s5_..._20260813T075100.json  [open]
   -> data/open/csv-raw/..._iaai.csv
   -> data/open/csv-cut/..._data.csv
```

## One decision I made for you

`lot_sub_status` has **three** values but you asked for two buckets. I mapped `live` → `open/`, since both are still biddable and only `ended` is history. The filename keeps them distinguishable (`apibara_iaai_live_...` vs `_open_...`). If you'd rather `live` had its own folder, it's one line in `MODE_BUCKET`.

`csv-enriched` → **`csv-cut`** everywhere, as asked.

Auto-discovery (`--all`, or no filename) now globs **both** buckets, so "newest archive" means newest overall rather than newest in whichever folder was hardcoded. Bare filenames still resolve — both `json-raw/` folders are searched first, then the old trees, so any command you have saved from before keeps working.

[analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) documents the tree, which layer is irreplaceable (`json-raw/` only — back that up and the rest rebuilds free), and a new note on reading open lots: `last_sold_*` and `sold_to_acv` are structurally empty there, and `current_bid_usd` / `buy_now_usd` are the live figures.

```
11

13	    python analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py iaai FILE.json ...       # specific ones
14	    python analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py iaai --all --tier 1      # every archive
15	    python analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py iaai --columns           # show the schema
16	
17	The platform argument selects which flattener to use. Each platform has its own,
18	because the payloads are different schemas rather than variants of one: Copart
19	records carry `details: None`, which removes ACV, repair estimate, body style and
20	storage coordinates in one go.
21	
22	    iaai    -> apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py
23	    copart  -> apibara_json2csv_copart_01.py   (not written yet)
24	
25	FILTERS (all opt-in, all inherited from the flattener)
26	------------------------------------------------------
27	    --exclude-damage water,flood,fire   drop lots whose damage matches
28	    --include-damage front,rear         keep ONLY lots whose damage matches
29	    --body-style coupe                  keep only these body styles
30	    --exclude-body-style coupe          drop these
31	    --seller-class insurance            keep only these seller classes
32	    --min-photos 8                      drop thin listings
33	    --sold-only                         drop lots with no realised sale price
34	
35	ADDED COLUMNS
36	-------------
37	`tier`            Want-list tier from app/tier.py. Because one archive is one
38	                  make/model, `--tier 1|2|3` sets it for the whole file. Left
39	                  off, each row is classified from make/model/year/engine, which
40	                  yields None for anything not on the want-list — so an explicit
41	                  --tier is the way to label a model the table does not know yet.
42	`tier_source`     `cli` or `auto`, so an override is never mistaken for a match.
43	`sold_period`     `YYYY-MM` of last_sold_day. Same convention as the month
44	                  folder in app/image_pipeline.py, so rows join to the photo
45	                  archive path.
46	
47	Distance USED to be computed here and now belongs to the flattener
48	(`distance_mi`, `distance_bucket`), because it needs no input from this stage:
```

## Routing verified in both directions

Stage 1 picks the folder from its two positional args:

```
iaai   ended -> sold/json-raw/iaai      copart ended -> sold/json-raw/copart
iaai   open  -> open/json-raw/iaai      copart open  -> open/json-raw/copart
```

Stages 2 and 3 read `platform` and `mode` **out of the archive itself** (each record now carries `_platform` alongside `_mode`), so outputs follow their input rather than a hardcoded path:

```
open archive  -> data/open/csv-raw/iaai/…_iaai.csv  -> data/open/csv-cut/iaai/…_data.csv
ended archive -> data/sold/csv-raw/iaai/…_iaai.csv  -> data/sold/csv-cut/iaai/…_data.csv
```

That's the same principle as before, extended one level: an archive moved by hand still converts into the right place, because the file describes itself.

## Two details worth knowing

**The `copart/` placeholders carry a `.gitkeep`.** Empty directories don't survive git or most archive tools, so without it the placeholders would silently vanish on the first clone or backup — and the structure you just asked for would half-exist.

**`copart` is wired end-to-end but stops with an explanation, not a crash.** `pull_apibara_01.py copart …` will happily write to `sold/json-raw/copart/` today, since the pull is platform-agnostic. It's only the converter that's missing, and it says so:

```
No flattener for 'copart': analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_copart_01.py does not exist yet.
  Copart needs its own because its payload has `details: None` — no ACV, no repair
  estimate, no body style, no branch coordinates.
```

So the folders aren't decorative — the moment `apibara_json2csv_copart_01.py` exists, the whole Copart path works with no other changes.

Auto-discovery now scans `data/{sold,open}/json-raw/iaai/`, and bare filenames still resolve through those first, then the parent layers and the pre-reorganisation trees — so saved commands keep working. [analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md](analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md) documents the three-axis tree.

Plus six lots with no repair estimate (ACV $10,312–$22,557).

## Reading it

**Every repair estimate is ≥ 0.69 of ACV** — this is a heavily-damaged cohort, and two are at or above 1.0, meaning IAAI's own estimate exceeds the car's value. Against your S5 sold data (median sold/ACV 0.33), the arithmetic is tight before transport from 1,000–3,000 miles enters the calculation.

**Bidding has barely opened.** Only 4 of 13 carry a bid, and three of those are the $25 floor. The four buy-now prices ($3,100 / $6,000 / $8,825 / $10,575) are the only real price signal today — `current_bid_usd` will populate as the sale dates approach, so a re-pull nearer Aug 17–21 costs 1 call and captures the actual movement.

**Two rows deserve a second look before trusting them:**

- the 2018 Sedan with **1 mile** on the clock and repair exactly equal to ACV ($17,655) — an odometer that's unread rather than genuine, and a repair figure that looks like a placeholder
- the **213k-mile** Coupe leading the table on ratio — the best r/ACV here (0.69) largely because the ACV is low, not because the damage is light

Mileage spread is wide (1 to 213k), so `repair_to_acv` alone won't rank these; it wants pairing with `odometer_mi` and `run_condition`. Six lots have no repair estimate at all, which on the sold data was a ~35% occurrence — so a blank there is normal, not a red flag.

```
### Response

**Correction on the premise:** Apibara's filter surface isn't thin — ~25 server-side params. Two
specific gaps hurt (no body style; include-only damage enum). And the constraint actually shaping
every decision isn't the filters — it's the **100-call budget**, which is the free tier, not the
product.

**Apibara plan tiers:**

| Plan | $/mo | Requests/mo | Rate | per_page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Test | $0 | **100** | 1/s | 20 |
| Basic | $25 | **30,000** | 1/s | 20 |
| Power | $50 | 60,000 | 3/s | 20 |
| Pro | $70 | 100,000 | 4/s | 20 |
| Pro+ | $90 | 300,000 | 4/s | 30 |
| Mega Max | $195 | 2,000,000 | 7/s | 40 |

$25 buys **300× the current quota**.

**The four compared:**

| | **Apibara** | **API Auctions** | **Rebrowser IAAI** | **Vehicle Databases** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sources | Copart + IAAI | Copart + IAAI + Emirates | **IAAI only** | NA salvage/insurance/dealer |
| Model | REST, per-call | REST, per-call/packs | **Bulk dataset** + scraper API | REST, per-VIN |
| Discovery search | ✅ ~25 filters | ✅ widest filter set | ✅ local (unlimited) | ❌ VIN only |
| Live bids | ✅ ~15s | ✅ active-lots endpoint | ⚠️ snapshot (~2d) | ❌ |
| Sale history | 1 call/VIN | **bundled in `get-cars`** | in dataset | ✅ full |
| Body style filter | ❌ | unverified | ✅ (80 fields) | returns it, no filter |
| Damage exclusion | ❌ | unverified | ✅ local | n/a |
| Filter by sold price | ❌ | ✅ `sale_price_from/to` | ✅ local | ❌ |
| Photos | thumbs | `get-original-photos` | ✅ | 10+/event |
| Pricing | **public** | packs/PAYG, not public | not public | not public |
| Scale | — | 20M records, 30k lots/day | 920k records, 80 fields | 80M records |

**API Auctions** returns *vehicles + full history in one call* via `POST /api/v2/get-cars`, and
supports `sale_price_from`/`sale_price_to`. Apibara can do neither. Paired-filter rule:
`auction_date_from` without `auction_date_to` returns 422.

**Rebrowser** sidesteps filtering entirely — 920k records, 80 fields, Parquet/CSV, filter in
pandas or SQL. Costs: **IAAI only**, ~2-day-old snapshots.

**Vehicle Databases** is VIN-enrichment only — no search, so no discovery.

**Recommendation:** pay Apibara **$25 first**, before adding any provider. Then API Auctions if
comps become the bottleneck. Rebrowser only if going analytics-heavy on IAAI. Skip Vehicle
Databases unless per-event photo sets matter. Each added source = another adapter + another entry
in the duplicated damage-mapping problem.
```

```bash
out, prev = [], None

        out.append(l); prev = l
```

```
The primary way to authenticate every v1 and v2 request is the
Authorization: Bearer <token>
header. As a legacy fallback for older integrations, the same token is also accepted as an
?api_token=<token>
query parameter — both forms are handled by the same middleware and resolve to the same account. Get your token from the dashboard; rotate it any time without downtime.
Store keys in your environment variables. Never commit them to source control or include them in client-side code.
```

```bash
import re
s = open('apiauctions.yaml').read()
# parameters for the two v2 listing endpoints
for path in ('/api/v2/get-cars', '/api/v2/get-active-lots'):
    i = s.find(f"  {path}:")
    if i < 0:
        print(f"{path}: NOT IN SPEC"); continue
    j = s.find("\n  /api/", i+5)
    block = s[i:j if j>0 else len(s)]
    names = re.findall(r"name:\s*'?([A-Za-z0-9_\[\]]+)'?", block)
    print(f"\n=== {path} — {len(names)} params ===")
    print(", ".join(names))
```

```
# API Auctions

> An independent REST API that indexes publicly listed lots from Copart, IAAI
> and Emirates Auction. Used by dealer storefronts, market analytics,
> VIN decoder products, and LLM agents.
> API Auctions is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by
> Copart, Inc., IAA, Inc. or Emirates Auction LLC.

## What this service is

API Auctions provides a developer-friendly HTTP/JSON interface to query
publicly listed auction lots and historical sales results. We index data that
is openly published by each auction site to attract buyers; we do not access
data behind authentication, member-only fields, or bidder identities.
Coverage includes ~10.4M records sourced from Copart public listings
(US, CA, FI), ~8.1M from IAAI public listings (US), and ~5M from
Emirates Auction (UAE).
New lots are typically indexed within 6 minutes of publication on the source
auction site. The service offers a REST API and an OpenAPI 3.1 specification.

## Authentication

All authenticated requests require an API token. The primary method is the
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` HTTP header. As a legacy fallback for older
integrations, the same token is also accepted as the `?api_token=<token>`
query-string parameter; both forms resolve to the same account. A free demo
token (10 requests / hour) is granted on sign-up at
https://apiauctions.io/register.
A payment method is required at signup to prevent abuse; the card is not
charged on the Free tier.

## Base URL

Production: https://apiauctions.io

The same host serves two concurrent versions:
- v2 (current production, POST, Bearer token) — under /api/v2/*
- v1 (POST, Bearer token)                     — under /api/v1/*
```

Got the docs (their WAF blocks the fetch tool's UA; the pages serve fine to a normal browser UA), plus the OpenAPI spec and `llms.txt`.

## Approach: different in four structural ways

| | Apibara | API Auctions |
|---|---|---|
| verb / auth | `GET`, `X-API-Key` header | **`POST`**, `Authorization: Bearer` |
| pagination | opaque **cursor**, `per_page` max **20** | **`page` + `per_page` max 100** |
| result size | **unknowable** — `meta` has no total | **`meta.total` + `last_page`** |
| sold vs open | one param, `lot_sub_status` | **two endpoints** — `get-cars` (sold+history) vs `get-active-lots` |

The pagination difference is the big one operationally. Your ES 350 pull cost 16 calls at 20/page; at 100/page that's **4**. And `meta.total` means you know the size *before* committing to page through — the exact thing I couldn't give you an estimate for earlier.

The sold/open split as separate endpoints maps cleanly onto the `data/{sold,open}/` layout you just built.

## Cost: the free tiers aren't comparable

- **Apibara Free**: 100 requests/**month**, hard ceiling.
- **API Auctions Free**: 10 requests/**hour** ≈ 7,200/month, all endpoints, card on file but $0 charged.

Paid inverts it: Apibara $25/mo = 30,000 requests (**$0.0008**/req); API Auctions PAYG **$0.01**/req, or $100 per 100k (**$0.001**), $250 per 1M (**$0.00025**). So Apibara is cheaper mid-tier, API Auctions cheaper at high volume — and dramatically more generous at $0.

## Data richness: Apibara wins on IAAI depth, decisively

The fields your pipeline is built on mostly **do not exist** at API Auctions:

| your column | Apibara (IAAI) | API Auctions |
|---|---|---|
| `acv_usd` | **100%** (686/686 measured) | ✗ — has `estimate_retail`, a *retail* estimate, not the insurer's ACV |
| `est_repair_usd` | 46–72% | ✗ |
| `seller_class` insurance/dealer | ✓ + **server-side filter** | ✗ no seller field, no filter |
| `run_condition` | ✓ 3 states | ✗ |
| `branch_lat/lng` | **100%** | ✗ — location is a string, `"FL — Tampa South"` |
| `body_style` | ✓ Sedan/Coupe/Convertible | ~ `car_info_vehicle_type` = `PASSENGER CAR`/`TRUCK` only |
| `cylinders`, `engine_raw` | ✓ on the lot | ✗ on the lot — needs a separate VIN-decode call |
| keys, airbags, grade, title brand/state | ✓ | ✗ |
| damage | ✓ positional | ✓ `primary_damage`/`secondary_damage` (history rows only) |

**That kills the `--seller insurance` filter and the whole ACV-anchored math.** Your max-bid model reads `clean_value` straight from IAAI's ACV at zero extra cost; API Auctions has no equivalent, so you'd be back to MarketCheck for pricing.

What it has that Apibara lacks: **`sale_price_from/to`** (filter sold price server-side — Apibara can't), **`created_at/updated_at` ranges** (incremental sync: pull only what changed since last run), **full trading history bundled in every row** (Apibara needs 1 call per VIN), `current_bid_from/to` and `buy_now_price_from/to` on active lots, and Copart Canada/Finland + Emirates.

## The unresolved question — and it's the one that matters

**History depth is nowhere in their docs.** No retention statement, no "since 20XX". Apibara documents ~10 months and delivers ~5.5 in practice — that wall is the single biggest limitation of your current archive. Their `10.4M + 8.1M` record counts *hint* at multi-year, and `auction_date_from` example values go back to `2023-01-01`, but that's inference, not evidence.

Two other things I could not verify from docs alone:

- **Response schemas are absent from the OpenAPI spec** — every response is just `200: 'OK - List of vehicles'`. My field list above comes from the docs' *example* responses, which are likely abridged. There may be more fields than shown.
- Whether `estimate_retail` is a usable clean-value proxy.

All three are answerable with a **free demo token** and ~3 calls: one `get-cars` for Audi S5 with `auction_date_from=2023-01-01`, read `meta.total`, and inspect one full row. That's the right next step before writing any code — it decides whether this is a *replacement* (if history is deep) or a *supplement* (if it isn't).

## Sketch for `pull_apiauctions_01.py`

Same three-stage shape, same `data/{sold,open}/json-raw/apiauctions/` layout, but:

- positional 2 becomes endpoint selection: `sold` → `get-cars`, `open` → `get-active-lots`
- `--seller` and `--cylinders` **drop** (no server equivalent); `--sale-price-range` and `--odometer-range` are added
- paging switches to `page`/`per_page=100`, and since `meta.total` exists, stage 1 can print "will need N pages" *before* spending them — a real improvement over the current `--max-pages` guess
- paired-parameter validation (`_to` requires `_from`, else 422) enforced client-side, same spirit as the enum validation we do for Apibara

Want me to grab a demo token and run those three probe calls first? On the free tier it costs nothing, and it would settle history depth before we commit to a design.

```
"""
API Auctions pull — stage 1, RAW JSON ONLY. Sibling of pull_apibara_01.py.

    pull_apiauctions_01.py  ->  raw .json  ->  (a json2csv stage, when written)

Same contract as the Apibara puller: build a server-side query, archive the
untouched responses, derive nothing. Output goes to the SAME tree, because the
folder axis is the auction house (iaai / copart), not the vendor:

    analytics/data/{sold|open}/json-raw/{iaai|copart}/apiauctions_*.json
                                                      ^^^^^^^^^^^
    the filename prefix is what separates vendors — apibara_* vs apiauctions_*

Run:

    python analytics/scripts/pull_apiauctions_01.py iaai open \
        --make Audi --model A5 --year-range 2018-2023 --max-pages 5

Token: APIAUCTIONS_API_TOKEN in the repo-root .env (see .env.example).
Free demo tier is 10 requests/HOUR — small, but per_page is 100, so one page
here carries what five Apibara pages do.

HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM APIBARA, AND WHY THE SCRIPT LOOKS DIFFERENT
-----------------------------------------------------------------
POST, not GET; `Authorization: Bearer` header, not `X-API-Key`. Beyond that,
three differences shape the code:

1. PAGE-BASED, WITH A TOTAL. Apibara hands out an opaque cursor and never says
   how many lots match, so `--max-pages` there is a guess. Here the first
   response carries `meta.total` and `meta.last_page`, so this script prints the
   real page count after ONE call and stops early rather than guessing. On a
   10-requests/hour tier that difference is the whole ballgame.

2. SOLD AND OPEN ARE DIFFERENT ENDPOINTS, not a status param:
       sold -> POST /api/v2/get-cars         (vehicles + full trading history)
       open -> POST /api/v2/get-active-lots  (live/scheduled, not yet sold)
   So the mode positional selects an endpoint, and the filter set legal for one
   is not legal for the other (see ENDPOINTS below).

3. PAIRED-REQUIRED RANGE FILTERS. Passing `*_to` without its `*_from` is a 422.
   That is validated here before spending a request, the same way the Apibara
   puller validates enums locally.

WHAT IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE (and is, on Apibara)
-----------------------------------------------
seller       No seller field and no seller filter. Apibara's
             `seller_type=insurance` — the filter every sold pull in this repo
             relies on — has no equivalent, so insurance and dealer lots come
             back mixed and cannot be told apart afterwards either.
body style   Only `car_info_vehicle_type` (PASSENGER CAR / TRUCK). Nothing that
             separates Coupe from Sedan.
ACV / repair The IAAI economics that make an Apibara row self-pricing
             (ActualCashValue, EstimatedRepairCost) are absent. There is
             `estimate_retail`, which is a retail estimate, NOT the insurer's
             cash value — do not treat them as the same number.
cylinders    Not on the lot; only via a separate /vin-decoding call.

WHAT IS AVAILABLE HERE (and is not, on Apibara)
-----------------------------------------------
sale_price_from/to      filter by realised sale price, server-side
created_at/updated_at   incremental sync — pull only what changed since a date
history[]               every row carries its own trading history, where Apibara
                        needs one /history call per VIN
per_page up to 100      vs 20
meta.total              know the result size before paging

Response schemas are NOT in their OpenAPI spec (every response is documented as
just "OK - List of vehicles"), so the field list above comes from the docs'
example responses and may be abridged. That is precisely what this script is
for: archive the real payload and look.
"""
import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ENV_PATH = ROOT / ".env"
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "analytics" / "data"

BASE = "https://apiauctions.io"
RATE_DELAY = 1.2                 # free tier is quota- not rate-bound; be polite
VENDOR = "apiauctions"           # filename prefix; folder stays the auction house

# mode -> (bucket folder, endpoint). Sold and open are different endpoints here,
# not two values of one status parameter.
ENDPOINTS = {
    "sold": ("sold", "/api/v2/get-cars"),
    "open": ("open", "/api/v2/get-active-lots"),
}

# platform -> exact `auction_name` value. From POST /api/v2/get-auctions:
# COPART, COPART CANADA, COPART FINLAND, IAAI, EMIRATES AUCTION.
AUCTION_NAMES = {"iaai": "IAAI", "copart": "COPART"}

# `*_to` requires its `*_from`, else the API answers 422. Checked locally so a
# malformed request never costs a request.
PAIRED = ("auction_date", "sale_price", "updated_at", "created_at",
          "estimate_retail", "odometer", "current_bid", "buy_now_price")

# Filters each endpoint accepts. get-active-lots has no sale_price/odometer
# (nothing has sold yet); get-cars has no current_bid/buy_now_price ranges.
COMMON = {"make", "model", "year_from", "year_to", "auction_name",
          "auction_date_from", "auction_date_to", "is_buy_now",
          "estimate_retail_from", "estimate_retail_to",
          "created_at_from", "created_at_to", "car_info_vehicle_type",
          "page", "per_page"}
ENDPOINT_PARAMS = {
    "/api/v2/get-cars": COMMON | {
        "sale_price_from", "sale_price_to", "odometer_from", "odometer_to",
        "updated_at_from", "updated_at_to"},
    "/api/v2/get-active-lots": COMMON | {
        "current_bid_from", "current_bid_to",
        "buy_now_price_from", "buy_now_price_to", "without_sale_date"},
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# env + transport
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def read_env_key(path=ENV_PATH, name="APIAUCTIONS_API_TOKEN"):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return ""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
                continue
            k, _, v = line.partition("=")
            if k.strip() == name:
                return v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return ""


def build_url(path, params):
    return f"{BASE}{path}?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True)


def post(token, path, params, form_body=False):
    """-> (status, payload, rate_headers).

    Their docs are inconsistent about where parameters travel: the curl examples
    put them on the query string of a POST with an empty body ("all parameters
    travel on the query string"), while the OpenAPI spec declares a required
    form-urlencoded body. Query string is tried first because that is what the
    documented examples do; main() retries once with a form body on a 422, and
    reports which shape worked so the next run can skip the retry.
    """
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json",
               "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    if form_body:
        url = f"{BASE}{path}"
        data = urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
    else:
        url = build_url(path, params)
        data = b""
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=45) as resp:
            body = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            return resp.getcode(), body, rate_headers(resp.headers)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        raw = e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
        except ValueError:
            body = {"error_body": raw[:600]}
        return e.code, body, rate_headers(e.headers)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return 0, {"error": str(e)}, {}


def rate_headers(headers):
    """X-RateLimit-* — worth surfacing on a 10-requests/hour tier."""
    out = {}
    for k in ("X-RateLimit-Limit", "X-RateLimit-Remaining", "X-RateLimit-Reset"):
        v = headers.get(k) if headers else None
        if v is not None:
            out[k] = v
    return out


def describe_rate(rl):
    if not rl:
        return ""
    left = rl.get("X-RateLimit-Remaining")
    limit = rl.get("X-RateLimit-Limit")
    reset = rl.get("X-RateLimit-Reset")
    bits = f"{left}/{limit} left" if left is not None else ""
    if reset:
        try:
            when = dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(int(reset)).strftime("%H:%M:%S")
            bits += f", resets {when}"
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    return f"   [rate: {bits}]" if bits else ""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def multiword(value):
    """nargs='+' -> one string, so `--model A5 Sportback` needs no quotes."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value.strip()
    return " ".join(str(x) for x in value).strip()


def parse_year_range(s):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d{4})\s*(?:[-:]\s*(\d{4}))?\s*", s or "")
    if not m:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"--year-range wants YYYY-YYYY or YYYY, got {s!r}")
    lo = int(m.group(1))
    hi = int(m.group(2) or m.group(1))
    if hi < lo:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"--year-range {lo}-{hi} is backwards")
    return lo, hi


def parse_date(s):
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(s.strip())
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"dates must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {s!r}") from None


def build_arg_parser():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="pull_apiauctions_01.py",
        description="Pull raw API Auctions JSON into "
                    "data/{sold|open}/json-raw/{iaai|copart}/apiauctions_*.json",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="Free demo tier: 10 requests/HOUR. per_page is 100, and the "
               "first response reports meta.total, so the run prints the real "
               "page count instead of guessing.")
    ap.add_argument("platform", choices=list(AUCTION_NAMES), type=str.lower)
    ap.add_argument("mode", choices=list(ENDPOINTS), type=str.lower,
                    help="sold -> /get-cars (history), open -> /get-active-lots")
    ap.add_argument("--make", nargs="+", metavar="MAKE")
    ap.add_argument("--model", nargs="+", metavar="MODEL")
    ap.add_argument("--year-range", type=parse_year_range, metavar="YYYY-YYYY")
    ap.add_argument("--auction-date-range", nargs="+", type=parse_date,
                    metavar="YYYY-MM-DD",
                    help="one date = today..that date; two = from..to")
    ap.add_argument("--sale-price-range", nargs=2, type=int,
                    metavar=("FROM", "TO"), help="sold only")
    ap.add_argument("--odometer-range", nargs=2, type=int,
                    metavar=("FROM", "TO"), help="sold only")
    ap.add_argument("--auction-name",
                    help=f"override the exact auction name "
                         f"(default: {AUCTION_NAMES})")
    ap.add_argument("--per-page", type=int, default=100,
                    help="max 100 (default 100)")
    ap.add_argument("--max-pages", type=int, default=5,
                    help="page cap; EACH PAGE IS ONE REQUEST (default 5). "
                         "Paging stops at meta.last_page on its own")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="output basename or path")
    ap.add_argument("--form-body", action="store_true",
                    help="send params as a form body instead of query string")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                    help="print the resolved request, make no call")
    return ap


def resolve_params(args, endpoint):
    p = {"page": 1, "per_page": min(max(args.per_page, 1), 100)}
    name = args.auction_name or AUCTION_NAMES[args.platform]
    p["auction_name"] = name
    if args.make:
        p["make"] = multiword(args.make)
    if args.model:
        p["model"] = multiword(args.model)
    if args.year_range:
        p["year_from"], p["year_to"] = (str(y) for y in args.year_range)
    if args.auction_date_range:
        d = args.auction_date_range
        if len(d) > 2:
            raise SystemExit("--auction-date-range takes one or two dates")
        lo, hi = sorted([dt.date.today(), d[0]] if len(d) == 1 else list(d))
        p["auction_date_from"], p["auction_date_to"] = lo.isoformat(), hi.isoformat()
    if args.sale_price_range:
        p["sale_price_from"], p["sale_price_to"] = sorted(args.sale_price_range)
    if args.odometer_range:
        p["odometer_from"], p["odometer_to"] = sorted(args.odometer_range)

    allowed = ENDPOINT_PARAMS[endpoint]
    bad = sorted(k for k in p if k not in allowed)
    if bad:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{', '.join(bad)} not accepted by {endpoint} — that endpoint takes "
            f"{', '.join(sorted(allowed))}")
    for stem in PAIRED:
        lo, hi = f"{stem}_from" in p, f"{stem}_to" in p
        if lo != hi:
            raise SystemExit(
                f"{stem}_from/{stem}_to must be passed together (the API "
                f"answers 422 otherwise)")
    return p


def default_basename(args, params):
    bits = [VENDOR, args.platform, args.mode]
    bits += [multiword(x).lower().replace(" ", "-")
             for x in (args.make, args.model) if x]
    if args.year_range:
        bits.append(f"{args.year_range[0]}-{args.year_range[1]}")
    if "auction_date_from" in params:
        bits.append(f"{params['auction_date_from']}_{params['auction_date_to']}")
    bits.append(dt.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S"))
    return "_".join(bits)


def resolve_out_path(args, params):
    bucket, _ = ENDPOINTS[args.mode]
    out_dir = DATA_DIR / bucket / "json-raw" / args.platform
    if args.out:
        p = Path(args.out)
        return (p if p.is_absolute() else out_dir / p).with_suffix(".json")
    return (out_dir / default_basename(args, params)).with_suffix(".json")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def summarize(records):
    """Coverage report, and a field census — the point of a first contact is
    finding out what the payload actually carries."""
    if not records:
        print("  no records returned")
        return
    keys, filled = {}, {}
    for r in records:
        for k, v in r.items():
            keys[k] = keys.get(k, 0) + 1
            if v not in (None, "", [], {}):
                filled[k] = filled.get(k, 0) + 1
    n = len(records)
    print(f"\n  records: {n}")
    print(f"  fields per record: {len(keys)}")
    print(f"  {'field':<28} filled")
    for k in sorted(keys, key=lambda k: (-filled.get(k, 0), k)):
        example = next((r[k] for r in records
                        if r.get(k) not in (None, "", [], {})), "")
        if isinstance(example, (list, dict)):
            example = f"<{type(example).__name__} len={len(example)}>"
        print(f"    {k:<28} {filled.get(k, 0):>3}/{n}   {str(example)[:52]}")


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.max_pages < 1:
        raise SystemExit("--max-pages must be >= 1")

    bucket, endpoint = ENDPOINTS[args.mode]
    params = resolve_params(args, endpoint)
    out_path = resolve_out_path(args, params)

    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"API AUCTIONS — {args.platform.upper()} / {args.mode}  ->  {endpoint}")
    print(f"  params:  {params}")
    print(f"  budget:  up to {args.max_pages} request(s), {params['per_page']}/page")
    print("=" * 78)

    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"\n  DRY RUN — no call made.\n  POST {build_url(endpoint, params)}")
        print(f"  would write -> {out_path}")
        return 0

    token = read_env_key()
    if not token:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"No APIAUCTIONS_API_TOKEN in {ENV_PATH}\n"
            f"  Add a line:  APIAUCTIONS_API_TOKEN=your_demo_token\n"
            f"  Get one at https://apiauctions.io/register (free tier).")

    out = {
        "generated_at": dt.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "argv": argv,
        "vendor": VENDOR,
        "platform": args.platform,
        "mode": args.mode,
        "endpoint": endpoint,
        "server_params": params,
        "pages": [],
    }
    records, calls, form_body = [], 0, args.form_body
    last_page = None

    while calls < args.max_pages:
        page_params = dict(params, page=len(out["pages"]) + 1)
        code, data, rl = post(token, endpoint, page_params, form_body)
        calls += 1

        # one automatic retry in the other parameter shape — their docs and
        # their OpenAPI spec disagree about which is correct
        if code == 422 and not form_body and calls == 1:
            print(f"  page 1: HTTP 422 on query-string params — retrying once "
                  f"as a form body{describe_rate(rl)}")
            form_body = True
            code, data, rl = post(token, endpoint, page_params, form_body)
            calls += 1

        out["pages"].append({"status": code, "params": page_params,
                             "form_body": form_body, "rate": rl, "raw": data})
        if code != 200:
            print(f"\n  HTTP {code}: {json.dumps(data)[:500]}{describe_rate(rl)}")
            if code == 401:
                print("  -> token missing/invalid")
            elif code == 402:
                print("  -> quota exhausted for this tier")
            elif code == 422:
                print("  -> parameters rejected in BOTH shapes; check the "
                      "paired *_from/*_to rules and endpoint-specific filters")
            break

        rows = data.get("data") or []
        records.extend(rows)
        meta = data.get("meta") or {}
        total, last_page = meta.get("total"), meta.get("last_page")
        page_no = meta.get("page", len(out["pages"]))
        print(f"  page {page_no}: {len(rows)} lot(s)"
              f"   total={total} last_page={last_page}"
              f"   [{'form' if form_body else 'query'}]{describe_rate(rl)}")

        # The whole advantage over a cursor API: after ONE call we know the size
        if page_no == 1 and last_page:
            need = min(last_page, args.max_pages)
            print(f"    -> {total} lot(s) across {last_page} page(s); this run "
                  f"will fetch {need}"
                  + ("" if last_page <= args.max_pages else
                     f" and STOP SHORT (raise --max-pages to {last_page})"))
        if not rows or (last_page and page_no >= last_page):
            break
        time.sleep(RATE_DELAY)

    truncated = bool(last_page and len(out["pages"]) < last_page)
    if truncated:
        print(f"\n  *** TRUNCATED at --max-pages {args.max_pages} of "
              f"{last_page} page(s) ***")

    out["counts"] = {"records": len(records), "calls_used": calls,
                     "truncated": truncated, "last_page": last_page}
    summarize(records)

    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print(f"Done. {calls} request(s) used.")
    print(f"  JSON -> {out_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```
     &make=Audi&model=A5&year_from=2018&year_to=2023
-> data/open/json-raw/iaai/apiauctions_iaai_open_audi_a5_2018-2023_<ts>.json
```

## Design notes worth flagging

**Same folder, different filename prefix.** Output lands in the existing `data/open/json-raw/iaai/` — the folder axis is the *auction house*, not the vendor, so `apibara_*` and `apiauctions_*` files sit side by side and stay directly comparable. No structure change needed.

**Sold/open are different endpoints here**, not a status param — so the mode positional picks the endpoint, and I enforce each endpoint's legal filter set locally. Asking for a sold-only filter on the open endpoint fails instantly rather than burning a request on a 422:

```
sale_price_from, sale_price_to not accepted by /api/v2/get-active-lots
```

Same for the paired-range rule (`*_to` without `*_from` = 422): checked before any request goes out.

**One thing I couldn't resolve from the docs, so the script handles both.** Their curl examples put parameters on the **query string** of a POST with an empty body ("all parameters travel on the query string"), while their OpenAPI spec declares a **required form-urlencoded body**. The script tries query-string first and, on a 422, retries once as a form body — then reports which shape worked (`[query]` or `[form]`) so we know for next time. Costs at most one extra request on first contact.

**`meta.total` gets used properly.** After page 1 it prints the true result size and page count, and says explicitly if `--max-pages` will cut the run short — the thing Apibara's cursor can never tell us.

**No `--seller` flag**, deliberately. There's no seller field at API Auctions, so insurance and dealer lots come back mixed *and can't be separated afterwards either*. You said that's fine for this test; just don't compare the row count against your `--seller insurance` Apibara pulls as if they were the same population.

The run also prints a **field census** — every key, fill rate, and a sample value — since their spec documents no response schema. That's what will actually answer whether `estimate_retail` is usable and how deep `history[]` goes.

**Yes — 100 lots per request vs Apibara's 20**, a hard 5× difference in rows-per-call. Their docs: `per_page · default 10 · max 100`; Apibara caps at 20 on every plan below $90/mo. Concretely, your 310-lot ES 350 pull cost **16 Apibara calls**; the same result set here would be **4 requests**.

Two caveats before you bank on it:

- Apibara's free tier is 100 requests/**month**; API Auctions' is 10/**hour**. So the *per-request* efficiency gain compounds with a very different quota shape — you can't do a 16-page pull here in one go, but you can do 10 requests every hour indefinitely.
- 100 rows/page doesn't mean 100 *usable* rows. Without ACV, repair estimate, or seller type, an API Auctions row carries far less than an Apibara IAAI row. More rows, thinner rows.

## On the token — one thing to flag

It's present in `.env`: **16 characters**, starting `sk_`. That's short for an API token and the `sk_`prefix is a Stripe-style convention. Their docs describe Bearer tokens from the dashboard, and their v1 spec references Laravel Sanctum tokens, which normally look like `123|longRandomString…` — 40+ chars with a pipe. This doesn't match that shape.

It may well be fine — plenty of services issue short opaque keys. But if it was copied from an "Overview" page it could be a *publishable/account* identifier rather than the API token. Worth a glance at the dashboard for a field explicitly labelled API token / Bearer token before we spend requests.

**The dry-run cannot validate it** — it makes no network call by design, so it proves the request is well-formed, not that the credential works. Only a real call settles that, and a bad token returns `401` (which the script reports explicitly, costing 1 of your 10/hour).

That settles it — what's in `.env` is the **display prefix**, not the key. Their own page says it: *"The full value is shown only at creation; afterwards just a stable prefix is visible."* The `…` after `sk_live_fd0c36fb` is literal truncation in the UI, and 16 chars is exactly `sk_live_` + 8 hex.

There's no way to recover the original — that's the point of showing it once. **Click Rotate** on the `api_token` row (their docs: two clicks, zero downtime), copy the full value from the creation dialog immediately, and replace the line in `.env`:

```
            f"  Get one at https://apiauctions.io/register (free tier).")

    # The dashboard lists keys by a truncated PREFIX ("sk_live_fd0c36fb…") and
    # shows the full value only once, at creation. Copying from the key list
    # therefore yields something that looks like a key but can only ever 401 —
    # and on a 10-requests/hour tier, finding that out the expensive way costs a
    # tenth of the hourly budget. Refuse the obvious prefix shape instead.
    if re.fullmatch(r"sk_(live|test)_[0-9a-f]{8}", token):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"APIAUCTIONS_API_TOKEN looks like the dashboard's display PREFIX, "
            f"not a full key ({len(token)} chars).\n"
            f"  The full value is shown only at creation — it cannot be "
            f"re-read from the key list.\n"
            f"  Fix: https://apiauctions.io/api-keys -> Rotate -> copy the full "
            f"value from the dialog.\n"
            f"  Override with --skip-token-check if their keys really are this "
            f"short.")
```

Two findings from one request, and the second is the blocker.

**1. The UA fix works** — with a proper `User-Agent` we reach their app (402, not Cloudflare's 403).

**2. `402: "No active tariff found."`** — your token authenticates fine (not 401), but the account has **no active plan attached**. Their docs list Free as `$0/mo · 10 requests/hour · card required ($0 charged)` — and you weren't asked for a card, which fits: the Free tier looks like it needs explicit activation rather than coming automatically with signup.

```
VENDOR = "apiauctions"           # filename prefix; folder stays the auction house

# REQUIRED. apiauctions.io sits behind Cloudflare with "browser signature"
```

## Where it stands

| step | status |
|---|---|
| Cloudflare edge | ✅ passes with a proper `User-Agent` |
| token / auth | ✅ valid — a bad token returns 401, we get past that |
| request shape | ✅ query-string params accepted, no 422 |
| rate limiter | ✅ live: `X-RateLimit: 58/60 left` |
| **plan** | ❌ `402 — "No active tariff found."` |

**Your account has no tariff attached.** The token authenticates, the rate limiter is even tracking you (58/60), but the billing layer refuses every call because no plan — not even Free — is active. That matches your note that no card was requested: signup created the account and key, but the Free plan was never activated.

Interesting detail: the rate-limit header says **60**, not the 10/hour their docs advertise for Free. So the limiter is running on some default while the tariff check fails independently.

**To fix:** in the dashboard, find Billing / Plans / Subscription and activate **Free ($0/mo, 10 req/hour)**. Their `llms.txt` says a card is required at signup for Free with $0 charged — since you weren't asked, the card step is probably what's waiting on the plan page. If it demands a card you'd rather not add, that's a fair place to stop; we'd have learned what we can without it.

## Two fixes now in the script

**`User-Agent` header** — required, not cosmetic. apiauctions.io runs Cloudflare with browser-signature blocking, and urllib's default `Python-urllib/3.12` is on the banned list, so it was rejected at the edge before the API or your token was ever consulted. It now identifies as `car-bid-tracker/1.0` — honest naming rather than impersonating a browser.

**Diagnostic messages** for both failure modes, so neither costs a puzzled request next time: the 402 now explains the tariff-vs-quota distinction, and a 403/1010 explains the UA cause.

I dug into it, and the answer is: **the demo token isn't a separate key you can go fetch — and that's exactly why this needs support.**

## What the docs say

| source | claim |
|---|---|
| Docs quickstart, step 1 | *"Grab a demo token — Sign up, **we drop a demo token into your dashboard. No credit card.**"* |
| "Get demo token" button | links to `/register` — plain signup, nothing else |
| Reference-dictionary section | *"**Demo (Free) tokens** cannot call these and will get 402"* |
| `llms.txt` | *"Free: $0/mo · 10 requests/hour · **card required** ($0 charged)"* |

So "demo token" and "Free-tier token" are **the same thing** — one key whose capability depends on the tariff attached to the account. There's no separate demo key to obtain, and no self-serve way to mint one: the demo tariff is supposed to be provisioned automatically at signup.

Note the docs contradict themselves on the card (`No credit card` vs `card required`), and neither version matches what you got: a key with **no tariff at all**.

Also telling — that same section says demo tokens get `402` only on the **paid-only reference dictionaries** (`get-makes`, `get-models`, …). We called `/api/v2/get-active-lots`, a core endpoint a demo token should reach. Getting 402 there means the account has *no* tariff, not that we hit a demo restriction.

## One hypothesis worth putting in the note

Your dashboard displayed the original key as `sk_live_fd0c36fb…`, but the key issued by **Rotate** is `4629|…` — a Laravel Sanctum `id|hash` token, a completely different format. It's plausible the auto-provisioned demo token carried the demo tariff binding, and rotating it minted a fresh `live`-env key without one. Can't verify from outside, but it's specific and actionable for them.
