- **(ii)** `--seller {insurance|dealer}` only. Documented that the two are not complements —
  **omit `--seller` entirely to get all sellers**, do not pass both.
- **(iii)** `--engine-type` replaced by `--cylinders {1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12}`. Note the enum has
  **no 7, 9 or 11** — taken verbatim from `/vehicles/filters`.
- **(iv)** modes are now `{open|live|ended}` mapping to `lot_sub_status` `Open|Live|Ended`.
""")

add(6, "how does the damage filter work? example run; how many calls?", """
#### How the client-side damage filter works

It is **not** a server-side param and cannot be. Apibara's `damage` filter is an **include-only
whitelist** whose enum is `Fire / Hail / Theft / Water / Chemical / Rollover / Mechanical /
Vandalized / Repossession` — it cannot express **collision damage, which is ~80% of lots**, and
there is no negation param.

So it runs at the json2csv stage: raw JSON is archived unfiltered, and the filter drops rows on
the way to CSV. No calculated field, no effect on the archive.

#### Example

```bash
python analytics/scripts/pull_apibara_01.py iaai ended \\
    --make Audi --model S5 --year-range 2018-2023 \\
    --auction-date-range 2025-08-01 2026-08-09 --seller insurance --max-pages 20
```

#### Call estimate

20 lots per page, 1 call per page. An Audi S5 IAAI ended pull over a year is roughly 60-80 lots
→ **3-4 calls**. `--max-pages` is a cap, not a target: paging stops when the cursor runs out, so
overestimating is free while underestimating silently truncates.
""")

add(7, "first run produced 6 months only; can we see terminal output?", """
#### On seeing your terminal

**No, I cannot see the VS Code terminal.** I only see output from commands I run myself. Paste
it, or write it to a file I can read — `tmp-terminal.txt` works well and you used that after.

#### The 6-month wall

Apibara's docs say the active database holds roughly the last **~10 months**; the S5 pull reached
only **~5.5 months** back. Lots age out. That single fact set the architecture:

> A raw archive pulled today is the ONLY copy of that window you will ever have.

Which is why stage 1 archives **unfiltered and unreshaped** — a filter applied at pull time
destroys data permanently, a filter applied at convert time costs nothing.

#### Restructure into stages (your i-vi)

- **(i)** removed the client-side damage filter from the puller — raw JSON only
- **(ii)** **Artifact: created `analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md`**, generated from the
  `SCHEMA` list so code and doc cannot drift
- **(iii)** CSV writing removed from `pull_apibara_01.py`
- **(iv)** **Artifact: created `analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py`** — 57 columns
- **(v)** added `iaai_image_url_prefix` + `iaai_image_keys`. The keys are **not contiguous** —
  they jump from ~11 to ~115 — so they cannot be regenerated from a count and must be stored
- **(vi)** added two video columns, dropped vr360 from the CSV (kept in JSON)
""")

add(8, "review both scripts; single-date range produced 0 rows; verify insurance", """
#### (a) The single-date bug

`--auction-date-range 2025-08-01` produced `from=2026-08-10, to=2025-08-01` — inverted. An
inverted range is **not an error to the API**; it silently matches almost nothing.

```python
lo, hi = sorted([dt.date.today(), d[0]] if len(d) == 1 else list(d))
```

#### (b) The insurance check found a real classification bug

The pull used `--seller insurance`, yet 12 lots were being classified `dealer`. Cause:

```
sale_information.SellerType = "******"    (literally asterisks)
seller.name                 = "unknown"
attributes.Origin           = "Insurance"   <- on all 68
attributes.ProviderType     = "INS"
```

**IAAI's masking hides WHICH carrier, not WHETHER it is a carrier.** Reading `SellerType`
naively classified 12 insurance lots as dealers.

Rewrote `seller_class()` to cascade most-reliable-source-first, starting from
`attributes.Origin` / `ProviderType`. Added `seller_name_masked` so anonymised lots can be
excluded from carrier-level analysis without being miscounted.
""")

add(9, "create a slim iaai_pull_01.py with duplicates removed", """
**Artifact: created `analytics/scripts/iaai_pull_01.py`.**

Duplicates were removed **by measurement across a 70-lot pull, not by eye**:

```
vehicle_class      == body_style        on every row
key_fob            == has_key
location_display   == selling_branch
primary_damage_code, acv_raw, est_repair_raw, body_style_name, runs_and_drives
                   each 1:1 with a column that survived
```

Tie-break rules: description beats code (`AO`/`LR` mean nothing in a spreadsheet), number beats
raw text (`"$29,240 USD"` does not sort), multi-valued beats boolean (`run_condition` keeps
IAAI's three run states, a boolean flattens them).

**The exception that justified measuring rather than assuming:** `secondary_damage_code` looks
like the twin of `primary_damage_code` and is not. Primary code is strictly 1:1 with its
description (14 values, both 70/70); secondary code is populated on **40/70** against the
description's **30/70**. Those extra 10 rows carry `UK` — IAAI inspected the car and recorded
secondary damage as UNKNOWN, which a blank description cannot be distinguished from "nothing
recorded at all". Dropping it would have silently merged two different facts.
""")

add(42, "TimedAuction = BID NOW; more detail; what happened to the vanished lots?", """
#### You are right about BID NOW

Verified the mechanism: the server-side HTML ships generic `Pre-Bid` text and the token
`TimedAuction`; the **BID NOW label is swapped in client-side** once the timed window is open. So
we *had* captured it, under IAAI's internal name.

#### The vanished lot: not accessible

`/VehicleDetail/45747871~US` returns **HTTP 200** — but it is a soft 404:
`DetailsNotFoundView`, 115 KB, no `ProductDetailsVM` (a live lot is ~360 KB). **Status code tells
you nothing**; absence of the view-model is the signal. Added explicit handling.

**The web source has no history whatsoever.** Once a lot leaves search, its final state is gone.

#### Three new columns

```
lot 45662018  auction_at 2026-08-21 16:30   timed_close_at   2026-08-15 01:53   (-6 days)
lot 45704693  auction_at 2026-08-21 13:30   buy_now_close_at 2026-08-21 01:00   (-12 hours)
```

`buy_now_sold` is the important one — IAAI sets it **while the lot is still listed**, so a
buy-now sale is catchable on the pull *before* the disappearance.

#### History design — three options

Proposed **A (compute from archives) with C's artifact as an optional cache**, over B (a
persistent ledger). The hard part is not detecting change but that **absence is only meaningful
within a comparable cohort** — and truncated snapshots cannot prove absence at all.

```

market excludes the tenant    -> cannot prove absence
keywords exclude the lot      -> cannot prove absence

by damage: Rear 9, Left side 8, Right side 4, Left rear 3, Roof 1, Right rear 1, Theft 1

#### A leak worth catching

`--market us` cannot retroactively clean archives written before it existed, and `--history`
widens across them — so **two Canadian lots reappeared** in a US-only analysis. Added `--market`
as a *cut-level* filter.

**`--dry-run` was mutating the filesystem** — renaming is a side effect of resolving a folder.
Fixed via `apply=False`, verified by hashing the directory listing either side.

What I cannot fully account for: during that sequence lot 45490663's folder and the manifest's
first 7 rows disappeared. The folder logic tests clean in a sandbox. I re-pulled the lot and
hardened the manifest, but I would rather say I lack a complete explanation than invent one.

Idempotency now proven: `0 downloaded, 441 already present`.

add(59, "group primary and secondary damage into REAR-SIDE / FRONT / OTHER", """
Added `primary_damage_group` and `secondary_damage_group` as **stage-2** columns, so they are in
csv-raw and flow to csv-cut. All 2,217 rows regenerated.

```
primary_damage_group    FRONT 1200   REAR-SIDE 635   OTHER 171   blank 211
secondary_damage_group  blank 1410   REAR-SIDE 363   FRONT 262   OTHER 182
```

#### One thing that would have silently broken this

**The two fields do not use the same casing.** Primary writes `Front end` / `Left side`;
secondary writes `Front End` / `Left Side`, and carries values primary never does
(`Left & Right Side`). A literal lookup would have grouped primary correctly and dumped nearly
all of secondary into OTHER without complaint. Matching is case- and spacing-insensitive.

#### Blank stays blank

`secondary_damage` is empty on **1,410 of 2,217 rows** — folding those into OTHER would make the
column read as though most lots had exotic damage. Two different facts.

**One value for your call:** a bare **`Front`** (1 lot) is in OTHER, since your list has
`Front End` and `Front & Rear` but not `Front` alone.
""")

````
"""Rebuild the .cc-discussion log as a VERBATIM copy of the chat.

No summarising. User prompts, assistant output, tool calls and tool results are
copied exactly as they appear in the session JSONL.

Thinking blocks are present in the log (357 of them) but their text is EMPTY —
only a cryptographic signature is persisted. They are emitted as explicit
placeholders rather than reconstructed, because reconstructing them would mean
inventing a record of reasoning that was never saved.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import re

T = ("/home/striker/.claude/projects/-home-striker-projects-car-bid-tracker/"
     "1de5f512-27cc-4a6f-a0ee-152360548399.jsonl")
OUT = pathlib.Path("/home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker/.cc-discussion/"
                   "Build analytics pipeline script from test files.md")

SKIP_TYPES = {"queue-operation", "ai-title", "last-prompt", "mode",
              "file-history-snapshot", "file-history-delta", "attachment", "system"}

NOISE = re.compile(
    r"<(system-reminder|ide_selection|ide_opened_file|local-command-stdout|"
    r"local-command-caveat|command-name|command-message|command-args)>.*?</\1>",
    flags=re.S)


def fence(text, lang=""):
    """Fence that cannot be broken by backticks inside the payload."""
    text = "" if text is None else str(text)
    bt = "```"
    while bt in text:
        bt += "`"
    return f"{bt}{lang}\n{text}\n{bt}"


def clean_user(t):
    t = NOISE.sub("", t)
    return t.strip()


def blocks_of(rec):
    c = rec.get("message", {}).get("content")
    if isinstance(c, str):
        return [{"type": "text", "text": c}]
    return c if isinstance(c, list) else []


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- collect
records = []
for line in open(T, encoding="utf-8"):
    try:
        d = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if d.get("type") in SKIP_TYPES:
        continue
    records.append(d)

# tool_use id -> result payload, so a call and its output sit together
results = {}
for d in records:
    for b in blocks_of(d):
        if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_result":
            cc = b.get("content")
            if isinstance(cc, list):
                cc = "\n".join(x.get("text", "") for x in cc
                               if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "text")
            results[b.get("tool_use_id")] = cc if isinstance(cc, str) else json.dumps(cc, indent=2)

HEAD = """---
title: Build analytics pipeline script from test files
project: car-bid-tracker
tool: Claude Code (Opus 5)
started: 2026-08-12
updated: 2026-08-16
status: ongoing
type: chat-transcript
tags: [car-bid-tracker, apibara, iaai, salvage-auction, analytics-pipeline, web-scraping, csv-schema, images]
---

# Build analytics pipeline script from test files

**Verbatim copy of the chat.** User prompts, assistant output, tool calls and tool
results are reproduced exactly as recorded in the session log — nothing summarised,
nothing paraphrased, nothing reordered.

> [!warning] Thinking blocks are not recoverable
> The session log contains 357 thinking blocks, but each one stores an empty
> `thinking` string and only a cryptographic `signature` — the reasoning text is
> never persisted to disk. They appear below as `*[thinking block — content not
> retained in the session log]*` placeholders. They are **not** reconstructed,
> because writing them from memory would fabricate a record of reasoning that was
> never saved.

Source: `~/.claude/projects/-home-striker-projects-car-bid-tracker/1de5f512-27cc-4a6f-a0ee-152360548399.jsonl`

---

"""

body = []
prompt_n = 0
pending_header = False

for d in records:
    kind = d.get("type")
    bs = blocks_of(d)

    if kind == "user":
        # a user record is either a real prompt or a tool_result carrier
        texts = [b.get("text", "") for b in bs
                 if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text"]
        joined = clean_user("\n".join(texts))
        if not joined:
            continue
        prompt_n += 1
        body.append(f"\n## Prompt {prompt_n}\n\n{fence(joined)}\n\n### Response\n")
        continue

    if kind != "assistant":
        continue

    for b in bs:
        if not isinstance(b, dict):
            continue
        bt = b.get("type")
        if bt == "thinking":
            body.append("\n*[thinking block — content not retained in the session log]*\n")
        elif bt == "text":
            txt = (b.get("text") or "").strip()
            if txt:
                body.append("\n" + txt + "\n")
        elif bt == "tool_use":
            name = b.get("name", "?")
            inp = b.get("input") or {}
            label = (inp.get("description") or inp.get("file_path")
                     or inp.get("prompt") or inp.get("query") or inp.get("skill") or "")
            label = str(label).splitlines()[0][:90] if label else ""
            head = f"**Tool — {name}**" + (f": {label}" if label else "")
            # command / body first, as the chat shows it
            if name == "Bash":
                payload = fence(inp.get("command", ""), "bash")
            elif name in ("Write",):
                payload = fence(inp.get("content", ""))
            elif name in ("Edit",):
                payload = ("*old_string*\n" + fence(inp.get("old_string", "")) +
                           "\n*new_string*\n" + fence(inp.get("new_string", "")))
            else:
                payload = fence(json.dumps(inp, indent=2), "json")
            res = results.get(b.get("id"))
            out = f"\n*Result*\n{fence(res)}\n" if res else ""
            body.append(f"\n<details>\n<summary>{head}</summary>\n\n{payload}\n{out}\n</details>\n")

OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
OUT.write_text(HEAD + "".join(body), encoding="utf-8")
txt = OUT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
print(f"wrote {OUT}")
print(f"  {prompt_n} prompts, {len(txt):,} chars, {len(txt.splitlines()):,} lines, "
      f"{OUT.stat().st_size/1e6:.2f} MB")

````

*new_string*

def _norm_damage(s):
    """Normalise a damage string for lookup: LOWERCASE, then tidy spacing.

    Both sides of the comparison go through this — the table above is written in
    lowercase and the incoming value is lowercased here — so casing can never
    decide a grouping. That is not cosmetic: `primary_damage` writes "Front end"
    and "Left side" while `secondary_damage` writes "Front End" and "Left Side",
    so a case-sensitive lookup would group one field correctly and silently drop
    the other into OTHER.
    """
    t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(s or "").strip().lower())
    return re.sub(r"\s*&\s*", " & ", t)
```

## The change

```
FRONT:      front & rear, front end, front, left front, right front, roof
REAR-SIDE:  left & right side, left rear, left side, rear,
            right rear, right side, normal wear & tear, theft
OTHER:      everything else
(blank):    stays blank
```

`_norm_damage()` lowercases the incoming value, collapses whitespace and tightens `&` spacing; the table itself is written lowercase. So casing can never decide a grouping — verified against `Front end`, `Front End`, `FRONT END`, `left side`, `Left Side`, `LEFT & RIGHT SIDE` and `  Front  `, all resolving correctly.

That symmetry is load-bearing rather than tidy: **the two fields genuinely disagree.** `primary_damage` writes `Front end` / `Left side` while `secondary_damage` writes `Front End` / `Left Side` and carries values primary never does (`Left & Right Side`). A case-sensitive lookup would have grouped primary correctly and silently dumped nearly all of secondary into OTHER.

```
def style_set(values):
    """Repeatable, multi-word, comma-separated body styles -> normalised set.

    Real IAAI values include "Compact Luxury Car" and "Sedan/Hatchback", so the
    same rule as everywhere else applies: spaces join a value, commas separate
    values. `--body-style Compact Luxury Car` is one style;
    `--body-style coupe,sedan` is two; repeating the flag adds more.
    """
    out = set()
    for occurrence in values or []:
        for token in multiword(occurrence).split(","):
            if token.strip():
                out.add(norm_style(token))
    return out


def main(argv=None):
  space-separated : {'coupe/convertible'}
  comma-separated : {'convertible', 'coupe'}
  repeated flag   : {'convertible', 'coupe'}

    """-> (path, renamed_from). Renames an existing folder as knowledge improves.

    A lot is identified by its lot number alone — stable across relists — so any
    existing `{lot}-*` folder is THIS lot, whatever VIN it was named with.

    Three cases, in order of how much they matter:
      masked -> full     the VIN resolved; rename in place, never a second folder
      full   -> masked   a web-only re-pull knows less; keep the resolved name
      masked -> masked   same knowledge, but possibly a different mask character;
                         normalise so one tree does not mix `******` and `xxxxxx`
    """
    want = lot_dir(platform, lot, vin, mask_char)
    parent = want.parent
    if not parent.exists():
        return want, ""

    for old in sorted(p for p in parent.glob(f"{lot}-*") if p.is_dir()):
        if old.name == want.name:
            return want, ""
        old_vin = old.name.split("-", 1)[-1]
        old_masked, new_masked = is_masked_vin(old_vin), is_masked_vin(want.name)
        if old_masked and not new_masked:
            if want.exists():
                # Both names already on disk: keep the resolved one and leave
                # the masked folder alone rather than merging blind.
                return want, ""
            if apply:
                old.rename(want)
            return want, old.name
        if not old_masked and new_masked:
            return old, ""          # never downgrade a resolved name
        if old_masked and new_masked and not want.exists():

    """-> (path, moved_from). Keeps ONE folder per lot as knowledge improves.

    A lot is identified by its lot number alone — stable across relists — so any
    existing `{lot}-*` folder anywhere in the tree is THIS lot, whatever VIN it
    was named with and whatever damage group it was filed under.

    Four cases, in order of how much they matter:
      group change       primary_damage was revised; MOVE, never fork
      masked -> full     the VIN resolved; rename in place, never a second folder
      full   -> masked   a web-only re-pull knows less; keep the resolved name
      masked -> masked   same knowledge, possibly a different mask character;
                         normalise so one tree does not mix `******` and `xxxxxx`
    """
    want = lot_dir(platform, lot, vin, group, mask_char)

        old_vin = old.name.split("-", 1)[-1]
        old_masked, new_masked = is_masked_vin(old_vin), is_masked_vin(want.name)

        # Pick the better NAME, then place it in the group the row says.
        if not old_masked and new_masked:
            target = old.parent / old.name     # keep the resolved VIN
            target = want.parent / old.name    # ...but still under the new group

        if target.exists():

            # the stale folder alone rather than merging two trees blind.
            return target, ""

## What's built

The folder structure is now `images/open/{FRONT|REAR-SIDE|OTHER}/{platform}/{lot}-{vin}`, with the group taken from **`primary_damage_group`** (the grouping of `primary_damage`, as you specified). Blanks fall into `OTHER`, per your note.

The non-obvious part was that folders must **move**, not fork. A lot's damage classification can change when IAAI revises the record, and its VIN resolves on a different schedule — so `existing_dirs()` searches every group folder *and* the legacy flat path, and one folder follows the lot wherever it belongs. Sandbox-tested five cases:

```
A legacy->group   open/iaai/…  ->  open/REAR-SIDE/iaai/…          file preserved
B group change    open/FRONT/… ->  open/REAR-SIDE/iaai/…          file preserved
C vin reveal      …xxxxxx      ->  …123456   (same group)         file preserved
D no downgrade    kept resolved VIN 999999 while moving to OTHER  file preserved
E dry-run inert   nothing moved
```

Case D is the one worth noting — a masked re-pull that *also* changes group keeps the good VIN name and still relocates. Name quality and group placement are decided independently.

## Migration in flight

13 of the 27 existing folders belong to lots in this cut and are migrating from the flat layout as they're processed — you can see the legacy dir draining (25 left) as `FRONT`/`REAR-SIDE` fill. The remaining ones aren't in this cut; they'll migrate on their next re-pull, since `existing_dirs()` keeps looking there.

I also moved the manifest from `images/open/iaai/manifest_open.csv` to **`images/open/manifest_open.csv`** — it now spans damage groups, and splitting it per group would fragment the very history the move logic depends on. All 53 prior rows preserved, plus a new `damage_group` column.

Of 84 rows, **82 matched** — 2 dropped for having no image URLs at all.

I'll report the final counts and rebuild the transcript when the download finishes.

## The migration, including one I nearly left broken

13 folders migrated automatically during the run (`MOVED from open/iaai/…`), preserving their images — you can see them reporting `0 new, 17 present`.

But **14 folders were stranded** in the legacy flat dir: lots excluded by this cut's coupe/convertible/mileage/distance filters, so the run never touched them. Leaving them there would have meant a permanently split tree that only healed if those exact lots reappeared in a future cut.

I migrated them using their `primary_damage_group` from the unfiltered `csv-raw` layer, through the same `resolve_folder()` logic rather than a one-off `mv`. All 14 resolved (all REAR-SIDE), images intact, and the empty legacy directory is gone.

## What the move logic handles

Sandbox-verified before touching real data:

```
legacy flat -> group      file preserved
group change              FRONT -> REAR-SIDE, folder moves, never forks
VIN resolves              …xxxxxx -> …123456 within the same group
no downgrade              keeps resolved VIN while still moving group
dry-run                   inert
```

Case 4 matters most: name quality and group placement are decided **independently**, so a masked re-pull that also reclassifies damage keeps the good VIN name and still relocates.

Manifest moved to `images/open/manifest_open.csv` with a new `damage_group` column — 135 rows, all 53 prior entries preserved (they show `damage_group` blank, since they predate the split).

Two of the 84 rows had no image URLs at all and were skipped.

# Audi S5 2018-2023 — full pipeline

**One thing to change from the A5 runs: S5 is `--tier 1`, not 2.** Confirmed against `app/tier.py`. Note 2023 S5 auto-classifies as `None` (the want-list window is 2018-2022), so the explicit `--tier 1` is doing real work here, not just echoing the classifier.

### 1 — Pull iaai.com, one year at a time

python analytics/scripts/pull_iaai_web_01.py \
    --make Audi --model S5 --year-range 2018-2023 --details

    --audit

    --exclude-body-style coupe,convertible \
    --max-odometer 100000 \
    --max-distance 3000 \
    --history --history-cache \
    --out audi_s5_2018-2023_open_ins_nocoupe_noconv_100k_3000mi.csv

## Three things worth knowing before you run it

**`coupe,convertible` must use the comma.** Spaces join a value, so `--exclude-body-style coupe convertible` parses as the single style `coupe/convertible` and silently excludes nothing.

**That filter will bite much harder on S5 than A5.** The S5 is sold predominantly as a coupe and cabriolet — the A5 run lost 47 of 180 lots to it, and I'd expect the S5 to lose a far larger share. Worth checking the `body_style=` drop counts in the stage-3 output before assuming the result is thin because inventory is thin.

**Step 5 is the long one.** The A5 cut took ~12 minutes for 1,372 images, so this is a background job. Add `--dry-run` first to see the count, or `--max-images N` to cap per lot.

'''def money_tag(v):
    """7200.0 -> '$7200'. Empty for absent or zero — no Buy Now, no segment."""
    try:
        n = float(str(v).replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip())
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return ""
    return f"${int(round(n))}" if n > 0 else ""


def folder_name(lot, vin, dist_bucket, buy_now, mask_char="x"):
    """{lot}-{vin}[-{distance}][-${buynow}]

    Distance and Buy Now are appended so the tree is browsable by the two things
    that decide whether a lot is worth opening: how far it is, and whether it can
    be bought outright. Both are OPTIONAL segments — a lot with no coordinates or
    no Buy Now simply has a shorter name, rather than a placeholder to decode.
    """
    vin = (vin or "").strip().upper() or "NOVIN"
    if is_masked_vin(vin):
        vin = _MASKED_TAIL.sub(mask_char * 6, vin)
    parts = [str(lot), vin]
    if str(dist_bucket or "").strip():
        parts.append(str(dist_bucket).strip())
    bn = money_tag(buy_now)
    if bn:
        parts.append(bn)
    return "-".join(parts)


def parse_folder_name(name):
    """'45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-2500mi-$7200' -> (lot, vin, dist, buynow).

    Component-aware on purpose. A naive `split('-', 1)[-1]` used to be enough
    when the name was just {lot}-{vin}; with trailing segments it would hand
    `is_masked_vin()` the whole tail, so `…xxxxxx-2500mi` would read as NOT
    masked and the VIN-resolution rename would silently stop firing.
    """
    parts = str(name).split("-")
    lot = parts[0] if parts else ""
    vin = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    dist = next((p for p in parts[2:] if p.endswith("mi")), "")
    bn = next((p for p in parts[2:] if p.startswith("$")), "")
    return lot, vin, dist, bn


def lot_dir(platform, lot, vin, group, model, dist_bucket="", buy_now="",
            mask_char="x"):
    return (IMAGES_ROOT / "open" / model / group / platform
            / folder_name(lot, vin, dist_bucket, buy_now, mask_char))


def existing_dirs(platform, lot, model=None):
    """Every folder on disk that belongs to this lot, wherever it sits.

    Searched across ALL damage groups AND all model folders, because both can
    change: IAAI revises `primary_damage`, and a lot can surface under a
    different search. The pre-model and pre-group layouts are searched too, so
    older trees migrate on first re-pull instead of being stranded.
    """
    root = IMAGES_ROOT / "open"
    if not root.exists():
        return
    seen = set()
    # every {model}/{group}/{platform}, plus the two legacy shapes
    candidates = list(root.glob(f"*/*/{platform}"))          # model/group/platform
    candidates += [root / g / platform for g in DAMAGE_DIRS]  # pre-model
    candidates.append(root / platform)                        # pre-group
    for c in candidates:
        if not c.is_dir() or c in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(c)
        for p in sorted(c.glob(f"{lot}-*")):
            if p.is_dir():
                yield p''',1)

All 290 covered. Fixing the derivation — the shortest model form is the search term, since trims extend it:

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Bash**: Fix and verify model-folder derivation</summary>

```bash
cd /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker
python - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("analytics/scripts/pull_images_01.py"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
s=s.replace('''def derive_model_folder(rows):
    """Dominant "Make Model" in the CSV — the search this cut came from.

    Derived rather than required, because the whole point of the folder is to
    mirror the pull_iaai_web search, and the CSV already carries that. A cut
    spanning several models still gets one folder, so --model-folder overrides.
    """
    counts = {}
    for r in rows:
        key = f"{(r.get('make') or '').title()} {(r.get('model') or '').upper()}".strip()
        if key:
            counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
    if not counts:
        return "UNKNOWN"
    return max(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])[0]''',
'''def derive_model_folder(rows):
    """The SEARCH this cut came from, e.g. "Audi A5" — not IAAI's per-lot model.

    IAAI writes the trim into `model`, so one "Audi A5" search returns both `A5`
    and `A5 SPORTBACK`. Taking the most common value would name the folder
    "Audi A5 SPORTBACK", which is a trim, not the search. Trims EXTEND the base
    model, so the shortest form is the search term.

    An existing `images/open/*` folder matching case-insensitively wins outright,
    so a tree already organised by hand keeps its exact names rather than
    gaining a near-duplicate.
    """
    makes, models = {}, {}
    for r in rows:
        mk = (r.get("make") or "").strip()
        md = (r.get("model") or "").strip()
        if mk:
            makes[mk] = makes.get(mk, 0) + 1
        if md:
            models[md] = models.get(md, 0) + 1
    if not makes and not models:
        return "UNKNOWN"
    make = max(makes.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])[0].title() if makes else ""
    # shortest model string; ties broken by frequency
    model = min(models, key=lambda m: (len(m), -models[m])) if models else ""
    guess = f"{make} {model}".strip()

    root = IMAGES_ROOT / "open"
    if root.is_dir():
        for d in sorted(root.iterdir()):
            if d.is_dir() and d.name.lower() == guess.lower():
                return d.name
    return guess''',1)
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8"); print("patched derivation")

5	                                              |
6	                                        data_pull_01.py  ->  + tier, sold_period
7	
8	This script owns everything derivable from the record alone, distance included.
9	`tier` and `sold_period` are NOT emitted here — tier takes an operator decision
10	per archive, so it belongs to data_pull_01.py.
11	
12	Reads the archives written by pull_apibara_01.py, flattens each IAAI record into
13	one row, and applies whatever filtering you ask for. No network, no API calls —
14	run it as often as you like, with different filters, against the same archive.
15	
16	KEY FIELDS ONLY — 57 columns, one per fact
17	------------------------------------------
18	Duplicates were removed after measuring them across a 70-lot pull, not by eye:
19	`vehicle_class` was identical to `body_style` on every row, `key_fob` to
20	`has_key`, `location_display` to `selling_branch`; `primary_damage_code`,
21	`acv_raw`, `est_repair_raw`, `body_style_name` and `runs_and_drives` were each
22	1:1 with a column that survived. Where a code and a description were 1:1 the
23	description won (codes like "AO"/"LR" mean nothing in a spreadsheet); where raw
24	text and a parsed number were 1:1 the number won ("$29,240 USD" does not sort);
25	where a boolean and a multi-valued field were 1:1 the multi-valued one won
26	(`run_condition` keeps IAAI's three run states, which a boolean flattens).
27	
28	`secondary_damage_code` is the exception that proves the rule, and the reason
29	every pair was measured rather than assumed. It looks like the twin of
30	`primary_damage_code` and is not: the primary code is strictly 1:1 with its
31	description (14 values, both 70/70), while the secondary code is populated on
32	40/70 against the description's 30/70. Those extra 10 rows carry "UK" — IAAI
33	inspected the car and recorded secondary damage as UNKNOWN, a state a blank
34	description cannot be distinguished from "nothing recorded at all". Dropping it
35	would have silently merged two different facts.
36	
37	Nothing is lost: every dropped field is still in the raw JSON archive, and
38	adding a column back is one line in SCHEMA plus a re-run — no API calls.
39	
40	    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py                # newest archive
41	    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py FILE.json ...  # specific ones
42	    python analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py --all          # every IAAI archive
43	
44	    --exclude-damage water,flood,fire   drop lots whose damage matches (OFF by default)
45	    --include-damage front,rear         keep ONLY lots whose damage matches
46	    --body-style coupe                  keep only these (repeatable/comma-separated)
47	    --exclude-body-style coupe          drop these
48	    --seller-class insurance            keep only these seller classes
49	    --min-photos 8                      drop thin listings
50	    --sold-only                         drop lots with no realised sale price
51	    --market unitedstates               keep only these markets (US / Canada)
52	    --max-odometer 100000               drop high-mileage and unknown-odometer lots
53	    --max-distance 3000                 drop far and unknown-location lots
54	    --schema                            print the column mapping table and exit
55	
56	IAAI ONLY. A Copart converter will be a separate script, because the two payload
57	shapes are not variations of one schema — they are different schemas. Copart
58	records carry `details: None`, which removes ActualCashValue, EstimatedRepairCost,
59	body style, storage coordinates and the entire attributes block in one go. Nearly
60	half the columns below simply do not exist on a Copart lot, so a shared converter
61	would be mostly null-handling.
62	
63	SELLER CLASSIFICATION — READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE COLUMN
64	------------------------------------------------------------
65	IAAI masks seller identity on a meaningful slice of lots. Observed on a 68-lot
66	insurance-filtered pull: 12 records came back with
67	
68	    sale_information.SellerType = "******"    (literally asterisks)
69	    seller.name                 = "unknown"
70	    seller.type                 = "unknown"
71	
72	...while `attributes.Origin` said "Insurance" and `attributes.ProviderType` said
73	"INS" on all 68. The masking hides WHICH carrier, not WHETHER it is a carrier.
74	Reading SellerType naively classifies those 12 as non-insurance, which is simply
75	wrong — every one of them came from a `seller_type=insurance` server-side query.
76	
77	So `seller_class` cascades, most reliable source first. Which rule fired is not
78	a CSV column — it would be constant across a single-carrier pull — but every run
79	prints the full audit table, so the classification stays checkable.
80	`seller_name_masked` flags the anonymised ones so they can be excluded from
81	carrier-level analysis without being miscounted as dealers.
82	
83	IMAGE / VIDEO COLUMNS
84	---------------------
85	IAAI thumb URLs look like:
86	
87	    https://vis.iaai.com/resizer?imageKeys=46139013~SID~I1&width=400&height=300
88	                                           ^^^^^^^^        ^
89	                                           SalvageId       image key
90	
91	`iaai_image_url_prefix` keeps everything up to and including the trailing "I",
92	and `iaai_image_keys` collects the numeric suffixes as a pipe-joined array
93	(1|2|...|115|116) — the keys are NOT contiguous, they jump from ~11 to ~115, so
94	they cannot be regenerated from a count and must be stored. Rebuild any URL as:
95	
96	    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=845&height=633"      # large
97	    f"{iaai_image_url_prefix}{key}&width=400&height=300"      # thumb
98	
99	Note the image key is `attributes.SalvageId`, which is NOT the lot number
100	(lot 45640490 -> SalvageId 46139013). Do not build image URLs from lot_number.
101	
102	vr360 is deliberately absent from the CSV — it carries no analytic signal and
103	one fixed URL shape per lot. It remains in the raw JSON if ever needed.

290 distance segments added, **19 buy-now segments**, 5 folders moved between groups by the hail change.

## Two things that needed solving

**Deriving the model folder from `model` doesn't work.** My first attempt produced `Audi A5 SPORTBACK` — IAAI writes the trim into that field. Taking the shortest form fixed A5 but then gave **`Audi RS 3`** for the RS 5 search, because IAAI's keyword matching is loose: `2018 Audi RS 5` came back **6 RS 3 and 6 RS 5**. No inference from per-lot data can recover the search term.

So I added a `search_keyword` column carrying the actual iaai.com search, and derive from that with the year stripped (`2019 Audi A5` → `Audi A5`). An existing `images/open/*` folder matching case-insensitively wins outright, so your hand-made names are preserved exactly. `--model-folder` overrides.

**Folder-name parsing had to become component-aware.** With trailing segments, the old `split("-", 1)[-1]` would have handed `is_masked_vin()` the whole tail — so `…xxxxxx-2500mi` would read as *not* masked and the VIN-resolution rename would have silently stopped firing. Now parsed into `(lot, vin, dist, buynow)`.

Sandbox-verified before touching real data: buy-now appearing, buy-now disappearing (+ VIN resolving simultaneously), group change, model change, and no-downgrade — files preserved in every case. Distance and buy-now are re-evaluated each run, so a withdrawn Buy Now can't linger in a folder name.

## One thing to know

Your existing csv-cut files predate `search_keyword`, so re-running `pull_images_01.py` against an old cut still derives `Audi RS 3`. Regenerating the cut fixes it, or pass `--model-folder "Audi RS 5"`. New cuts carry the column automatically.

The run reported **`manifest: 0 prior + 24 new entries`**. The manifest that had 135 rows is gone — it was already missing before this run, so it was lost when the images tree was reorganized by hand, not by this run.

s=s.replace('''def folder_name(lot, vin, dist_bucket, buy_now, mask_char="x"):
    """{lot}-{vin}[-{distance}][-${buynow}]

    Distance and Buy Now are appended so the tree is browsable by the two things
    that decide whether a lot is worth opening: how far it is, and whether it can
    be bought outright. Both are OPTIONAL segments — a lot with no coordinates or
    no Buy Now simply has a shorter name, rather than a placeholder to decode.
    """
    vin = (vin or "").strip().upper() or "NOVIN"

def parse_folder_name(name):
    """'45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-2500mi-$7200' -> (lot, vin, dist, buynow).

    Component-aware on purpose. A naive `split('-', 1)[-1]` used to be enough
    when the name was just {lot}-{vin}; with trailing segments it would hand
    `is_masked_vin()` the whole tail, so `…xxxxxx-2500mi` would read as NOT
    masked and the VIN-resolution rename would silently stop firing.
    """
    parts = str(name).split("-")
    lot = parts[0] if parts else ""
    vin = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    dist = next((p for p in parts[2:] if p.endswith("mi")), "")
    bn = next((p for p in parts[2:] if p.startswith("$")), "")

'''_YEAR_SEG = re.compile(r"^(?:19|20)\\d{2}$")


def folder_name(lot, vin, year, dist_bucket, buy_now, mask_char="x"):
    """{lot}-{vin}[-{year}][-{distance}][-${buynow}]

    Everything after the VIN is an OPTIONAL segment appended in a fixed order,
    so a lot missing a year, coordinates or a Buy Now simply has a shorter name
    rather than a placeholder to decode. The three are what decide whether a lot
    is worth opening: how old, how far, and whether it can be bought outright.
    """
    vin = (vin or "").strip().upper() or "NOVIN"
    if is_masked_vin(vin):
        vin = _MASKED_TAIL.sub(mask_char * 6, vin)
    parts = [str(lot), vin]
    y = str(year or "").strip()
    if _YEAR_SEG.match(y):
        parts.append(y)
    if str(dist_bucket or "").strip():
        parts.append(str(dist_bucket).strip())
    bn = money_tag(buy_now)
    if bn:
        parts.append(bn)
    return "-".join(parts)


def parse_folder_name(name):
    """'45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-2019-2500mi-$7200'
        -> (lot, vin, year, dist, buynow)

    Component-aware on purpose, and each optional segment is identified by SHAPE
    rather than position: a year is 19xx/20xx, a distance ends in `mi`, a Buy Now
    starts with `$`. Position would be fragile precisely because the segments are
    optional — and a naive `split('-', 1)[-1]` would hand `is_masked_vin()` the
    whole tail, so `…xxxxxx-2019-2500mi` would read as NOT masked and the
    VIN-resolution rename would silently stop firing.
    """
    parts = str(name).split("-")
    lot = parts[0] if parts else ""
    vin = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    tail = parts[2:]
    year = next((p for p in tail if _YEAR_SEG.match(p)), "")
    dist = next((p for p in tail if p.endswith("mi")), "")
    bn = next((p for p in tail if p.startswith("$")), "")
    return lot, vin, year, dist, bn''',1)

## One design point worth flagging

Segments are now identified by **shape, not position** — a year is `19xx`/`20xx`, a distance ends in `mi`, a Buy Now starts with `$`. That matters because they're optional: position-based parsing would misread `45704693-WAUENCF5XJAxxxxxx-2500mi` (a pre-year folder) by treating `2500mi` as the year.

It also protects the masked-VIN detection, which is what drives the VIN-resolution rename. Verified across all four name shapes including pre-year folders — a `…xxxxxx-2019-2500mi` still reads as masked, so a lot whose VIN resolves later will still get renamed rather than silently forking.

## A gap the migration surfaced

The first pass renamed 294 and reported **20 folders with no `csv-raw` row** — the S4 lots. I'd gone straight from `iaai_web_adapt` to `data_pull_01` in the end-to-end run, skipping the stage-2 flatten, so S4 never produced a csv-raw file. Generated it (30 rows × 68 cols) and the remaining 20 migrated cleanly.

Worth remembering for future end-to-end runs: `data_pull_01` reads the *adapted JSON*, not csv-raw, so csv-raw is easy to skip — and anything keyed off it (this migration, cross-model lookups) then has a hole. The pipeline works either way; the artifact is just missing.

Tree now **1.73 GB across five models**. Schema doc and transcript updated (**71 prompts, 2.43 MB**).

def folder_name(lot, vin, year, dist_bucket, buy_now, mask_char="x"):

    Everything after the VIN is an OPTIONAL segment appended in a fixed order,
    so a lot missing a year, coordinates or a Buy Now simply has a shorter name
    rather than a placeholder to decode. The three are what decide whether a lot
    is worth opening: how old, how far, and whether it can be bought outright.
    """
    vin = (vin or "").strip().upper() or "NOVIN"

def parse_folder_name(name):
    """'45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-2019-2500mi-$7200'
        -> (lot, vin, year, dist, buynow)

    Component-aware on purpose, and each optional segment is identified by SHAPE
    rather than position: a year is 19xx/20xx, a distance ends in `mi`, a Buy Now
    starts with `$`. Position would be fragile precisely because the segments are
    optional — and a naive `split('-', 1)[-1]` would hand `is_masked_vin()` the
    whole tail, so `…xxxxxx-2019-2500mi` would read as NOT masked and the
    VIN-resolution rename would silently stop firing.
    """
    parts = str(name).split("-")
    lot = parts[0] if parts else ""
    vin = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    tail = parts[2:]
    year = next((p for p in tail if _YEAR_SEG.match(p)), "")
    dist = next((p for p in tail if p.endswith("mi")), "")
    bn = next((p for p in tail if p.startswith("$")), "")
    return lot, vin, year, dist, bn''',
'''_YEAR_SEG = re.compile(r"^(?:19|20)\\d{2}$")
_DIST_SEG = re.compile(r"^(\\d+)mi$")


def dist_tag(bucket):
    """'250mi' -> '0250mi'. Zero-padded to 4 digits so names sort by distance.

    Without padding, plain string ordering puts 250mi after 2500mi and before
    3000mi — the folder listing reads as noise. Four digits covers the 3250mi
    top of the observed range with room to spare.
    """
    m = _DIST_SEG.match(str(bucket or "").strip())
    return f"{int(m.group(1)):04d}mi" if m else str(bucket or "").strip()


def folder_name(lot, vin, year, dist_bucket, buy_now, mask_char="x"):
    """[{year}-][{distance}-]{lot}-{vin}[-${buynow}]

    Year and distance lead so a listing sorts by age then proximity — the two
    coarse filters a human applies before opening anything. Lot and VIN follow as
    the identity, and Buy Now trails because it is the most volatile.

    Every segment except lot and VIN is OPTIONAL, so a lot missing a year,
    coordinates or a Buy Now simply has a shorter name rather than a placeholder
    to decode.
    """
    vin = (vin or "").strip().upper() or "NOVIN"
    if is_masked_vin(vin):
        vin = _MASKED_TAIL.sub(mask_char * 6, vin)
    parts = []
    y = str(year or "").strip()
    if _YEAR_SEG.match(y):
        parts.append(y)
    d = dist_tag(dist_bucket)
    if d:
        parts.append(d)
    parts += [str(lot), vin]
    bn = money_tag(buy_now)
    if bn:
        parts.append(bn)
    return "-".join(parts)


def parse_folder_name(name):
    """'2019-2500mi-45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-$7200'
        -> (lot, vin, year, dist, buynow)

    Every segment is identified by SHAPE, never position, because the optional
    ones can be absent and because they have now moved twice. A year is
    19xx/20xx; a distance is digits + `mi`; a Buy Now starts with `$`; the lot is
    the remaining all-digit token; the VIN is the token containing letters.

    Shape-based parsing is what lets one function read every naming generation
    this tree has had — `{lot}-{vin}`, `{lot}-{vin}-{dist}`,
    `{lot}-{vin}-{year}-{dist}` and now `{year}-{dist}-{lot}-{vin}` — which is
    exactly what makes migrating existing folders possible instead of guessing.
    It also keeps masked-VIN detection honest: hand `is_masked_vin()` a whole
    tail and `…xxxxxx-2019-2500mi` reads as NOT masked, silently disabling the
    VIN-resolution rename.
    """
    parts = [p for p in str(name).split("-") if p]
    year = next((p for p in parts if _YEAR_SEG.match(p)), "")
    dist = next((p for p in parts if _DIST_SEG.match(p)), "")
    bn = next((p for p in parts if p.startswith("$")), "")
    used = {year, dist, bn}
    rest = [p for p in parts if p not in used]
    lot = next((p for p in rest if p.isdigit()), "")
    vin = next((p for p in rest if not p.isdigit() and not p.startswith("$")), "")
    return lot, vin, year, dist, bn''',1)

        for p in sorted(c.iterdir()):
            if p.is_dir() and parse_folder_name(p.name)[0] == str(lot):
                yield p''',1)

images/open/Audi A5/FRONT/iaai/2018-3000mi-45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-$7600
images/open/Audi A5/FRONT/iaai/2021-0250mi-45354112-WAUDACF58MAxxxxxx-$6750""")
s=s.replace("""Year, distance and Buy Now are optional trailing segments, so a lot missing any
of them just has a shorter name. All three are re-evaluated on every run and the
folder is renamed in place — a Buy Now that has since been withdrawn must not
linger in a folder name.

Segments are identified by **shape, not position**, precisely because they are
optional: a year is `19xx`/`20xx`, a distance ends in `mi`, a Buy Now starts with
`$`. This also keeps masked-VIN detection working — parsing by position, or the
old `split('-', 1)[-1]`, would hand `is_masked_vin()` the whole tail, so
`…xxxxxx-2019-2500mi` would read as NOT masked and the VIN-resolution rename
would silently stop firing.""",
"""**Year and distance lead** so a listing sorts by age then proximity — the two
coarse filters a human applies before opening anything. Lot and VIN follow as the
identity, and Buy Now trails because it is the most volatile.

**Distance is zero-padded to four digits** (`0250mi`, not `250mi`). Unpadded,
plain string ordering puts `250mi` after `2500mi` and before `3000mi`, and the
listing reads as noise:

```
2018-1250mi-45662018-WAUENCF51JA104260
2018-2250mi-45490663-WAUENCF55JA084384
2018-3000mi-45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-$7600
```

Year, distance and Buy Now are all optional, so a lot missing any of them just
has a shorter name. All three are re-evaluated on every run and the folder is
renamed in place — a Buy Now that has since been withdrawn must not linger in a
folder name.

Segments are identified by **shape, never position**: a year is `19xx`/`20xx`, a
distance is digits + `mi`, a Buy Now starts with `$`, the lot is the remaining
all-digit token, the VIN is the token containing letters. That is what lets one
parser read every naming generation this tree has had —

```
{lot}-{vin}                          gen 1
{lot}-{vin}-{dist}                   gen 2
{lot}-{vin}-{year}-{dist}            gen 3
{year}-{dist}-{lot}-{vin}            gen 4 (current)
```

— which is what makes migrating existing folders possible rather than guessed at.
It also keeps masked-VIN detection honest: hand `is_masked_vin()` a whole tail
and `…xxxxxx-2019-2500mi` reads as NOT masked, silently disabling the
VIN-resolution rename.""")
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8"); print("schema doc updated")
PY
python analytics/scripts/build_chat_transcript.py 2>&1 | tail -1

Both changes applied and **all 314 folders migrated** — no re-downloads, no duplicates, 5,207 images intact.

```
[{year}-][{dist}-]{lot}-{vin}[-${buynow}]

2018-1250mi-45662018-WAUENCF51JA104260
2018-3000mi-45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-$7600
2021-0250mi-45354112-WAUDACF58MAxxxxxx-$6750
```

The padding does exactly what you'd want — `Audi A5/FRONT` now reads in order:

```
2018-1250mi-45662018-WAUENCF51JA104260
2018-2250mi-45490663-WAUENCF55JA084384
2018-2250mi-45681606-WAUENCF50JAxxxxxx
2018-2500mi-44874926-WAUANCF56JAxxxxxx
2018-2750mi-45521986-WAUANCF56JAxxxxxx
2018-3000mi-45107640-WAUENCF58JAxxxxxx
```

Unpadded, `250mi` would have sorted between `2500mi` and `3000mi`.

## What the reorder broke, and how it's handled

Moving the lot number off the front broke two things that had been relying on position:

- **`existing_dirs()` globbed `{lot}-*`** to find a lot's folder. That now matches nothing, so it parses every folder instead — ~300 folders makes the cost irrelevant.
- **Positional parsing** would misread the old names entirely.

So parsing is now purely **shape-based**: a year is `19xx`/`20xx`, a distance is digits + `mi`, a Buy Now starts with `$`, the lot is the remaining all-digit token, the VIN is the token with letters.

That's what made the migration possible rather than guesswork — one parser reads all four generations this tree has had:

```
{lot}-{vin}                    gen 1
{lot}-{vin}-{dist}             gen 2
{lot}-{vin}-{year}-{dist}      gen 3
{year}-{dist}-{lot}-{vin}      gen 4
```

Verified on a sample of each before touching the tree, including that a masked VIN still reads as masked in every form — otherwise the VIN-resolution rename would silently stop firing and lots would fork into duplicate folders when Apibara revealed their VINs.

```
314 folders / 314 distinct lots / 0 duplicates
parse ok 314/314   year 314   distance 314 (all 4-digit padded)   buy-now 21
1.73 GB
```

Full S5 update done. Your premise about pre-running the ended pull was right — it caught something the web source structurally cannot show.

## 1 — Apibara history depth: **the Basic plan does not extend it**

Asked for 12 months, got **5.8**:

```
requested  2025-08-17 .. 2026-08-17
returned   2026-02-24 .. 2026-08-17     90 lots, 5 calls
```

Confirmed as a hard wall, not sparse data:

```
S5 ended, 2025-08-17..2026-02-23        ->  0 lots
whole corpus, 1,445 sold records        ->  earliest 2026-02-16
```

Today is 08-17, so that's exactly a rolling **6-month window**. The $25 plan buys rate and volume (30k/month, 1 req/sec), **not depth** — same horizon the demo key gave. Which means your raw archives really are the only long-term history, and the archive-everything design is load-bearing rather than cautious.

One gotcha: a very wide window (`2025-01-01..2026-02-23`, no model filter) returned **HTTP 502 "Vehicle API request failed"**. Keep ranges inside the retention window.

## 2 — The four validations

**(i) VINs resolved — 4 of 71.** Low because Apibara only returns scheduled lots, and 64 of 71 are `Auction Not Assigned`.

**(ii) Images back-filled — 0.** One lot still has none: `45896410`, `Auction Not Assigned`, `Wait Title`. Same signature as every other no-image lot we've seen.

**(iii) Buy Now — one change, and it wasn't a sale.** Lot `45655991` went **$7,400 → None** with `buyNowSold` staying `False`. The Buy Now was *withdrawn*, not taken. That's exactly why the folder name re-evaluates it every run — a stale `-$7400` would have been a lie.

**(iv) A relist caught mid-flight** — the one genuinely new thing:

```
lot 45655991   vin WAUC4DF50KA028113
   PRIOR (ended):  sold 2026-08-17  $3,300  "Sold on Approval"
   NOW   (web):    Prebid, auction_at 2026-08-17, buy-now withdrawn
```

It ran **today**, drew $3,300, the seller hasn't accepted, and it's still listed. Three facts the web pull alone can't give you: the bid amount (login-gated), the approval status, and the VIN. The `current_bid_usd = 3300` on that row came from the ended pull.

## 3 — Cut and images

```
39 rows (from 71)   14 coupe, 5 convertible, 11 mileage, 2 distance excluded
years    2018:10  2019:12  2020:2  2021:4  2022:3  2023:8
damage   FRONT 21, REAR-SIDE 12, OTHER 6
ACV      27/39, median $30,924

Done. 0 downloaded, 648 already present, 0 failed
```

Zero renames and zero downloads — correct, not a no-op bug. The 39 lots already had current folders, and **none of the 4 VIN-resolved lots are in the cut** (S5 is predominantly coupe, and those four were excluded by body style or mileage). I verified that specifically rather than assuming.

Worth flagging: **`buy-now: 0` and `VIN resolved: 0/39`** in this cut. The enrichment worked, but it lands on lots the filters then remove — so for S5 the Apibara join currently adds nothing to the *filtered* set. It only pays off once more S5 lots get scheduled.

### The folder renames itself when the VIN resolves

```
images/open/iaai/45769760-WAUWNGF57JNxxxxxx/     web-only, still masked
images/open/iaai/45490663-WAUENCF55JA084384/     Apibara revealed it
```

The masked tail is written as **`xxxxxx`, not `******`** (`--mask-char`). `*` is
legal on ext4 and illegal on Windows, so an asterisk tree cannot cross the WSL
boundary at all. Folders created under the old scheme are migrated on sight —
that is a third rename case alongside the two below.

Masked-ness is detected as **six trailing mask characters**, never as "contains
an x". `X` is a legal VIN character and a legal check digit, so a substring test
would misread real VINs like `WAUXNCF55JA084384` as masked.

When Apibara later supplies
the full VIN — typically once the lot is scheduled and starts appearing in open
pulls — the next image run **renames the folder in place** instead of creating a
second one. Verified end to end on lot 45490663:

```
[1/1] 45490663-WAUENCF55JA******      2 new, 0 present
   ... enrich from an Apibara open pull, regenerate the cut ...
[1/1] 45490663-WAUENCF55JA084384      0 new, 2 present   RENAMED from 45490663-WAUENCF55JA******
```

One lot, one folder, photos preserved, nothing re-downloaded.

The rename only goes **masked -> full**. A later web-only pull, which knows less,
finds the resolved folder and reuses it rather than downgrading the name — also
verified. This works because `lot_number` identifies the folder and is stable
across relists (1 VIN = 1 lot number, 1338/1338).
````

```
""","""```

images/open/Audi A5/FRONT/iaai/2018-3000mi-45704693-WAUENCF5XJA060484-$7600
images/open/Audi A5/FRONT/iaai/2021-0250mi-45354112-WAUDACF58MAxxxxxx-$6750
```

**The top folder is the SEARCH**, not IAAI's per-lot `model`. `--model-folder`
sets it; left off it is derived from the `search_keyword` column with the leading
year stripped (`2019 Audi A5` -> `Audi A5`). Deriving from `model` is wrong twice
over: IAAI writes the trim into that field, so one A5 search yields both `A5` and
`A5 SPORTBACK`; and its keyword search matches loosely — a `2018 Audi RS 5`
search came back **6 RS 3 and 6 RS 5**, which no inference from `model` can undo.

**Year and distance lead** so a listing sorts by age then proximity — the two
coarse filters a human applies before opening anything. Lot and VIN follow as the
identity; Buy Now trails because it is the most volatile.

**Distance is zero-padded to four digits** (`0250mi`, not `250mi`). Unpadded,
string ordering puts `250mi` after `2500mi` and before `3000mi`, and the listing
reads as noise.

Year, distance and Buy Now are all optional, so a lot missing any just has a
shorter name. All three are re-evaluated on every run and the folder renamed in
place — verified on lot 45655991, whose $7,400 Buy Now was **withdrawn** (not
sold) between two pulls; a stale price in a folder name is a lie.

Segments are identified by **shape, never position**: a year is `19xx`/`20xx`, a
distance is digits + `mi`, a Buy Now starts with `$`, the lot is the remaining
all-digit token, the VIN is the token containing letters. That is what lets one
parser read every naming generation this tree has had —

```
{lot}-{vin}                      gen 1
{lot}-{vin}-{dist}               gen 2
{lot}-{vin}-{year}-{dist}        gen 3
{year}-{dist}-{lot}-{vin}        gen 4 (current)
```

— which is what made migrating 314 existing folders possible rather than guessed
at. It also keeps masked-VIN detection honest: hand `is_masked_vin()` a whole
tail and `…xxxxxx-2019-2500mi` reads as NOT masked, silently disabling the
VIN-resolution rename.

A folder also **moves between damage groups and model folders** when those
change, rather than forking — `existing_dirs()` searches every group and model,
plus the pre-group and pre-model layouts, so older trees migrate on first
re-pull instead of being stranded.
""")

# 3) manifest path

p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8")
print(f"folder section rewritten (+{len(s)-before} chars)")
PY

Confirmed as a wall rather than sparse data: the same query restricted to

months before the pull date. The docs say ~10 months; the demo key gave ~5.5;
Basic gives the same ~6. **The paid plan buys rate and volume, not depth.**

Two consequences. A relist older than the window is invisible to
`/vehicles/{VIN}/history` as well. And the json-raw archives really are the only
long-term record — anything older than six months exists nowhere else, which is
what makes the archive-everything rule load-bearing rather than cautious.

with no model filter returned **HTTP 502 `Vehicle API request failed`**. Keep
requested ranges inside the retention window.""")

## .gitignore

Added `tmp/`, plus tree-preserving rules for both data directories:

```gitignore
analytics/data/**
!analytics/data/**/
!analytics/data/**/.gitkeep

images/**
!images/**/
!images/**/.gitkeep
```

The `!.../` line is the one that matters — without re-including directories, git stops descending and never sees the `.gitkeep` files below them. I created 22 of them covering the canonical `{sold,open}/{json-raw,json-adapted,csv-raw,csv-cut,history}/{iaai,copart}` tree so a fresh clone can run the pipeline without reverse-engineering the layout.

Also added `.claude/settings.local.json` (machine-local permissions) while keeping `settings.json`.

Verified by spot-check — every one reports IGNORED: a real `json-raw` archive, a `csv-cut`, `manifest_open.csv`, a `.jpg`, `tmp-terminal.txt`, `.env`.

## Why it hung

The `>` prompt is bash saying "I'm still waiting for you to close something." The command I gave used a heredoc inside command substitution:

```bash
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
...
EOF
)"
```

Pasted into a terminal, that's fragile — if the `EOF` line picks up trailing whitespace, or the paste mangles a newline, bash never sees the terminator and waits forever. My fault for handing you a multi-line construct to paste rather than something paste-safe.

Replacing both the key and the merge in one pass:

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Bash**: Implement 11-char key and field-level merge</summary>

```bash
cd /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker
python - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = s[s.index("    # De-dupe across overlapping archives: richest first, then newest."):
        s.index("    kept, dropped = [], []")]
new = '''    # De-dupe across overlapping archives, then MERGE per field.
    #
    # The key uses the first 11 VIN characters, not the whole VIN. IAAI masks
    # the last 6, so the SAME lot is `WAUENCF5XJA******` from a web pull and
    # `WAUENCF5XJA060484` once Apibara resolves it — a full-VIN key files those
    # as two different cars and emits the lot twice. The unmasked 11 are the
    # portion both sources always agree on.
    def dedupe_key(v):
        vin = str(v.get("vin") or "").strip().upper()
        return (v.get("platform"), str(v.get("lot_number") or ""), vin[:11])

    groups = {}
    for v in records:
        groups.setdefault(dedupe_key(v), []).append(v)
    dupes = sum(len(g) - 1 for g in groups.values())

    by_key = {k: merge_observations(g) for k, g in groups.items()}

'''
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

MERGE = '''
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# merging repeat observations of one lot
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fields that genuinely change between pulls. Everything else about a lot —
# damage, odometer, engine, branch, coordinates, ACV, photos — is fixed for the
# life of the listing, so it can safely come from whichever snapshot has it.
VOLATILE_BLOCKS = ("auction", "pricing")
VOLATILE_KEYS = ("_web_state", "_mode")


def _has_detail(v):
    return v.get("_detail_level") != "search"


def _better_vin(a, b):
    """Prefer a resolved VIN over a masked one, regardless of which is newer."""
    av, bv = str(a or ""), str(b or "")
    if "*" in av and "*" not in bv and bv:
        return bv
    return av or bv


def merge_observations(obs):
    """Several sightings of one lot -> one row.

    Neither newest-wins nor richest-wins is right on its own:

      newest-wins   a 1-request search pull carries no ACV, no repair estimate
                    and no damage codes, so being newest it blanks them.
      richest-wins  a full pull from yesterday then shadows today's listing
                    state, auction date and Buy Now — the row looks current and
                    is not.

    So: take the RICHEST record as the base for static detail, then overlay the
    volatile auction/pricing blocks from the NEWEST record. Identity fields that
    only ever improve (VIN, seller name) take the better value from either.
    """
    if len(obs) == 1:
        return obs[0]

    by_time = sorted(obs, key=lambda v: v.get("_pulled_at") or "")
    newest = by_time[-1]
    # richest = has detail; ties broken by recency
    richest = sorted(obs, key=lambda v: (_has_detail(v), v.get("_pulled_at") or ""))[-1]
    if richest is newest:
        return newest

    merged = dict(richest)
    for blk in VOLATILE_BLOCKS:
        if isinstance(newest.get(blk), dict):
            merged[blk] = newest[blk]
    for k in VOLATILE_KEYS:
        if k in newest:
            merged[k] = newest[k]
    merged["ad"] = newest.get("ad", merged.get("ad"))

    # identity only improves, never degrades
    merged["vin"] = _better_vin(richest.get("vin"), newest.get("vin"))
    rs, ns = richest.get("seller") or {}, newest.get("seller") or {}
    if not str(rs.get("name") or "").strip() and str(ns.get("name") or "").strip():
        merged["seller"] = ns

    # Provenance describes CURRENCY: the row is as of the newest sighting, even
    # though its static detail may have been captured earlier in the cohort.
    merged["_pulled_at"] = newest.get("_pulled_at")
    merged["_source_file"] = newest.get("_source_file")
    merged["_detail_level"] = richest.get("_detail_level")
    merged["_merged_from"] = sorted({v.get("_source_file") for v in obs if v.get("_source_file")})
    return merged


'''
s = s.replace("# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef parse_tier(s):", MERGE + "# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef parse_tier(s):",1)
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8"); print("patched")
PY
python -m py_compile analytics/scripts/data_pull_01.py && echo "compile OK"
```

<details>
<summary>**Tool — Bash**: Add the archive_sold pass</summary>

```bash
cd /home/striker/projects/car-bid-tracker
python - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("analytics/scripts/pull_images_01.py"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

ARCHIVE = '''
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# archiving lots that have left the listings
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def archive_sold(platform="iaai", apply=True):
    """Move folders for departed lots from images/open/ to images/sold/.

    Photos of a lot that sold are the most valuable thing in the tree — they are
    the comp. Deleting them would be worse than useless, and leaving them in
    `open/` makes the open tree a lie about what is actually biddable. So they
    are archived, keeping the identical {model}/{group}/{platform}/{name} shape
    so an open folder and its sold counterpart are directly comparable.

    "Departed" is `exit_state == 'gone'` from lot_history_01, which is itself
    scope-aware — a lot is only called gone when a later, non-truncated snapshot
    that actually covered its market and keyword failed to contain it. That
    matters here because the move is destructive-ish: a false positive would
    bury a live lot in the sold archive.

    A relist reverses it. `existing_dirs()` searches both buckets, so a lot that
    comes back is found under sold/ and moved to open/ by the next image run
    rather than being downloaded a second time.
    """
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    import lot_history_01 as HIST
    import apibara_json2csv_iaai_01 as F

    paths = HIST.all_archives()
    if not paths:
        return [], []
    history = HIST.build_history(F.load_records(paths), paths)

    moved, skipped = [], []
    root = IMAGES_ROOT / "open"
    if not root.is_dir():
        return moved, skipped
    for folder in sorted(root.glob(f"*/*/{platform}/*")):
        if not folder.is_dir():
            continue
        lot = parse_folder_name(folder.name)[0]
        h = history.get(lot)
        if not h or h.get("exit_state") != "gone":
            continue
        dest = (IMAGES_ROOT / "sold" / folder.parents[1].name
                / folder.parent.name.replace(platform, platform)
                / platform / folder.name)
        dest = IMAGES_ROOT / "sold" / folder.parents[2].name / folder.parents[1].name / platform / folder.name
        if dest.exists():
            skipped.append((folder, dest, "destination exists"))
            continue
        if apply:
            dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            folder.rename(dest)
        moved.append((folder, dest, h.get("exit_reason") or "unknown",
                      h.get("exit_price_usd") or ""))
    return moved, skipped


'''
s=s.replace("# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# filtering", ARCHIVE + "# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# filtering",1)

s=s.replace('''    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",''',
'''    ap.add_argument("--archive-sold", action="store_true",
                    help="before downloading, move folders for lots that have "
                         "left the listings from images/open/ to images/sold/, "
                         "keeping the same {model}/{group}/{platform} shape")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",''',1)
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8"); print("archive_sold added")

````bash

python - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

s=s.replace("""Which forces one change in stage 3: **de-dupe is richest-first, then newest.**
Straight newest-wins would let a 1-request search pull shadow a full record and
blank ACV, repair estimate and damage codes. Static fields do not change between
pulls anyway, and the fields that do move are captured in the history columns.
Verified: lot 45856028 survives from the full 08-14 08:56 archive with its
odometer and damage intact, even though the newest snapshot holds only a thin
record for it.""",
"""### De-dupe key: the first 11 VIN characters, not the whole VIN

IAAI masks the last 6, so the SAME lot is `WAUENCF5XJA******` from a web pull and
`WAUENCF5XJA060484` once Apibara resolves it. Keying on the full VIN files those
as two different cars:

```
lot 45738201   enriched WAUENCF54JA009708 / web-only WAUENCF54JA******
   full-VIN key -> 2 distinct  => lot emitted TWICE
   11-char key  -> 1 distinct  => lot emitted ONCE
```

The unmasked 11 are the portion both sources always agree on. Current cuts happen
to contain no duplicates only because every archive on disk has been enriched;
the next web-only pull alongside an older enriched archive would have produced
them.

### Merging repeat sightings: static from the richest, volatile from the newest

Neither newest-wins nor richest-wins is right on its own:

| strategy | failure |
|---|---|
| newest-wins | a 1-request search pull carries no ACV, repair estimate or damage codes, so being newest it **blanks them** |
| richest-wins | a full pull from yesterday then shadows today's `listing_state`, `auction_at` and `buy_now_usd` — the row **looks current and is not** |

So `merge_observations()` takes the richest record as the base and overlays the
`auction` and `pricing` blocks plus `_web_state` from the newest. Identity fields
that only ever improve — VIN, seller name — take the better value from either,
so a masked re-pull can never overwrite a resolved VIN.

```
richest (08-16, full)   ACV 17,975   state Prebid          auction 08-18   buy-now -
newest  (08-17, search) ACV -        state Prebid/BuyNow   auction 08-21   buy-now 7,600
merged                  ACV 17,975   state Prebid/BuyNow   auction 08-21   buy-now 7,600
```

`pulled_at` and `source_file` describe **currency** — they name the newest
sighting, because that is what the row's live fields are as of. The static detail
may have been captured earlier in the same cohort; `_merged_from` records every
file involved, and `--history` gives the full span via `first_seen_at` /
`last_seen_at`.""")
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8"); print("dedupe/merge documented")
PY
python - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("analytics/schema/iaai_csv_schema.md"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
s=s.replace("""### Note on which lots have photos at all""",
"""### Departed lots are archived, not pruned

```bash
python analytics/scripts/pull_images_01.py CUT.csv --archive-sold
```

Photos of a lot that sold are the most valuable thing in the tree — they are the
comp. Deleting them would be worse than useless, and leaving them under `open/`
makes that tree a lie about what is biddable. So they move to `images/sold/`
keeping the identical shape, which makes an open folder and its sold counterpart
directly comparable:

```
images/open/Audi A4/FRONT/iaai/2018-2000mi-45316975-WAUKMAF44JN015356
images/sold/Audi A4/FRONT/iaai/2018-2000mi-45316975-WAUKMAF44JN015356
```

"Departed" is `exit_state == 'gone'` from `lot_history_01.py`, which is
scope-aware: a lot is only called gone when a later, non-truncated snapshot that
actually covered its market **and** its search keyword failed to contain it. That
matters here because the move is close to destructive — a false positive buries a
live lot in the sold archive.

**A relist reverses it.** `existing_dirs()` searches both buckets, so a lot that
comes back is found under `sold/` and moved to `open/` by the next image run
rather than being downloaded again. Verified round-trip in both directions with
the photos preserved.

### Note on which lots have photos at all""")
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8"); print("sold archive documented")

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("analytics/scripts/apibara_json2csv_iaai_01.py"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

BANDS = '''
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derived: IAA vehicle score band
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IAA's own automated computer-vision assessment of visible damage severity,
# from the check-in photos. Two things about it are easy to get backwards:
# HIGHER IS BETTER (50 is the least damaged, 0 the worst), and it is NOT a
# percentage of anything. Band names and boundaries are IAA's, from their score
# flyer — kept verbatim rather than paraphrased so a row can be checked against
# the official document.
_SCORE_BANDS = (
    (0, 9, "non-repairable"),
    (10, 19, "severe damage"),
    (20, 29, "major damage"),
    (30, 39, "moderate damage"),
    (40, 49, "minor damage"),
    (50, 50, "little damage"),
)


def vehicle_score(v):
    """IAA's 0-50 score as a number, or None when not assessed."""
    raw = clean(attrs(v).get("VehicleGrade"))
    if raw is None:
        return None
    try:
        return int(float(str(raw).strip()))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def vehicle_score_band(v):
    """-> IAA's band name, or '' when the lot carries no score.

    Blank stays blank rather than collapsing into the worst band: "not assessed"
    and "assessed as non-repairable" are opposite facts, and 209 of 2,679 rows
    have no score at all.
    """
    n = vehicle_score(v)
    if n is None:
        return ""
    for lo, hi, name in _SCORE_BANDS:
        if lo <= n <= hi:
            return name
    return ""


'''
s=s.replace("# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# derived: damage grouping", BANDS + "# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# derived: damage grouping",1)

s=s.replace('''    ("vehicle_grade",       lambda v: clean(attrs(v).get("VehicleGrade")),    "raw"),''',
'''    # IAA's own photo-based damage score. Renamed from `vehicle_grade` because
    # "grade" reads like a letter grade or a percentage and this is neither.
    ("iaa_vehicle_score",   vehicle_score,                                    "raw"),
    ("iaa_vehicle_score_band", vehicle_score_band,                            "calc"),''',1)
s=s.replace('''    "vehicle_grade": "details.attributes.VehicleGrade",''',
'''    "iaa_vehicle_score": "details.attributes.VehicleGrade — IAA photo score, 0-50, HIGHER IS BETTER",
    "iaa_vehicle_score_band": "IAA band name for the score (non-repairable .. little damage)",''',1)

def score_tag(score):
    """38 -> 'score38'. Prefixed on purpose.

    A bare number would be ambiguous against the year and lot segments, which
    are also digits — and this parser identifies segments by shape, not
    position. The prefix also makes the folder self-describing: `score38` needs
    no legend, `38` does.
    """
    try:

    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return ""
    return f"score{n}" if 0 <= n <= 50 else ""''',1)

    used = {year, dist, bn}

    lot = next((p for p in rest if p.isdigit()), "")

'''    parts = [p for p in str(name).split("-") if p]

    bn = next((p for p in parts if p.startswith("$")), "")

All five done.

## 1 — Dedupe key: 11-char VIN prefix

The failure mode was latent, so I reproduced it against a real record before and after:

```
lot 45738201   enriched WAUENCF54JA009708 / web-only WAUENCF54JA******
   full-VIN key -> 2 distinct  => lot emitted TWICE
   11-char key  -> 1 distinct  => lot emitted ONCE
```

Zero lots currently carry both forms — only because every archive on disk has been enriched. Your next web-only pull alongside an older enriched archive would have produced duplicates.

## 2 — Field-level merge

You were right that richest-wins leaves volatile fields stale. `merge_observations()` now takes the richest record as the base and overlays `auction` + `pricing` + `_web_state` from the newest:

```
richest (08-16, full)   ACV 17,975   state Prebid          auction 08-18   buy-now -
newest  (08-17, search) ACV -        state Prebid/BuyNow   auction 08-21   buy-now 7,600
merged                  ACV 17,975   state Prebid/BuyNow   auction 08-21   buy-now 7,600
```

VIN and seller name take the *better* value rather than the newer one, so a masked re-pull can't overwrite a resolved VIN. `pulled_at`/`source_file` now mean **currency** (newest sighting); `_merged_from` records every file involved.

Real cut: 84 rows, 84 distinct lots, no duplicates, all 84 with `listing_state` and `auction_at`.

## 3 — `images/sold/`

```bash
python analytics/scripts/pull_images_01.py CUT.csv --archive-sold
```

Moves departed lots to the identical shape you specified:

```
images/open/Audi A4/FRONT/iaai/2018-2000mi-45316975-WAUKMAF44JN015356
images/sold/Audi A4/FRONT/iaai/2018-2000mi-45316975-WAUKMAF44JN015356
```

It reports **0 to move right now** — I verified that's correct, not a no-op: all 314 folder lots are `still_listed`. The 1,345 `gone` lots are Apibara `ended` records that never had folders. Sandbox-tested both directions, including the **relist round-trip** — a sold lot that comes back is found under `sold/` and moved to `open/` rather than re-downloaded.

Departure uses `exit_state == 'gone'`, which is scope-aware — that matters here because a false positive would bury a live lot.

## 4 — `iaa_vehicle_score` + band

Renamed from `vehicle_grade`, raw 0–50 retained, band names verbatim from IAA's flyer:

```
278  little damage       (50)
534  minor damage        (40-49)
661  moderate damage     (30-39)
559  major damage        (20-29)
441  severe damage       (10-19)
 97  non-repairable      (0-9)
211  not assessed        (blank)
```

Observed values are integers across the full 0–50 range, so the data matches the published scale exactly.

**Blank stays blank rather than becoming `non-repairable`** — "not assessed" and "assessed as a write-off" are opposite facts, and folding them would have invented 211 write-offs.

## 5 — Score in folder names, all 314 migrated

```

2018-2250mi-45490663-WAUENCF55JA084384-score32
2018-1000mi-45719990-WAUB4AF44JAxxxxxx-score0
```

One choice worth flagging: I prefixed it (`score38`, not `38`). A bare number would be ambiguous against the year and lot segments, since parsing is shape-based. It also required matching the score **before** the VIN — `score38` contains letters and would otherwise be read as the VIN, which would have broken masked-VIN detection and forked folders on the next enrichment.

import pathlib
